children.text: om ity etad akṣaram udgītham upāsīta
children.translated_text: One should meditate on this syllable <s>oṃ</s> as the <s>udgītha</s> (loud chant).
For one sings the <s>udgītha</s> with "<s>oṃ</s>."
Its explanation follows.
Of these beings, earth is the essence.
Of earth, the waters are the essence.
Of the waters, plants are the essence.
Of plants, the person is the essence.
Of the person, speech is the essence.
Of speech, the Ṛg is the essence.
Of the Ṛg, the Sāman is the essence.
Of the Sāman, the <s>udgītha</s> is the essence.

children.text: sa eṣa rasānāṃ rasatamaḥ paramaḥ parārdhyo 'ṣṭamo yadudgīthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That <s>udgītha</s>, then, is the most essential of essences, supreme, deserving the highest place, the eighth.

children.text: katamā katamark katamat katamat sāma katamaḥ katama udgītha iti vimṛṣṭaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: The question is considered: Which is the Ṛg? Which is the Sāman? Which is the <s>udgītha</s>?
Speech itself is the Ṛg.
Breath is the Sāman.
This syllable <s>oṃ</s> is the <s>udgītha</s>.

children.text: tad vā etan mithunaṃ yad vāk ca prāṇaś cark ca sāma ca ||
children.translated_text: This pair, then, is speech and breath, the Ṛg and the Sāman.

children.text: tad etan mithunam om ity etasminn akṣare saṃsṛjyate
children.translated_text: This pair is joined together in this syllable <s>oṃ</s>.

children.text: yadā vai mithunau samāgacchata āpayato vai tāv anyonyasya kāmam ||
children.translated_text: When a pair come together, they fulfill each other's desire.

children.text: āpayitā ha vai kāmānāṃ bhavati ya etad evaṃ vidvān akṣaram udgītham upāste ||
children.translated_text: He who, knowing thus, meditates on this syllable as the <s>udgītha</s> becomes a fulfiller of desires.
This, then, is the syllable of assent.

children.text: yaddhi kiṃcānujānāty om ity eva tad āha
children.translated_text: For whenever one assents to anything, one says just "<s>oṃ</s>."
Assent itself is prosperity.

children.text: samardhayitā ha vai kāmānāṃ bhavati ya etad evaṃ vidvān akṣaram udgītham upāste ||
children.translated_text: He who, knowing thus, meditates on this syllable as the <s>udgītha</s> becomes one who brings desires to fulfillment.
By means of it this threefold knowledge proceeds.
With "<s>oṃ</s>" he makes the invitation to recite.
With "<s>oṃ</s>" he recites the praise.
With "<s>oṃ</s>" he sings the <s>udgītha</s>.
This is for the honoring of this very syllable, through its greatness and its essence.
By it both perform the rite.

children.text: yaś caitad evaṃ veda yaś ca na veda
children.translated_text: Both the one who knows this in this way and the one who does not know it.
But knowledge and ignorance are different.

children.text: yad eva vidyayā karoti śraddhayopaniṣadā tad eva vīryavattaraṃ bhavatīti khalv etasyaivākṣarasyopavyākhyānaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Whatever one does with knowledge, with faith, and with the secret teaching, that very act becomes more powerful; thus, indeed, this is the explanation of this syllable.

children.text: devāsurā ha vai yatra saṃyetire ubhaye prājāpatyās taddha devā udgītham ājahrur anenainān abhibhaviṣyāma iti ||
children.translated_text: Once, when the devas and the asuras, both descendants of <s>Prajāpati</s>, contended with each other, the devas took up the <s>udgītha</s>, thinking, "By this we shall overcome them."

children.text: te ha nāsikyaṃ prāṇam udgītham upāsāṃcakrire
children.translated_text: They meditated on the breath in the nose as the <s>udgītha</s>.
The asuras pierced it with evil.

children.text: tasmāt tenobhayaṃ jighrati surabhi ca durgandhi ca
children.translated_text: Therefore through it one smells both kinds of things, both fragrant and foul-smelling.
For it is pierced by evil.
Then they meditated on speech as the <s>udgītha</s>.
The asuras pierced it with evil.

children.text: tasmāt tayobhayaṃ vadati satyaṃ cānṛtaṃ ca
children.translated_text: Therefore through it one speaks both kinds of things, truth and falsehood.
For it is pierced by evil.
Then they meditated on the eye as the <s>udgītha</s>.
The asuras pierced it with evil.

children.text: tasmāt tenobhayaṃ paśyati darśanīyaṃ cādarśanīyaṃ ca
children.translated_text: Therefore through it one sees both kinds of things, both what is worth seeing and what is not worth seeing.
For it is pierced by evil.
Then they meditated on the ear as the <s>udgītha</s>.
The asuras pierced it with evil.

children.text: tasmāt tenobhayaṃ śṛṇoti śravaṇīyaṃ cāśravaṇīyaṃ ca
children.translated_text: Therefore through it one hears both kinds of things, both what is worth hearing and what is not worth hearing.
For it is pierced by evil.
Then they meditated on the mind as the <s>udgītha</s>.
The asuras pierced it with evil.

children.text: tasmāt tenobhayaṃ saṃkalpayate saṃkalpanīyaṃ cāsaṃkalpanīyaṃ ca
children.translated_text: Therefore with it one forms both kinds of intentions, both what is fit to be intended and what is not fit to be intended.
For it is pierced by evil.

children.text: atha ha ya evāyaṃ mukhyaḥ prāṇas tam udgītham upāsāṃcakrire
children.translated_text: Then they meditated on this chief breath in the mouth as the <s>udgītha</s>.

children.text: taṃ hāsurā ṛtvā vidadhvaṃsur yathāśmānam ākhaṇam ṛtvā vidhvaṃsetaivam ||
children.translated_text: When the asuras struck against it, they were shattered, just as one would be shattered by striking against a solid stone.

children.text: evaṃ yathāśmānam ākhaṇam ṛtvā vidhvaṃsata evaṃ haiva sa vidhvaṃsate ya evaṃvidi pāpaṃ kāmayate yaś cainam abhidāsati
children.translated_text: Just as one is shattered by striking against a solid stone, so indeed he is shattered who wishes evil against one who knows this in this way, or who attacks him.
This, then, is a solid stone.
By it one discerns neither fragrant nor foul-smelling things.
For it is free from evil.

children.text: tena yad aśnāti yat pibati tenetarān prāṇān avati
children.translated_text: By what one eats and what one drinks with it, one protects the other breaths.
Not knowing this one departs at the end.
At the end, he merely opens his mouth.
<s>Aṅgirā</s> meditated on that as the <s>udgītha</s>.

children.text: etam u evāṅgirasaṃ manyante 'ṅgānāṃ yad rasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: They consider this very one to be <s>Aṅgirasa</s>, because it is the essence of the limbs.

children.text: tena taṃ ha bṛhaspatir udgītham upāsāṃcakre
children.translated_text: By means of it <s>Bṛhaspati</s> meditated on that as the <s>udgītha</s>.
They consider this very one to be <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.
For speech is the bṛhatī, and he is its lord.
By means of it <s>Āyāsya</s> meditated on that as the <s>udgītha</s>.
They consider this very one to be <s>Āyāsya</s>.
Because it goes forth from the mouth.

children.text: tena taṃ ha bako dālbhyo vidāṃcakāra
children.translated_text: By means of it <s>Baka Dālbhya</s> came to know that.
He became the <s>udgātṛ</s> of the people of <s>Naimiṣa</s>.
He used to sing desires into fulfillment for them.

children.text: āgātā ha vai kāmānāṃ bhavati ya etad evaṃ vidvān akṣaram udgītham upāste
children.translated_text: He who, knowing thus, meditates on this syllable as the <s>udgītha</s> becomes one who sings desires into fulfillment.
Thus concerning the self.
Now concerning the deities.

children.text: ya evāsau tapati tam udgītham upāsīta
children.translated_text: One should meditate on that which shines there as the <s>udgītha</s>.
For as it rises, it sings the <s>udgītha</s> for creatures.
As it rises, it drives away darkness and fear.

children.text: apahantā ha vai bhayasya tamaso bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He who knows thus becomes a driver-away of fear and darkness.
This one here and that one there are just the same.
This one is warm; that one is warm.

children.text: svara itīmam ācakṣate svara iti pratyāsvara ity amum
children.translated_text: They call this one svara, and that one svara and pratyāsvara.

children.text: tasmād vā etam imam amuṃ ca udgītham upāsīta ||
children.translated_text: Therefore one should meditate on both this one and that one as the <s>udgītha</s>.
Now, further, one should meditate on the vyāna (diffusive breath) itself as the <s>udgītha</s>.
What breathes forward is prāṇa.
What breathes downward is apāna.

children.text: atha yaḥ prāṇāpānayoḥ saṃdhiḥ sa vyānaḥ
children.translated_text: But the junction of prāṇa and apāna is vyāna.
What is vyāna is speech.
Therefore one utters speech while neither breathing forward nor breathing downward.
What is speech is the Ṛg.
Therefore one recites the Ṛg while neither breathing forward nor breathing downward.
What is the Ṛg is the Sāman.
Therefore one sings the Sāman while neither breathing forward nor breathing downward.
What is the Sāman is the <s>udgītha</s>.
Therefore one sings the <s>udgītha</s> without breathing out and without breathing in.

children.text: ato yāny anyāni vīryavanti karmāṇi yathāgner manthanam ājeḥ saraṇaṃ dṛḍhasya dhanuṣa āyamanam aprāṇann anapānaṃs tāni karoti
children.translated_text: Hence whatever other vigorous actions there are, such as kindling fire by friction, running in a race, or drawing a strong bow, one performs them without breathing out and without breathing in.
For this reason one should meditate on <s>vyāna</s> as the <s>udgītha</s>.
Now then one should meditate on the syllables of the <s>udgītha</s>, namely "ud-gī-tha."
<s>Prāṇa</s> is indeed "ut."
For by <s>prāṇa</s> one rises up.
Speech is "gīḥ."
For people call speech "giraḥ."
Food is "tham."
For in food all this is established.
Heaven is indeed "ut."
The midspace is "gīḥ."
The earth is "tham."
The sun is indeed "ut."
Wind is "gīḥ."
Fire is "tham."
The <s>Sāmaveda</s> is indeed "ut."
The <s>Yajurveda</s> is "gīḥ."
The <s>Ṛgveda</s> is "tham."

children.text: dugdhe 'smai vāg dohaṃ yo vāco dohaḥ
children.translated_text: Speech milks out for him the milk-yield, whatever milk-yield belongs to speech.
He becomes possessed of food and an eater of food.

children.text: ya etāny evaṃ vidvān udgīthākṣarāṇy upāsta udgītha iti ||
children.translated_text: Such is the one who, knowing thus, meditates on these very syllables of the <s>udgītha</s>, namely "ud-gī-tha."
Now then, there is the prosperity of a wish.
One should meditate on the approaches.

children.text: yena sāmnā stoṣyan syāt tat sāmopadhāvet ||
children.translated_text: With whatever <s>sāman</s> he is going to praise, he should approach that <s>sāman</s>.

children.text: yasyām ṛci tām ṛcaṃ yad ārṣeyaṃ tam ṛṣiṃ yāṃ devatām abhiṣṭoṣyan syāt tāṃ devatām upadhāvet ||
children.translated_text: On whatever <s>ṛc</s> he is going to praise, he should approach that <s>ṛc</s>, the seer to whom it belongs, and the deity whom he is going to praise.

children.text: yena chandasā stoṣyan syāt tac chanda upadhāvet
children.translated_text: With whatever meter he is going to praise, he should approach that meter.

children.text: yena stomena stoṣyamāṇaḥ syāt taṃ stomam upadhāvet ||
children.translated_text: With whatever <s>stoma</s> he is going to praise, he should approach that <s>stoma</s>.

children.text: yāṃ diśam abhiṣṭoṣyan syāt tāṃ diśam upadhāvet ||
children.translated_text: In whatever direction he is going to praise, he should approach that direction.

children.text: ātmānam antata upasṛtya stuvīta kāmaṃ dhyāyann apramattaḥ
children.translated_text: Having at last approached himself, he should praise while meditating on his desire, without negligence.

children.text: abhyāśo ha yad asmai sa kāmaḥ smṛdhyeta yatkāmaḥ stuvīteti yatkāmaḥ stuvīteti ||
children.translated_text: Indeed, the desire with which he praises is likely to prosper for him, the desire with which he praises, the desire with which he praises.

children.text: om ity etad akṣaram udgītham upāsīta
children.translated_text: One should meditate on this syllable, <s>om</s>, as the <s>udgītha</s>.
For with <s>om</s> one sings the <s>udgītha</s>.
This is its further explanation.

children.text: devā vai mṛtyor bibhyatas trayīṃ vidyāṃ prāviśan
children.translated_text: The gods, fearing death, entered the threefold knowledge.
They covered themselves with the meters.
Because they covered themselves with these, that is the meterhood of the meters.

children.text: tān u tatra mṛtyur yathā matsyam udake paripaśyed evaṃ paryapaśyad ṛci sāmni yajuṣi
children.translated_text: Death saw them there, in the <s>ṛc</s>, in the <s>sāman</s>, and in the <s>yajus</s>, just as one might see a fish in water.

children.text: te nu vittvordhvā ṛcaḥ sāmno yajuṣaḥ svaram eva prāviśan ||
children.translated_text: Then, knowing this, they rose up from the <s>ṛc</s>, the <s>sāman</s>, and the <s>yajus</s>, and entered the sound itself.

children.text: yadā vā ṛcam āpnoty om ity evātisvarati evaṃ sāmaivaṃ yajuḥ
children.translated_text: When one reaches a <s>ṛc</s>, one utters only <s>om</s> with raised voice; so too with a <s>sāman</s>, so too with a <s>yajus</s>.

children.text: eṣa u svaro yad etad akṣaram etad amṛtam abhayam
children.translated_text: This sound is this syllable; this is immortal and fearless.
Having entered it, the gods became immortal.

children.text: sa ya etad evaṃ vidvān akṣaraṃ praṇautyetad evākṣaraṃ svaram amṛtam abhayaṃ praviśati
children.translated_text: So one who, knowing thus, praises this syllable enters this very syllable, the sound, the immortal and fearless.

children.text: tat praviśya yad amṛtā devās tad amṛto bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Having entered it, he becomes immortal, just as the gods are immortal.

children.text: atha khalu ya udgīthaḥ sa praṇavo yaḥ praṇavaḥ sa udgītha iti
children.translated_text: Now then, what is the <s>udgītha</s> is the <s>praṇava</s>, and what is the <s>praṇava</s> is the <s>udgītha</s>.

children.text: asau vā āditya udgītha eṣa praṇavaḥ
children.translated_text: That sun is indeed the <s>udgītha</s>; this is the <s>praṇava</s>.

children.text: om iti hy eṣa svarann eti ||
children.translated_text: For sounding <s>om</s>, it moves on.

children.text: etam u evāham abhyagāsiṣaṃ tasmān mama tvam eko 'sīti ha kauṣītakiḥ putram uvāca
children.translated_text: "This very one I sang toward; therefore you are my only one," so <s>Kauṣītaki</s> said to his son.
"You should turn yourself toward the rays.
Many indeed will be yours."
So much with reference to the deities.
Now with reference to the self.

children.text: ya evāyaṃ mukhyaḥ prāṇas tam udgītham upāsīta
children.translated_text: One should meditate on this chief breath here as the <s>udgītha</s>.

children.text: om iti hy eṣa svarann eti ||
children.translated_text: For sounding <s>om</s>, it moves on.

children.text: etam u evāham abhyagāsiṣaṃ tasmān mama tvam eko 'sīti ha kauṣītakiḥ putram uvāca
children.translated_text: "This very one I sang toward; therefore you are my only one," so <s>Kauṣītaki</s> said to his son.

children.text: prāṇāṃs tvaṃ bhūmānam abhigāyatād bahavo vai me bhaviṣyantīti ||
children.translated_text: "You should sing toward the abundance of breaths; many indeed will be mine."

children.text: atha khalu ya udgīthaḥ sa praṇavo yaḥ praṇavaḥ sa udgītha iti
children.translated_text: Now then, what is the <s>udgītha</s> is the <s>praṇava</s>, and what is the <s>praṇava</s> is the <s>udgītha</s>.
Even from the seat of the <s>hotṛ</s>, one sets right a badly sung <s>udgītha</s>, so they say, so they say.
This earth itself is the <s>ṛc</s>.
Fire is the <s>sāman</s>.

children.text: tad etad etasyām ṛcy adhyūḍhaṃ sāma
children.translated_text: This <s>sāman</s> is mounted upon that <s>ṛc</s>.
Therefore the <s>sāman</s> is sung mounted upon a <s>ṛc</s>.
This earth itself is "sā."
Fire is "amaḥ."
That is <s>sāman</s>.
The midspace itself is the <s>ṛc</s>.
Wind is the <s>sāman</s>.

children.text: tad etad etasyām ṛcy adhyūḍhaṃ sāma
children.translated_text: This <s>sāman</s> is mounted upon that <s>ṛc</s>.
Therefore the <s>sāman</s> is sung mounted upon a <s>ṛc</s>.
The midspace itself is "sā."
Wind is "amaḥ."
That is <s>sāman</s>.
Heaven itself is the <s>ṛc</s>.
The sun is the <s>sāman</s>.
This <s>sāman</s> is mounted upon that <s>ṛc</s>.
Therefore the <s>sāman</s> is sung mounted upon a <s>ṛc</s>.
Heaven itself is "sā."
The sun is "amaḥ."
That is <s>sāman</s>.
The stars themselves are the <s>ṛc</s>.
The moon is the <s>sāman</s>.
This <s>sāman</s> is mounted upon that <s>ṛc</s>.
Therefore the <s>sāman</s> is sung mounted upon a <s>ṛc</s>.
The stars themselves are "sā."
The moon is "amaḥ."
That is <s>sāman</s>.

children.text: atha yad etad ādityasya śuklaṃ bhāḥ saivark
children.translated_text: Now the white brightness of the sun is itself the <s>ṛc</s>.

children.text: atha yan nīlaṃ paraḥkṛṣṇaṃ tat sāma
children.translated_text: And what is blue, very dark, is the <s>sāman</s>.

children.text: tad etad etasyām ṛcy adhyūḍhaṃ sāma
children.translated_text: This <s>sāman</s> is mounted upon that <s>ṛc</s>.
Therefore the <s>sāman</s> is sung mounted upon a <s>ṛc</s>.

children.text: atha yad evaitad ādityasya śuklaṃ bhāḥ saiva sā
children.translated_text: Now the white brightness of the sun is itself "sā."

children.text: atha yan nīlaṃ paraḥkṛṣṇaṃ tad amaḥ
children.translated_text: And what is blue, very dark, is "amaḥ."
That is <s>sāman</s>.

children.text: atha ya eṣo 'ntarāditye hiraṇmayaḥ puruṣo dṛśyate hiraṇyaśmaśrur hiraṇyakeśa ā praṇakhāt sarva eva suvarṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now that golden person who is seen within the sun has a golden beard and golden hair; he is entirely golden, down to the very nails.

children.text: tasya yathā kapyāsaṃ puṇḍarīkam evam akṣiṇī
children.translated_text: His two eyes are like a reddish lotus.
His name is "Ut."
This one has risen above all evils.

children.text: udeti ha vai sarvebhyaḥ pāpmabhyo ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: One who knows thus indeed rises above all evils.
The <s>ṛc</s> and the <s>sāman</s> are his two singers.
Therefore he is the <s>udgītha</s>.
Therefore, indeed, he is the <s>udgātṛ</s>.
For he is the singer of this.

children.text: sa eṣa ye cāmuṣmāt parāñco lokās teṣāṃ ceṣṭa devakāmānāṃ ca
children.translated_text: This one rules the worlds beyond that sun and the desires of the gods.
So much with reference to the deities.
Now with reference to the self.
Speech itself is the <s>ṛc</s>.
Breath is the <s>sāman</s>.

children.text: tad etad etasyām ṛcy adhyūḍhaṃ sāma
children.translated_text: This <s>sāman</s> is mounted upon that <s>ṛc</s>.
Therefore the <s>sāman</s> is sung as set upon a <s>ṛc</s>.
Speech indeed is the syllable <s>sā</s>.
Breath is the syllable <s>amaḥ</s>.
That is the <s>sāman</s>.
The eye indeed is the <s>ṛc</s>.
The self is the <s>sāman</s>.

children.text: tad etad etasyām ṛcy adhyūḍhaṃ sāma
children.translated_text: This <s>sāman</s> is set upon this <s>ṛc</s>.
Therefore the <s>sāman</s> is sung as set upon a <s>ṛc</s>.
The eye indeed is the syllable <s>sā</s>.
The self is the syllable <s>amaḥ</s>.
That is the <s>sāman</s>.
Hearing indeed is the <s>ṛc</s>.
The mind is the <s>sāman</s>.

children.text: tad etad etasyām ṛcy adhyūḍhaṃ sāma
children.translated_text: This <s>sāman</s> is set upon this <s>ṛc</s>.
Therefore the <s>sāman</s> is sung as set upon a <s>ṛc</s>.
Hearing indeed is the syllable <s>sā</s>.
The mind is the syllable <s>amaḥ</s>.
That is the <s>sāman</s>.

children.text: atha yad etad akṣṇaḥ śuklaṃ bhāḥ saivark
children.translated_text: Now the white brightness of the eye is itself the <s>ṛc</s>.

children.text: atha yan nīlaṃ paraḥkṛṣṇaṃ tat sāma
children.translated_text: And what is blue, intensely dark, is the <s>sāman</s>.

children.text: tad etad etasyām ṛcy adhyūḍhaṃ sāma
children.translated_text: This <s>sāman</s> is set upon this <s>ṛc</s>.
Therefore the <s>sāman</s> is sung as set upon a <s>ṛc</s>.

children.text: atha yad evaitad akṣṇaḥ śuklaṃ bhāḥ saiva sā
children.translated_text: Now that very white brightness of the eye is the syllable <s>sā</s>.

children.text: atha yan nīlaṃ paraḥkṛṣṇaṃ tad amaḥ
children.translated_text: And what is blue, intensely dark, is the syllable <s>amaḥ</s>.
That is the <s>sāman</s>.

children.text: atha ya eṣo 'ntar akṣiṇi puruṣo dṛśyate saivark
children.translated_text: Now the person who is seen within the eye is himself the <s>ṛc</s>.
That is the <s>sāman</s>.
That is the <s>uktha</s>.
That is the <s>yajus</s>.
That is <s>brahman</s>.

children.text: tasya etasya tad eva rūpaṃ yad amuṣya rūpam
children.translated_text: The form of this one is just the form of that one.

children.text: yāv amuṣya geṣṇau tau tau goṣṇau
children.translated_text: Whatever are that one's two <s>geṣṇau</s>, those are this one's two <s>goṣṇau</s>.
Whatever is that one's name, that is this one's name.

children.text: sa eṣa ye caitasmād arvāñco lokās teṣāṃ ceṣṭe manuṣyakāmānāṃ ceti
children.translated_text: This one rules over the worlds that are on this side of that, and over human desires.

children.text: tad ya ime vīṇāyāṃ gāyanty etaṃ te gāyanti
children.translated_text: Therefore those who sing to the lute sing of this one.
For that reason they are winners of wealth.

children.text: atha ya etad evaṃ vidvān sāma gāyaty ubhau sa gāyati
children.translated_text: Now the one who, knowing this, sings the <s>sāman</s>, sings both.

children.text: so 'munaiva sa eṣa ye cāmuṣmāt parāñco lokās tāṃś cāpnoti devakāmāṃś ca ||
children.translated_text: By means of that one, he obtains the worlds that are beyond that, and the divine desires.

children.text: athānenaiva ye caitasmād arvāñco lokās tāṃś cāpnoti manuṣyakāmāṃś ca
children.translated_text: And by means of this one, he obtains the worlds that are on this side of that, and human desires.
Therefore an <s>udgātṛ</s> who knows this should indeed say:
"What desire shall I sing for you?"

children.text: eṣa hy eva kāmāgānasyeṣṭe ya evaṃ vidvān sāma gāyati sāma gāyati ||
children.translated_text: For the one who, knowing this, sings the <s>sāman</s> is indeed master of desire-singing; he sings the <s>sāman</s>, he sings the <s>sāman</s>.

children.text: trayo hodgīthe kuśalā babhūvuḥ śilakaḥ śālāvatyaś caikitāyano dālbhyaḥ pravāhaṇo jaivalir iti
children.translated_text: There were three men skilled in the <s>udgītha</s>: <s>Śilaka Śālāvatya</s>, <s>Caikitāyana Dālbhya</s>, and <s>Pravāhaṇa Jaivali</s>.

children.text: te hocur udgīthe vai kuśalāḥ smo hantodgīthe kathāṃ vadāma iti ||
children.translated_text: They said, "We are skilled in the <s>udgītha</s>; come, let us hold a discussion about the <s>udgītha</s>."
Saying, "So be it," they sat down together.
Then <s>Pravāhaṇa Jaivali</s> said:
"Let the two venerable men speak first.
I shall listen to the speech of the two Brahmins as they speak."

children.text: sa ha śilakaḥ śālāvatyaś caikitāyanaṃ dālbhyam uvāca hanta tvā pṛcchānīti
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śilaka Śālāvatya</s> said to <s>Caikitāyana Dālbhya</s>, "Come, let me question you."
He said, "Ask."
"What is the support of the <s>sāman</s>?"
"Tone," he said.
"What is the support of tone?"
"Breath," he said.
"What is the support of breath?"
"Food," he said.
"What is the support of food?"
"Waters," he said.
"What is the support of the waters?"
"That world," he said.
"What is the support of that world?"

children.text: na svargaṃ lokam atinayed iti hovāca
children.translated_text: "One should not carry it beyond the heavenly world," he said.
"We establish the <s>sāman</s> upon the heavenly world.
For the <s>sāman</s> has heaven as its basis of praise."

children.text: taṃ ha śilakaḥ śālāvatyaś caikitāyanaṃ dālbhyam uvācāpratiṣṭhitaṃ vai kila te dālbhya sāma
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śilaka Śālāvatya</s> said to <s>Caikitāyana Dālbhya</s>, "Your <s>sāman</s>, <s>Dālbhya</s>, is certainly unsupported.

children.text: yas tv etarhi brūyān mūrdhā te vipatiṣyatīti mūrdhā te vipated iti ||
children.translated_text: If someone now were to say, 'Your head will fall off,' your head would fall off."
"Come, let me learn this from the venerable one," he said.
"Know it," he said.
"What is the support of that world?"
"This world," he said.
"What is the support of this world?"

children.text: na pratiṣṭhāṃ lokam atinayed iti hovāca
children.translated_text: "One should not carry it beyond the world that is the foundation," he said.
"We establish the <s>sāman</s> upon the world that is the foundation.
For the <s>sāman</s> has foundation as its basis of praise."
Then <s>Pravāhaṇa Jaivali</s> said to him:

children.text: antavad vai kila te śālāvatya sāma
children.translated_text: "Your <s>sāman</s>, <s>Śālāvatya</s>, is certainly finite.

children.text: yas tv etarhi brūyān mūrdhā te vipatiṣyatīti mūrdhā te vipated iti
children.translated_text: If someone now were to say, 'Your head will fall off,' your head would fall off."
"Come, let me learn this from the venerable one," he said.
"Know it," he said.
"What is the support of this world?"
"<s>Ākāśa</s>," he said.

children.text: sarvāṇi ha vā imāni bhūtāny ākāśād eva samutpadyante
children.translated_text: For all these beings arise from <s>ākāśa</s> alone.
They pass away back into <s>ākāśa</s>.
For <s>ākāśa</s> alone is greater than these.
<s>Ākāśa</s> is the final resort.
This is the higher-and-higher <s>udgītha</s>.
This is infinite.

children.text: parovarīyo hāsya bhavati parovarīyaso ha lokāñ jayati ya etad evaṃ vidvān parovarīyāṃsam udgītham upāste ||
children.translated_text: He becomes higher and higher, and wins worlds ever higher, who, knowing this, worships the <s>udgītha</s> as higher and higher.
Having taught this to <s>Udara Śāṇḍilya</s>, <s>Atidhanvan Śaunaka</s> said to him:

children.text: yāvat ta enaṃ prajāyām udgīthaṃ vediṣyante parovarīyo haibhyas tāvad asmiṃlloke jīvanaṃ bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: "As long as your descendants know this <s>udgītha</s>, their life in this world will be higher and higher.
And likewise in that world there will be a world," he said.

children.text: sa ya etam eva vidvān upāste parovarīya eva hāsyāmuṣmiṃlloke jīvanaṃ bhavati tathāmuṣmiṃl loke loka iti loke loka iti ||
children.translated_text: Whoever, knowing this, worships it has a higher and higher life in that world; and likewise in that world there is a world, a world indeed.

children.text: maṭacīhateṣu kuruṣv āṭikyā saha jāyayoṣastir ha cākrāyaṇa ibhyagrāme pradrāṇaka uvāsa ||
children.translated_text: Among the <s>Kurus</s>, when <s>Maṭacīhata</s> had occurred, <s>Uṣasti Cākrāyaṇa</s>, together with his wife <s>Āṭikī</s>, lived in distress in a village of a wealthy man.
He begged pulse-beans from that wealthy man, who was eating pulse-beans.
The man said to him:

children.text: neto 'nye vidyante yac ca ye ma ima upanihitā iti ||
children.translated_text: "There are no others here except these that have been set before me."
"Give me some of these," he said.
He gave them to him.
"Here, take some drink as well," he said.

children.text: ucchiṣṭaṃ vai me pītaṃ syād iti hovāca ||
children.translated_text: "What I drink would be your leavings," he said.
"But are these not also leavings?"

children.text: na vā ajīviṣyam imān akhādann iti hovāca
children.translated_text: "I would not have lived without eating these," he said.
"But drinking water is available to me as I wish."
After eating, he carried the remainder to his wife.
She had already become well supplied with food.
Receiving them, she put them away.
He, rising in the morning, said,
"If only we might obtain food; if only we might obtain even a little wealth.
That king is going to perform a sacrifice.
May he choose me for all the priestly offices."
His wife said to him,

children.text: hanta pata ima eva kulmāṣā iti
children.translated_text: "Come, husband, here are these very boiled beans."
Having eaten them, he went to that sacrifice that had been spread out.
There he sat down beside the <s>udgātṛ</s> priests as they were about to sing the opening chant.
He said to the <s>prastotar</s>:

children.text: prastotar yā devatā prastāvam anvāyattā tāṃ ced avidvān prastoṣyasi mūrdhā te vipatiṣyatīti ||
children.translated_text: "O <s>prastotar</s>, if, not knowing the deity on which the <s>prastāva</s> depends, you sing the <s>prastāva</s>, your head will fall off."
In just the same way he spoke to the <s>udgātṛ</s>.

children.text: udgātar yā devatodgītham anvāyattā tāṃ ced avidvān udgāsyasi mūrdhā te vipatiṣyatīti ||
children.translated_text: "O <s>udgātṛ</s>, if, not knowing the deity on which the <s>udgītha</s> depends, you sing the <s>udgītha</s>, your head will fall off."
In just the same way he spoke to the <s>pratihartṛ</s>.

children.text: pratihartar yā devatā pratihāram anvāyattā tāṃ ced avidvān pratihariṣyasi mūrdhā te vipatiṣyatīti
children.translated_text: "O <s>pratihartṛ</s>, if, not knowing the deity on which the <s>pratihāra</s> depends, you perform the <s>pratihāra</s>, your head will fall off."
They stopped completely and sat in silence.
Then the sacrificer said to him,
"I should like to know Your Reverence."
"I am <s>Uṣasti Cākrāyaṇa</s>," he said.
He said,

children.text: bhagavantaṃ vā aham ebhiḥ sarvair ārtvijyaiḥ paryaiṣiṣam
children.translated_text: "Indeed, Your Reverence, I searched everywhere for all these officiating priests.
Because I did not find Your Reverence, I chose others.

children.text: bhagavāṃs tv eva me sarvair ārtvijyair iti
children.translated_text: But let Your Reverence himself be my officiant for all the priestly offices."
"So be it."

children.text: atha tarhy eta eva samatisṛṣṭāḥ stuvatām
children.translated_text: "Then let these same men, authorized by me, chant.

children.text: yāvat tv ebhyo dhanaṃ dadyās tāvan mama dadyā iti
children.translated_text: But whatever wealth you would give to them, give that same amount to me."
"So be it," the sacrificer said.
Then the <s>prastotar</s> approached him.

children.text: prastotar yā devatā prastāvam anvāyattā tāṃ ced avidvān prastoṣyasi mūrdhā te vipatiṣyatīti mā bhagavān avocat
children.translated_text: "Your Reverence said to me, 'O <s>prastotar</s>, if, not knowing the deity on which the <s>prastāva</s> depends, you sing the <s>prastāva</s>, your head will fall off.'
Which deity is that?"
"<s>Prāṇa</s> (breath)," he said.

children.text: sarvāṇi ha vā imāni bhūtāni prāṇam evābhisaṃviśanti
children.translated_text: "For all these beings enter into <s>prāṇa</s> alone.
They rise up from <s>prāṇa</s>.
This is the deity on which the <s>prastāva</s> depends.

children.text: tāṃ ced avidvān prāstoṣyo mūrdhā te vipatiṣyat tathoktasya mayeti ||
children.translated_text: If, not knowing it, you had sung the <s>prastāva</s>, your head would have fallen off, just as I told you."
Then the <s>udgātṛ</s> approached him.

children.text: udgātar yā devatodgītham anvāyattā tāṃ ced avidvān udgāsyasi mūrdhā te vipatiṣyatīti mā bhagavān avocat
children.translated_text: "Your Reverence said to me, 'O <s>udgātṛ</s>, if, not knowing the deity on which the <s>udgītha</s> depends, you sing the <s>udgītha</s>, your head will fall off.'
Which deity is that?"
"The <s>Āditya</s> (Sun)," he said.

children.text: sarvāṇi ha vā imāni bhūtāny ādityam uccaiḥ santaṃ gāyanti
children.translated_text: "For all these beings sing up to the <s>Āditya</s> standing high above.
This is the deity on which the <s>udgītha</s> depends.

children.text: tāṃ ced avidvān udagāsyo mūrdhā te vyapatiṣyat tathoktasya mayeti ||
children.translated_text: If, not knowing it, you had sung the <s>udgītha</s>, your head would have fallen off, just as I told you."
Then the <s>pratihartṛ</s> approached him.

children.text: pratihartar yā devatā pratihāram anvāyattā tāṃ ced avidvān pratihariṣyasi mūrdhā te vipatiṣyatīti mā bhagavān avocat
children.translated_text: "Your Reverence said to me, 'O <s>pratihartṛ</s>, if, not knowing the deity on which the <s>pratihāra</s> depends, you perform the <s>pratihāra</s>, your head will fall off.'
Which deity is that?"
"Food," he said.

children.text: sarvāṇi ha vā imāni bhūtāny annam eva pratiharamāṇāni jīvanti
children.translated_text: "For all these beings live by taking in food alone.
This is the deity on which the <s>pratihāra</s> depends.

children.text: tāṃ ced avidvān pratyahariṣyo mūrdhā te vyapatiṣyat tathoktasya mayeti tathoktasya mayeti ||
children.translated_text: If, not knowing it, you had performed the <s>pratihāra</s>, your head would have fallen off, just as I told you, just as I told you."
Now, therefore, the dog <s>udgītha</s>.

children.text: taddha bako dālbhyo glāvo vā maitreyaḥ svādhyāyam udvavrāja ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Baka Dālbhya</s>, or <s>Glāva Maitreya</s>, went out for recitation.
A white dog appeared before him.
Other dogs came up to it and said,
"May Your Reverence sing food for us.
For we are hungry."
It said to them, "Come to me right here in the morning."

children.text: taddha bako dālbhyo glāvo vā maitreyaḥ pratipālayāṃcakāra ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Baka Dālbhya</s>, or <s>Glāva Maitreya</s>, waited.

children.text: te ha yathaivedaṃ bahiṣpavamānena stoṣyamāṇāḥ saṃrabdhāḥ sarpantīty evam āsasṛpuḥ
children.translated_text: Just as those about to sing with the <s>bahiṣpavamāna</s> move along together in a connected line, so they crept along.
Having sat down together, they made the <s>hiṃ</s> sound.
"Om, let us eat.
Om, let us drink.
Om, the god <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s>, has brought food here.
O lord of food, bring food here, bring it, bring it. Om."
This world, indeed, is the <s>hāu</s>-syllable.
<s>Vāyu</s> is the <s>hāi</s>-syllable.
The moon is the <s>atha</s>-syllable.
The self is the <s>iha</s>-syllable.
<s>Agni</s> is the <s>ī</s>-syllable.
The <s>Āditya</s> is the <s>ū</s>-syllable.
Invocation is the <s>e</s>-syllable.
The <s>Viśve Devāḥ</s> are the <s>auhoyi</s>-syllable.
<s>Prajāpati</s> is the <s>hiṅ</s>-syllable.
<s>Prāṇa</s> is the tone.
Food is <s>yā</s>; speech is <s>virāṭ</s>.
The thirteenth <s>stobha</s> (inserted chant-syllable), undefined and moving about, is the <s>huṅ</s>-syllable.

children.text: dugdhe 'smai vāg dohaṃ yo vāco dohaḥ
children.translated_text: Speech milks for him the yield, whatever is the yield of speech.
He becomes possessed of food and an eater of food,

children.text: ya etām evaṃ sāmnām upaniṣadaṃ vedopaniṣadaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: who knows in this way this secret teaching of the <s>Sāman</s>s, this <s>upaniṣad</s>.
Meditation on the whole <s>Sāman</s>, indeed, is good.

children.text: yat khalu sādhu tat sāmety ācakṣate
children.translated_text: For what is good, that they call <s>Sāman</s>.
What is not good, that they call <s>asāman</s>.
And indeed they also say:

children.text: sāmnainam upāgād iti sādhunainam upāgād ity eva tad āhuḥ
children.translated_text: "He approached him with <s>Sāman</s>"; that is, they say, "He approached him with what is good."

children.text: asāmnainam upāgād ity eva tad āhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: "He approached him with <s>asāman</s>"; that is what they say.
And again they also say:

children.text: sāma no bateti yat sādhu bhavati sādhu batety eva tad āhuḥ
children.translated_text: "May it be <s>Sāman</s> for us indeed," when something is good; that is, they say, "Good indeed."

children.text: asāma no bateti yad asādhu bhavaty asādhu batety eva tad āhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: "May it be <s>asāman</s> for us," when something is not good; that is, they say, "Not good indeed."

children.text: sa ya etad evaṃ vidvān sādhu sāmety upāste 'bhyāśo ha yad enaṃ sādhavo dharmā ā ca gaccheyur upa ca nameyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: He who, knowing this thus, meditates on <s>Sāman</s> as good: it is likely that good <s>dharmas</s> (qualities) will come to him and bow near to him.
In the worlds one should meditate on the <s>Sāman</s> as fivefold.
The earth is the <s>hiṅkāra</s>.
<s>Agni</s> is the <s>prastāva</s>.
The midspace is the <s>udgītha</s>.
The <s>Āditya</s> is the <s>pratihāra</s>.
Heaven is the <s>nidhana</s>.
Thus among the upward worlds.
Now among those in reverse order:
Heaven is the <s>hiṅkāra</s>.
The <s>Āditya</s> is the <s>prastāva</s>.
The midspace is the <s>udgītha</s>.
Fire is the <s>pratihāra</s>.
The earth is the <s>nidhana</s>.

children.text: kalpante hāsmai lokā ūrdhvāś cāvṛttaś ca ya etad evaṃ vidvāṃl lokeṣu pañcavidhaṃ sāmopāste ||
children.translated_text: For him the worlds, both the higher and the lower, become fit who, knowing this in this way, meditates on the fivefold <s>Sāman</s> among the worlds.
One should meditate on the fivefold <s>Sāman</s> in rain.
The wind before the rain is the <s>hiṅkāra</s>.
A cloud forms; that is the <s>prastāva</s>.
It rains; that is the <s>udgītha</s>.
It flashes and thunders; that is the <s>pratihāra</s>.

children.text: udgṛhṇāti tan nidhanaṃ varṣayati ha ya etad evaṃ vidvān vṛṣṭau pañcavidhaṃ sāmopāste ||
children.translated_text: It lifts up; that is the <s>nidhana</s>. He indeed causes rain to fall who, knowing this in this way, meditates on the fivefold <s>Sāman</s> in rain.
One should meditate on the fivefold <s>Sāman</s> in all waters.
When the cloud gathers together, that is the <s>hiṅkāra</s>.
When it rains, that is the <s>prastāva</s>.
The waters that flow eastward are the <s>udgītha</s>.
Those that flow westward are the <s>pratihāra</s>.
The ocean is the <s>nidhana</s>.

children.text: na hāpsu praity apsumān bhavati ya etad evaṃ vidvān sarvāsv apsu pañcavidhaṃ sāmopāste ||
children.translated_text: He does not perish in waters, and he becomes possessed of waters, who, knowing this in this way, meditates on the fivefold <s>Sāman</s> in all waters.
One should meditate on the fivefold <s>Sāman</s> in the seasons.
Spring is the <s>hiṅkāra</s>.
Summer is the <s>prastāva</s>.
The rains are the <s>udgītha</s>.
Autumn is the <s>pratihāra</s>.
Winter is the <s>nidhana</s>.

children.text: kalpante hāsmā ṛtava ṛtumān bhavati ya etad evaṃ vidvān ṛtuṣu pañcavidhaṃ sāmopāste ||
children.translated_text: The seasons become fit for him, and he becomes possessed of seasons, who, knowing this in this way, meditates on the fivefold <s>Sāman</s> in the seasons.
One should meditate on the fivefold <s>Sāman</s> among animals.
Goats are the <s>hiṅkāra</s>.
Sheep are the <s>prastāva</s>.
Cows are the <s>udgītha</s>.
Horses are the <s>pratihāra</s>.
A human being is the <s>nidhana</s>.

children.text: bhavanti hāsya paśavaḥ paśumān bhavati ya etad evaṃ vidvān paśuṣu pañcavidhaṃ sāmopāste ||
children.translated_text: Animals become his, and he becomes possessed of animals, who, knowing this in this way, meditates on the fivefold <s>Sāman</s> among animals.
One should meditate on the fivefold, increasingly higher <s>Sāman</s> in the vital powers.
The <s>prāṇa</s> is the <s>hiṅkāra</s>.
Speech is the <s>prastāva</s>.
The eye is the <s>udgītha</s>.
The ear is the <s>pratihāra</s>.
The mind is the <s>nidhana</s>.
These, indeed, are increasingly higher.

children.text: parovarīyo hāsya bhavati parovarīyaso ha lokāñ jayati ya etad evaṃ vidvān prāṇeṣu pañcavidhaṃ parovarīyaḥ sāmopāste
children.translated_text: He becomes increasingly higher, and he wins increasingly higher worlds, who, knowing this in this way, meditates on the fivefold, increasingly higher <s>Sāman</s> in the vital powers.
Thus, then, concerning the fivefold one.
Now concerning the sevenfold one.
One should meditate on the sevenfold <s>Sāman</s> in speech.

children.text: yat kiṃca vāco hum iti sa hiṅkāraḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever part of speech is 'hum' is the <s>hiṅkāra</s>.
What is 'pra' is the <s>prastāva</s>.
What is 'ā' is the beginning.
What is 'ud' is the <s>udgītha</s>.
What is 'prati' is the <s>pratihāra</s>.
What is 'upa' is the <s>upadrava</s>.
What is 'ni' is the <s>nidhana</s>.

children.text: dugdhe 'smai vāg dohaṃ yo vāco dohaḥ
children.translated_text: Speech milks out milk for him, whatever yield speech has.
He becomes possessed of food and an eater of food,

children.text: ya etad evaṃ vidvān vāci saptavidhaṃ sāmopāste ||
children.translated_text: who, knowing this in this way, meditates on the sevenfold <s>Sāman</s> in speech.

children.text: atha khalv amum ādityaṃ saptavidhaṃ sāmopāsīta
children.translated_text: Now, further, one should meditate on that sun as the sevenfold <s>Sāman</s>.
It is always equal; by that it is <s>Sāman</s>.

children.text: māṃ prati māṃ pratīti sarveṇa samas tena sāma ||
children.translated_text: It is equal toward all, as if toward me, toward me; by that it is <s>Sāman</s>.

children.text: tasminn imāni sarvāṇi bhūtāny anvāyattānīti vidyāt
children.translated_text: One should know that all these beings are dependent on it.
Of it, what is before sunrise is the <s>hiṅkāra</s>.
Its animals are dependent on that.
Therefore they make the sound 'hiṃ'.
For they share in the <s>hiṅkāra</s> of this <s>Sāman</s>.
Now, what is at first sunrise is the <s>prastāva</s>.
Its human beings are dependent on that.
Therefore they desire praise and desire commendation.
For they share in the <s>prastāva</s> of this <s>Sāman</s>.
Now, what is at the time of the forenoon is the beginning.
Its birds are dependent on that.
Therefore, in the midspace, without support, they hold themselves up and fly about.
For they share in the beginning of this <s>Sāman</s>.

children.text: atha yat saṃprati madhyaṃdine sa udgīthaḥ
children.translated_text: Now, what is exactly at midday is the <s>udgītha</s>.
Its gods are dependent on that.
Therefore they are the best among the offspring of <s>Prajāpati</s>.
For they share in the <s>udgītha</s> of this <s>Sāman</s>.

children.text: atha yad ūrdhvaṃ madhyaṃdināt prāg aparāhṇāt sa pratihāraḥ
children.translated_text: Now, what is after midday and before afternoon is the <s>pratihāra</s>.
Its embryos are dependent on that.
Therefore they are held back and do not fall down.
For they share in the <s>pratihāra</s> of this <s>Sāman</s>.

children.text: atha yad ūrdhvam aparāhṇāt prāg astamayāt sa upadravaḥ
children.translated_text: Now, what is after afternoon and before sunset is the <s>upadrava</s>.
Its forest creatures are dependent on that.

children.text: tasmāt te puruṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā kakṣaṃ śvabhram ity upadravanti
children.translated_text: Therefore, when they have seen a man, they run off, thinking, 'A thicket! A pit!'
For they share in the <s>upadrava</s> of this <s>Sāman</s>.
Now, what is at first sunset is the <s>nidhana</s>.
Its ancestors are dependent on that.
Therefore they lay them away.
For they share in the <s>nidhana</s> of this <s>Sāman</s>.

children.text: evaṃ khalv amum ādityaṃ saptavidhaṃ sāmopāste ||
children.translated_text: Thus, indeed, one meditates on that sun as the sevenfold <s>Sāman</s>.

children.text: atha khalv ātmasaṃmitam atimṛtyu saptavidhaṃ sāmopāsīta
children.translated_text: Now, further, one should meditate on the self-measured, death-transcending, sevenfold <s>Sāman</s>.
'<s>Hiṅkāra</s>' has three syllables.
'<s>Prastāva</s>' has three syllables.
That is equal.
'<s>Ādi</s>' has two syllables.
'<s>Pratihāra</s>' has four syllables.
From that, here there is one.
That is equal.

children.text: udgītha iti tryakṣaram upadrava iti caturakṣaraṃ tribhis tribhiḥ samaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: '<s>Udgītha</s>' has three syllables; '<s>upadrava</s>' has four syllables. By three and three it becomes equal.
One syllable remains over; it is three-syllabled.
That is equal.
'<s>Nidhana</s>' has three syllables.
That indeed becomes equal.

children.text: tāni ha vā etāni dvāviṃśatir akṣarāṇi ||
children.translated_text: These, indeed, are twenty-two syllables.
By twenty-one he obtains the sun.
For that sun is twenty-first from here.
With the twenty-second he wins what is beyond the sun.
That is heaven.
That is free from sorrow.
Here he obtains victory over the sun.

children.text: paro hāsyādityajayāj jayo bhavati ya etad evaṃ vidvān ātmasaṃmitam atimṛtyu saptavidhaṃ sāmopāste sāmopāste ||
children.translated_text: Beyond his victory over the sun there is victory for him who, knowing this in this way, meditates on the self-measured, death-transcending, sevenfold <s>Sāman</s>, meditates on the <s>Sāman</s>.
The mind is the <s>hiṅkāra</s>.
Speech is the <s>prastāva</s>.
The eye is the <s>udgītha</s>.
The ear is the <s>pratihāra</s>.
The <s>prāṇa</s> is the <s>nidhana</s>.
This <s>gāyatra</s> is woven upon the breaths.

children.text: sa ya evam etad gāyatraṃ prāṇeṣu protaṃ veda
children.translated_text: He who knows this <s>gāyatra</s> as woven upon the breaths
becomes full of life.
He reaches the full span of life.
He lives long.
He becomes great through offspring and cattle,
great through fame.
He should be great-minded.
That is the observance.
He rubs the fire-stick: that is the <s>hiṅkāra</s>.
Smoke arises: that is the <s>prastāva</s>.
It blazes: that is the <s>udgītha</s>.
Coals come into being: that is the <s>pratihāra</s>.
It subsides: that is the <s>nidhana</s>.
It becomes fully quiet: that is the <s>nidhana</s>.
This <s>Rathaṃtara</s> is woven in fire.

children.text: sa ya evam etad rathaṃtaram agnau protaṃ veda
children.translated_text: He who knows this <s>Rathaṃtara</s> as woven in fire
becomes brilliant in sacred knowledge and an eater of food.
He reaches the full span of life.
He lives long.
He becomes great through offspring and cattle,
great through fame.

children.text: na pratyaṅṅ agnim ācāmen na niṣṭhīvet
children.translated_text: He should not sip water toward the fire, nor spit toward it.
That is the observance.
He invites her: that is the <s>hiṅkāra</s>.
He makes it known: that is the <s>prastāva</s>.
He lies together with the woman: that is the <s>udgītha</s>.

children.text: prati strīṃ saha śete sa pratihāraḥ
children.translated_text: He lies with the woman face to face: that is the <s>pratihāra</s>.
He reaches the appointed time: that is the <s>nidhana</s>.
He reaches the far shore: that is the <s>nidhana</s>.
This <s>Vāmadevya</s> is woven in sexual union.

children.text: sa ya evam etad vāmadevyaṃ mithune protaṃ veda
children.translated_text: He who knows this <s>Vāmadevya</s> as woven in sexual union
becomes paired.
From pair after pair he brings forth offspring.
He reaches the full span of life.
He lives long.
He becomes great through offspring and cattle,
great through fame.
He should not reject any woman.
That is the observance.
The sun as it rises is the <s>hiṅkāra</s>.
When risen, it is the <s>prastāva</s>.
At midday it is the <s>udgītha</s>.
In the afternoon it is the <s>pratihāra</s>.
As it sets, it is the <s>nidhana</s>.
This <s>Bṛhad</s> is woven in the sun.

children.text: sa ya evam etad bṛhad āditye protaṃ veda
children.translated_text: He who knows this <s>Bṛhad</s> as woven in the sun
becomes radiant and an eater of food.
He reaches the full span of life.
He lives long.
He becomes great through offspring and cattle,
great through fame.
He should not disparage it when it is burning hot.
That is the observance.
Cloud-banks gather together: that is the <s>hiṅkāra</s>.
A rain-cloud arises: that is the <s>prastāva</s>.
It rains: that is the <s>udgītha</s>.
It flashes and thunders: that is the <s>pratihāra</s>.
It draws up the waters: that is the <s>nidhana</s>.
This <s>Vairūpa</s> is woven in <s>Parjanya</s>.

children.text: sa ya evam etad vairūpaṃ parjanye protaṃ veda
children.translated_text: He who knows this <s>Vairūpa</s> as woven in <s>Parjanya</s>

children.text: virūpāṃś ca surūpāṃś ca paśūn avarundhe
children.translated_text: secures cattle both varied in form and beautiful in form.
He reaches the full span of life.
He lives long.
He becomes great through offspring and cattle,
great through fame.
He should not disparage it when it is raining.
That is the observance.
Spring is the <s>hiṅkāra</s>.
Summer is the <s>prastāva</s>.
The rains are the <s>udgītha</s>.
Autumn is the <s>pratihāra</s>.
Winter is the <s>nidhana</s>.
This <s>Vairāja</s> is woven in the seasons.

children.text: sa ya evam etad vairājam ṛtuṣu protaṃ veda
children.translated_text: He who knows this <s>Vairāja</s> as woven in the seasons
shines with offspring,
with cattle and sacred brilliance.
He reaches the full span of life.
He lives long.
He becomes great through offspring and cattle,
great through fame.
He should not disparage the seasons.
That is the observance.
The earth is the <s>hiṅkāra</s>.
The midspace is the <s>prastāva</s>.
Heaven is the <s>udgītha</s>.
The directions are the <s>pratihāra</s>.
The ocean is the <s>nidhana</s>.
These <s>Śakvarī</s> chants are woven in the worlds.

children.text: sa ya evam etāḥ śakvaryo lokeṣu protā veda
children.translated_text: He who knows these <s>Śakvarī</s> chants as woven in the worlds
becomes possessed of worlds and reaches the full span of life.
He lives long.
He becomes great through offspring and cattle,
great through fame.
He should not disparage the worlds.
That is the observance.
Goats are the <s>hiṅkāra</s>.
Sheep are the <s>prastāva</s>.
Cows are the <s>udgītha</s>.
Horses are the <s>pratihāra</s>.
Man is the <s>nidhana</s>.
These <s>Revatī</s> chants are woven in animals.

children.text: sa ya evam etā revatyaḥ paśuṣu protā veda
children.translated_text: He who knows these <s>Revatī</s> chants as woven in animals
becomes possessed of animals.
He reaches the full span of life.
He lives long.
He becomes great through offspring and cattle,
great through fame.
He should not disparage animals.
That is the observance.
Hair is the <s>hiṅkāra</s>.
Skin is the <s>prastāva</s>.
Flesh is the <s>udgītha</s>.
Bone is the <s>pratihāra</s>.
Marrow is the <s>nidhana</s>.
This <s>Yajñāyajñīya</s> is woven in the limbs.

children.text: sa ya evam etad yajñāyajñīyam aṅgeṣu protaṃ veda
children.translated_text: He who knows this <s>Yajñāyajñīya</s> as woven in the limbs
becomes possessed of complete limbs.
He does not become deficient in any limb.
He reaches the full span of life.
He lives long.
He becomes great through offspring and cattle,
great through fame.
For a year he should not eat marrow.
That is the observance.
Or simply, he should not eat marrow.
Fire is the <s>hiṅkāra</s>.
Wind is the <s>prastāva</s>.
The sun is the <s>udgītha</s>.
The stars are the <s>pratihāra</s>.
The moon is the <s>nidhana</s>.
This <s>Rājana</s> is woven among the deities.

children.text: sa ya evam etad rājanaṃ devatāsu protaṃ veda
children.translated_text: He who knows this <s>Rājana</s> as woven among the deities

children.text: etāsām eva devatānāṃ salokatāṃ sarṣṭitāṃ sāyujyaṃ gacchati
children.translated_text: attains sharing the same world, the same lordly power, and union with these very deities.
He reaches the full span of life.
He lives long.
He becomes great through offspring and cattle,
great through fame.
He should not disparage Brahmins.
That is the observance.
The threefold knowledge is the <s>hiṅkāra</s>.
These three worlds are the <s>prastāva</s>.
Fire, wind, and the sun are the <s>udgītha</s>.
The stars, birds, and rays are the <s>pratihāra</s>.
Serpents, <s>Gandharvas</s>, and the Fathers are the <s>nidhana</s>.
This <s>Sāman</s> is woven in everything.

children.text: sa ya evam etat sāma sarvasmin protaṃ veda sarvaṃ ha bhavati ||
children.translated_text: He who knows this <s>Sāman</s> as woven in everything indeed becomes everything.
On this there is this verse:
Whatever things are fivefold, three groups of three,

children.text: tebhyo na jyāyaḥ param anyad asti ||
children.translated_text: there is nothing else higher or beyond them.

children.text: yas tad veda sa veda sarvam
children.translated_text: Whoever knows that knows everything.
All the directions bring tribute to him.
One should meditate: 'I am everything.'
That is the observance; that is the observance.

children.text: vinardi sāmno vṛṇe paśavyam ity agner udgīthaḥ
children.translated_text: 'I choose the roaring, cattle-bringing one of the <s>Sāman</s>': this is the <s>udgītha</s> of fire.
The indistinct one belongs to <s>Prajāpati</s>.
The distinct one belongs to <s>Soma</s>.
Soft and smooth belongs to <s>Vāyu</s>.
Smooth and strong belongs to <s>Indra</s>.
The heron-like tone belongs to <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.
The obscured tone belongs to <s>Varuṇa</s>.
One should practice all of these.
But one should avoid the <s>Vāruṇa</s> tone.
He should sing, thinking, "May I sing forth immortality for the gods."

children.text: svadhāṃ pitṛbhya āśāṃ manuṣyebhyas tṛṇodakaṃ paśubhyaḥ svargaṃ lokaṃ yajamānāyānnam ātmana āgāyānīty etāni manasā dhyāyann apramattaḥ stuvīta ||
children.translated_text: He should praise attentively, meditating on these things in his mind: "May I sing forth <s>svadhā</s> for the ancestors, hope for human beings, grass and water for cattle, the heavenly world for the sacrificer, and food for myself."
All vowels are embodiments of <s>Indra</s>.
All sibilants and breath-sounds are embodiments of <s>Prajāpati</s>.
All stops are embodiments of <s>Mṛtyu</s>.
If someone should criticize him with regard to the vowels,

children.text: indraṃ śaraṇaṃ prapanno 'bhūvaṃ sa tvā prativakṣyatīty enaṃ brūyāt ||
children.translated_text: he should say to him, "I have taken refuge in <s>Indra</s>; he will answer you."
Then, if someone should criticize him with regard to the breath-sounds,

children.text: prajāpatiṃ śaraṇaṃ prapanno 'bhūvaṃ sa tvā pratipekṣyatītyenaṃ brūyāt
children.translated_text: he should say to him, "I have taken refuge in <s>Prajāpati</s>; he will look to you."
Then, if someone should criticize him with regard to the stops,

children.text: mṛtyuṃ śaraṇaṃ prapanno 'bhūvaṃ sa tvā pratidhakṣyatītyenaṃ brūyāt ||
children.translated_text: he should say to him, "I have taken refuge in <s>Mṛtyu</s>; he will burn you back."

children.text: sarve svarā ghoṣavanto balavanto vaktavyā indre balaṃ dadānīti
children.translated_text: All vowels should be pronounced sonorous and strong, thinking, "I am giving strength to <s>Indra</s>."

children.text: sarva ūṣmāṇo 'grastā anirastā vivṛtā vaktavyāḥ prajāpater ātmānaṃ paridadānīti
children.translated_text: All sibilants and breath-sounds should be pronounced unswallowed, not cast out, and open, thinking, "I am handing over the self to <s>Prajāpati</s>."

children.text: sarve sparśā leśenānabhinihitā vaktavyā mṛtyor ātmānaṃ pariharāṇīti ||
children.translated_text: All stops should be pronounced lightly and without being pressed together, thinking, "I am avoiding the self of <s>Mṛtyu</s>."
There are three branches of <s>dharma</s>.
Sacrifice, study, and giving: this is the first.
Austerity alone is the second.
The third is the student living in the teacher's household as a <s>brahmacārin</s>, settling himself completely in the teacher's household.
All these become possessors of meritorious worlds.
The one established in <s>Brahman</s> attains immortality.
<s>Prajāpati</s> brooded over the worlds.
From them, when they had been heated, the threefold knowledge flowed forth.
He brooded over it.

children.text: tasyā abhitaptāyā etāny akṣarāṇi saṃprasrvanta bhūr bhuvaḥ svar iti ||
children.translated_text: From it, when it had been heated, these syllables flowed forth: <s>bhūr</s>, <s>bhuvaḥ</s>, <s>svar</s>.
He brooded over them.
From them, when they had been heated, the syllable <s>oṃ</s> flowed forth.

children.text: tad yathā śaṅkunā sarvāṇi parṇāni saṃtṛṇṇāny evam oṃkāreṇa sarvā vāk saṃtṛṇṇā
children.translated_text: Just as all leaves are pierced together by a pin, so all speech is pierced together by the syllable <s>oṃ</s>.

children.text: oṃkāra evedaṃ sarvam oṃkāra eva idaṃ sarvam ||
children.translated_text: The <s>oṃkāra</s> alone is all this; the <s>oṃkāra</s> alone is all this.
The knowers of <s>Brahman</s> say:
"The morning pressing belongs to the <s>Vasus</s>;
the midday pressing belongs to the <s>Rudras</s>;

children.text: ādityānāṃ ca viśveṣāṃ ca devānāṃ tṛtīyasavanam ||
children.translated_text: the third pressing belongs to the <s>Ādityas</s> and to all the gods."
"Where, then, is the world of the sacrificer?"

children.text: sa yas taṃ na vidyāt kathaṃ kuryāt
children.translated_text: How should a man who did not know that perform the rite?
But one who knows should perform it.

children.text: purā prātaranuvākasyopākaraṇāj jaghanena gārhapatyasyodaṅmukha upaviśya sa vāsavaṃ sāmābhigāyati ||
children.translated_text: Before the beginning of the morning recitation, sitting behind the <s>Gārhapatya</s> fire and facing north, he sings the <s>Vāsava</s> <s>Sāman</s>.
"The door of what?"
"May we see you, we," thus.
Then he makes an oblation.
"Homage to <s>Agni</s>, dwelling on earth, dwelling in the world.
Find a world for me, the sacrificer.
This indeed is the sacrificer's world.
Here I am."
"Here is the sacrificer, beyond the span of life. Svāhā."
Having said, "Remove the bolt," he rises.
For him the <s>Vasus</s> hand over the morning pressing.

children.text: purā mādhyaṃdinasya savanasyopākaraṇāj jaghanenāgnīdhrīyasyodaṅmukha upaviśya sa raudraṃ sāmābhigāyati ||
children.translated_text: Before the beginning of the midday pressing, sitting behind the <s>Āgnīdhrīya</s> fire and facing north, he sings the <s>Raudra</s> <s>Sāman</s>.
"Open the door of what," with the prolonged chant-syllable.
"May we see you, we," thus.
Then he makes an oblation.
"Homage to <s>Vāyu</s>, dwelling in the midspace, dwelling in the world.
Find a world for me, the sacrificer.
This indeed is the sacrificer's world.
Here I am."
"Here is the sacrificer, beyond the span of life. Svāhā."
Having said, "Remove the bolt," he rises.
For him the <s>Rudras</s> hand over the midday pressing.

children.text: purā tṛtīyasavanasyopākaraṇāj jaghanenāhavanīyasyodaṅmukha upaviśya sa ādityaṃ sa vaiśvadevaṃ sāmābhigāyati ||
children.translated_text: Before the beginning of the third pressing, sitting behind the <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire and facing north, he sings the <s>Āditya</s> and the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> <s>Sāman</s>.
Then the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> chant.
"Open the door of the world," with prolonged chant-syllables.
"May we see you, we, hum," thus.
Then he makes an oblation.

children.text: nama ādityebhyaś ca viśvebhyaś ca devebhyo divikṣidbhyo lokakṣidbhyaḥ
children.translated_text: "Homage to the <s>Ādityas</s> and to all the gods, dwelling in heaven, dwelling in the world.
Find a world for me, the sacrificer.
This indeed is the sacrificer's world.

children.text: etāsmy atra yajamānaḥ parastād āyuṣaḥ svāhā
children.translated_text: Here I am; here is the sacrificer, beyond the span of life. Svāhā."
Having said, "Remove the bolt," he rises.

children.text: tasmā ādityāś ca viśve ca devās tṛtīyasavanaṃ samprayacchanti
children.translated_text: For him the <s>Ādityas</s> and all the gods hand over the third pressing.

children.text: eṣa ha vai yajñasya mātrāṃ veda ya evaṃ veda ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He who knows thus knows the measure of the sacrifice; he who knows thus, he who knows thus.
That sun is indeed the honey of the gods.
Its crossbeam is heaven itself.
The midspace is its honeycomb.
The rays are its offspring.

children.text: tasya ye prāñco raśmayas tā evāsya prācyo madhunāḍyaḥ
children.translated_text: The rays that are turned eastward are its eastern honey-channels.
The ṛc verses themselves are the honey-makers.
The <s>Ṛgveda</s> itself is the flower.
Those are the immortal waters.
Those, indeed, are these ṛc verses.
They brooded over this <s>Ṛgveda</s>.

children.text: tasyābhitaptasya yaśas teja indriyaṃ vīryam annādyaṃ raso 'jāyata ||
children.translated_text: From it, when it had been heated, fame, splendor, power, vigor, food, and sap were born.
That flowed out.
It took refuge all around the sun.

children.text: tad vā etad yad etad ādityasya rohitaṃ rūpam ||
children.translated_text: That, indeed, is this red form of the sun.

children.text: atha ye 'sya dakṣiṇā raśmayas tā evāsya dakṣiṇā madhunāḍyaḥ
children.translated_text: Now the rays of it that are southern are its southern honey-channels.
The yajus formulas themselves are the honey-makers.
The <s>Yajurveda</s> itself is the flower.
Those are the immortal waters.

children.text: tāni vā etāni yajūṃṣy etaṃ yajurvedam abhyatapan
children.translated_text: Those, indeed, are these yajus formulas; they brooded over this <s>Yajurveda</s>.

children.text: tasya abhitaptasya yaśas teja indriyaṃ vīryam annādyaṃ raso 'jāyata ||
children.translated_text: From it, when it had been heated, fame, splendor, power, vigor, food, and essence arose.
That flowed forth.
It took refuge all around the sun.

children.text: tad vā etad yad etad ādityasya śuklaṃ rūpam ||
children.translated_text: That, indeed, is what this white form of the sun is.

children.text: atha ye 'sya pratyañco raśmayas tā evāsya pratīcyo madhunāḍyaḥ
children.translated_text: Now those rays of his which turn westward are his western honey-channels.
The <s>Sāmans</s> themselves are the honey-makers.
The <s>Sāmaveda</s> itself is the flower.
Those are the immortal waters.

children.text: tāni vā etāni sāmāny etaṃ sāmavedam abhyatapan
children.translated_text: These <s>Sāmans</s>, indeed, heated this <s>Sāmaveda</s>.

children.text: tasyābhitaptasya yaśas teja indriyaṃ vīryam annādyaṃ raso 'jāyata ||
children.translated_text: From it, when it had been heated, fame, splendor, power, vigor, food, and essence arose.
That flowed forth.
It took refuge all around the sun.

children.text: tad vā etad yad etad ādityasya kṛṣṇaṃ rūpam ||
children.translated_text: That, indeed, is what this black form of the sun is.

children.text: atha ye 'syodañco raśmayas tā evāsyodīcyo madhunāḍyaḥ
children.translated_text: Now those rays of his which turn northward are his northern honey-channels.
The <s>Atharvāṅgirasas</s> themselves are the honey-makers.
The <s>Itihāsapurāṇa</s> is the flower.
Those are the immortal waters.

children.text: te vā ete 'tharvāṅgirasa etad itihāsapurāṇam abhyatapan
children.translated_text: These <s>Atharvāṅgirasas</s>, indeed, heated this <s>Itihāsapurāṇa</s>.

children.text: tasyābhitaptasya yaśas teja indriyaṃ vīryam annādyaṃ raso 'jāyata ||
children.translated_text: From it, when it had been heated, fame, splendor, power, vigor, food, and essence arose.
That flowed forth.
It took refuge all around the sun.

children.text: tad vā etad yad etad ādityasya paraḥkṛṣṇaṃ rūpam ||
children.translated_text: That, indeed, is what this very dark form of the sun is.

children.text: atha ye 'syordhvā raśmayas tā evāsyordhvā madhunāḍyaḥ
children.translated_text: Now those rays of his which go upward are his upward honey-channels.
The secret teachings themselves are the honey-makers.
<s>Brahman</s> itself is the flower.
Those are the immortal waters.

children.text: te vā ete guhyā ādeśā etad brahmābhyatapan
children.translated_text: These secret teachings, indeed, heated this <s>brahman</s>.

children.text: tasyābhitaptasya yaśas teja indriyaṃ vīryam annādyaṃ raso 'jāyata ||
children.translated_text: From it, when it had been heated, fame, splendor, power, vigor, food, and essence arose.
That flowed forth.
It took refuge all around the sun.

children.text: tad vā etad yad etad ādityasya madhye kṣobhata iva ||
children.translated_text: That, indeed, is what appears to tremble in the middle of the sun.
These, indeed, are the essences of essences.
For the <s>Vedas</s> are essences.
These are their essences.
These, indeed, are the immortals of the immortals.
For the <s>Vedas</s> are immortal.
These are their immortals.

children.text: tad yat prathamam amṛtaṃ tad vasava upajīvanty agninā mukhena
children.translated_text: That first <s>amṛta</s> (immortal nectar) is what the <s>Vasus</s> live upon, with <s>Agni</s> as their mouth.

children.text: na vai devā aśnanti na pibanti
children.translated_text: The gods, indeed, do not eat and do not drink.
They are satisfied simply by seeing this <s>amṛta</s>.
They enter into this very form.
From this form they arise.

children.text: sa ya etad evam amṛtaṃ veda vasūnām evaiko bhūtvāgninaiva mukhenaitad evāmṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā tṛpyati
children.translated_text: One who knows this <s>amṛta</s> thus, having become one of the <s>Vasus</s>, is satisfied simply by seeing this <s>amṛta</s> through <s>Agni</s> as his mouth.
He enters into this very form.
From this form he arises.

children.text: sa yāvad ādityaḥ purastād udetā paścād astam etā vasūnām eva tāvad ādhipatyaṃ svārājyaṃ paryetā ||
children.translated_text: So long as the sun rises in the east and sets in the west, for that long he ranges over the overlordship and sovereignty of the <s>Vasus</s>.

children.text: atha yad dvitīyam amṛtaṃ tad rudrā upajīvantīndreṇa mukhena
children.translated_text: Now that second <s>amṛta</s> is what the <s>Rudras</s> live upon, with <s>Indra</s> as their mouth.

children.text: na vai devā aśnanti na pibanti
children.translated_text: The gods, indeed, do not eat and do not drink.
They are satisfied simply by seeing this <s>amṛta</s>.
They enter into this very form.
From this form they arise.

children.text: sa ya etad evam amṛtaṃ veda rudrāṇām evaiko bhūtvendreṇaiva mukhenaitad evāmṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā tṛpyati
children.translated_text: One who knows this <s>amṛta</s> thus, having become one of the <s>Rudras</s>, is satisfied simply by seeing this <s>amṛta</s> through <s>Indra</s> as his mouth.
He enters into this very form.
From this form he arises.

children.text: sa yāvad ādityaḥ purastād udetā paścād astam etā dvis tāvad dakṣiṇata udetottarato 'stam etā rudrāṇām eva tāvad ādhipatyaṃ svārājyaṃ paryetā ||
children.translated_text: So long as the sun rises in the east and sets in the west, and for twice that long rises in the south and sets in the north, for that long he ranges over the overlordship and sovereignty of the <s>Rudras</s>.

children.text: atha yat tṛtīyam amṛtaṃ tad ādityā upajīvanti varuṇena mukhena
children.translated_text: Now that third <s>amṛta</s> is what the <s>Ādityas</s> live upon, with <s>Varuṇa</s> as their mouth.

children.text: na vai devā aśnanti na pibanti
children.translated_text: The gods, indeed, do not eat and do not drink.
They are satisfied simply by seeing this <s>amṛta</s>.
They enter into this very form.
From this form they arise.

children.text: sa ya etad evam amṛtaṃ vedādityānām evaiko bhūtvā varuṇenaiva mukhenaitad evāmṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā tṛpyati
children.translated_text: One who knows this <s>amṛta</s> thus, having become one of the <s>Ādityas</s>, is satisfied simply by seeing this <s>amṛta</s> through <s>Varuṇa</s> as his mouth.
He enters into this very form.
From this form he arises.

children.text: sa yāvad ādityo dakṣiṇata udetottarato 'stam etā dvis tāvat paścād udetā purastād astam etādityānām eva tāvad ādhipatyaṃ svārājyaṃ paryetā ||
children.translated_text: So long as the sun rises in the south and sets in the north, and for twice that long rises in the west and sets in the east, for that long he ranges over the overlordship and sovereignty of the <s>Ādityas</s>.

children.text: atha yac caturtham amṛtaṃ tan maruta upajīvanti somena mukhena
children.translated_text: Now that fourth <s>amṛta</s> is what the <s>Maruts</s> live upon, with <s>Soma</s> as their mouth.

children.text: na vai devā aśnanti na pibanti
children.translated_text: The gods, indeed, do not eat and do not drink.
They are satisfied simply by seeing this <s>amṛta</s>.
They enter into this very form.
From this form they arise.

children.text: sa ya etad evam amṛtaṃ veda marutām evaiko bhūtvā somenaiva mukhenaitad evāmṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā tṛpyati
children.translated_text: One who knows this <s>amṛta</s> thus, having become one of the <s>Maruts</s>, is satisfied simply by seeing this <s>amṛta</s> through <s>Soma</s> as his mouth.
He enters into this very form.
From this form he arises.

children.text: sa yāvad ādityaḥ paścād udetā purastād astam etā dvis tāvad uttarata udetā dakṣiṇato 'stam etā marutām eva tāvad ādhipatyaṃ svārājyaṃ paryetā ||
children.translated_text: So long as the sun rises in the west and sets in the east, and for twice that long rises in the north and sets in the south, for that long he ranges over the overlordship and sovereignty of the <s>Maruts</s>.

children.text: atha yat pañcamam amṛtaṃ tat sādhyā upajīvanti brahmaṇā mukhena
children.translated_text: Now that fifth <s>amṛta</s> is what the <s>Sādhyas</s> live upon, with <s>Brahman</s> as their mouth.

children.text: na vai devā aśnanti na pibanti
children.translated_text: The gods, indeed, do not eat and do not drink.
They are satisfied simply by seeing this <s>amṛta</s>.
They enter into this very form.
From this form they arise.

children.text: sa ya etad evam amṛtaṃ veda sādhyānām evaiko bhūtvā brahmaṇaiva mukhenaitad evāmṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā tṛpyati
children.translated_text: One who knows this <s>amṛta</s> thus, having become one of the <s>Sādhyas</s>, is satisfied simply by seeing this <s>amṛta</s> through <s>Brahman</s> as his mouth.
He enters into this very form.
From this form he arises.

children.text: sa yāvad āditya uttarata udetā dakṣiṇato 'stam etā dvis tāvad ūrdhvam udetārvāg astam etā sādhyānām eva tāvad ādhipatyaṃ svārājyaṃ paryetā ||
children.translated_text: For as long as the sun were to rise in the north and set in the south, and for twice that long were to rise upward and set downward, for just so long he would move about with overlordship and self-rule among the <s>Sādhyas</s>.

children.text: atha tata ūrdhva udetya naivodetā nāstam etaikala eva madhye sthātā
children.translated_text: Then, after that, having risen upward, it would neither rise nor set; it would stand alone in the middle.
On this there is this verse:
There, indeed, it never sets,
nor has it ever risen.
By that truth, O gods,
may I not be separated from <s>brahman</s>.

children.text: na ha vā asmā udeti na nimlocati
children.translated_text: For him, indeed, the sun does not rise and does not set.
For him it is day once and for all.
This is so for the one who knows this <s>brahmopaniṣad</s>, this secret teaching of <s>brahman</s>, in this way.
This, indeed, <s>Brahmā</s> spoke to <s>Prajāpati</s>.
<s>Prajāpati</s> spoke it to <s>Manu</s>.
<s>Manu</s> spoke it to his offspring.

children.text: taddhaitad uddālakāyāruṇaye jyeṣṭhāya putrāya pitā brahma provāca ||
children.translated_text: This, indeed, the father spoke as <s>brahman</s> to <s>Uddālaka Āruṇi</s>, his eldest son.

children.text: idaṃ vāva taj jyeṣṭhāya putrāya pitā brahma prabrūyāt praṇāyyāya vāntevāsine ||
children.translated_text: A father should speak this <s>brahman</s> only to his eldest son, or to a worthy resident pupil.
He should not speak it to anyone else at all.

children.text: yady apy asmā imām adbhiḥ parigṛhītāṃ dhanasya pūrṇāṃ dadyād etad eva tato bhūya iti ||
children.translated_text: Even if someone were to give him this earth, encircled by waters and full of wealth, this teaching alone would be greater than that.

children.text: gāyatrī vā idaṃ sarvaṃ bhūtaṃ yad idam kiṃca
children.translated_text: <s>Gāyatrī</s>, indeed, is all this, whatever being there is here.
Speech, indeed, is <s>Gāyatrī</s>.

children.text: vāg vā idaṃ sarvaṃ bhūtaṃ gāyati ca trāyate ca ||
children.translated_text: For speech sings of all this being and protects it.

children.text: yā vai sā gāyatrīyaṃ vāva sā yeyaṃ pṛthivī
children.translated_text: That which is <s>Gāyatrī</s> is truly this earth here.
For on this earth all this being is established.
It does not go beyond this earth.

children.text: yā vai sā pṛthivīyaṃ vāva sā yad idam asmin puruṣe śarīram
children.translated_text: That which is this earth is truly this body here in the person.
For in this body these <s>prāṇas</s> (vital breaths) are established.
They do not go beyond this body.

children.text: yad vai tat puruṣe śarīram idaṃ vāva tad yad idam asminn antaḥ puruṣe hṛdayam
children.translated_text: That which is the body in the person is truly this heart here within the inner person.
For in this heart these <s>prāṇas</s> are established.
They do not go beyond this heart.
This, then, is the four-footed, sixfold <s>Gāyatrī</s>.
This has been declared by a Ṛg-verse:

children.text: tāvān asya mahimā tato jyāyāṃś ca puruṣaḥ
children.translated_text: So great is his greatness, and the <s>puruṣa</s> (person) is greater than that.

children.text: pādo 'sya sarvā bhūtāni tripād asyāmṛtaṃ divīti ||
children.translated_text: All beings are one quarter of him; three quarters of him are the immortal in heaven.

children.text: yad vai tad brahmetīdaṃ vāva tad yo 'yaṃ bahirdhā puruṣād ākāśaḥ
children.translated_text: That which is called <s>brahman</s> is truly this space outside the person.

children.text: yo vai sa bahirdhā puruṣād ākāśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That which is the space outside the person

children.text: ayaṃ vāva sa yo 'yam antaḥ puruṣa ākāśaḥ
children.translated_text: is truly this space here within the person.
That which is the space within the person

children.text: ayaṃ vāva sa yo 'yam antarhṛdaya ākāśaḥ
children.translated_text: is truly this space here within the heart.
That is full and unmoving.

children.text: pūrṇam apravartinīṃ śriyaṃ labhate ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: The one who knows this in this way obtains full, unmoving prosperity.

children.text: tasya ha vā etasya hṛdayasya pañca devasuṣayaḥ
children.translated_text: Of this heart there are, indeed, five divine openings.

children.text: sa yo 'sya prāṅ suṣiḥ sa prāṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Its eastern opening is <s>prāṇa</s>.
That is the eye.
That is the sun.
One should meditate on this as brilliance and the eating of food.

children.text: tejasvy annādo bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: The one who knows this in this way becomes brilliant and an eater of food.

children.text: atha yo 'sya dakṣiṇaḥ suṣiḥ sa vyānaḥ
children.translated_text: Now its southern opening is <s>vyāna</s>.
That is the ear.
That is the moon.

children.text: tad etac chrīś ca yaśaś cety upāsīta
children.translated_text: One should meditate on this as prosperity and fame.

children.text: śrīmān yaśasvī bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: The one who knows this in this way becomes prosperous and famous.
Now its western opening is <s>apāna</s>.
That is speech.
That is fire.

children.text: tad etad brahmavarcasam annādyam ity upāsīta
children.translated_text: One should meditate on this as sacred luster and the eating of food.

children.text: brahmavarcasy annādo bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: The one who knows this in this way becomes endowed with sacred luster and an eater of food.
Now its northern opening is <s>samāna</s>.
That is the mind.
That is <s>Parjanya</s>.

children.text: tad etat kīrtiś ca vyuṣṭiś cetyupāsīta
children.translated_text: One should meditate on this as fame and brightness.

children.text: kīrtimān vyuṣṭimān bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: The one who knows this in this way becomes famous and bright.
Now its upward opening is <s>udāna</s>.
That is wind.
That is space.

children.text: tad etad ojaś ca mahaś cety upāsīta
children.translated_text: One should meditate on this as vigor and greatness.

children.text: ojasvī mahasvān bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: The one who knows this in this way becomes vigorous and great.

children.text: te vā ete pañca brahmapuruṣāḥ svargasya lokasya dvārapāḥ
children.translated_text: These five, indeed, are the <s>brahmapuruṣas</s>, the persons of <s>brahman</s>, the gatekeepers of the heavenly world.

children.text: sa ya etān evaṃ pañca brahmapuruṣān svargasya lokasya dvārapān vedāsya kule vīro jāyate
children.translated_text: For the one who knows these five <s>brahmapuruṣas</s> in this way as the gatekeepers of the heavenly world, a hero is born in his family.

children.text: pratipadyate svargaṃ lokaṃ ya etān evaṃ pañca brahmapuruṣān svargasya lokasya dvārapān veda ||
children.translated_text: The one who knows these five <s>brahmapuruṣas</s> in this way as the gatekeepers of the heavenly world reaches the heavenly world.

children.text: atha yad ataḥ paro divo jyotir dīpyate viśvataḥpṛṣṭheṣu sarvataḥpṛṣṭheṣv anuttameṣūttameṣu lokeṣv idaṃ vāva tad yad idam asminn antaḥ puruṣe jyotiḥ
children.translated_text: Now the light that shines beyond heaven, on the backs of all, on the backs of everything, in the unsurpassed and highest worlds, is truly this light here within the person.

children.text: tasyaiṣā dṛṣṭir yatraitad asmiñcharīre saṃsparśenoṣṇimānaṃ vijānāti
children.translated_text: Its visible sign is this: where, in this body, one recognizes warmth by touch.

children.text: tasyaiṣā śrutir yatraitat karṇāv apigṛhya ninadam iva nadathur ivāgner iva jvalata upaśṛṇoti
children.translated_text: Its audible sign is this: when, having covered the ears, one hears something like a roar, like a rumbling, like a blazing fire.

children.text: tad etad dṛṣṭaṃ ca śrutaṃ cety upāsīta
children.translated_text: One should meditate on this as what is seen and heard.

children.text: cakṣuṣyaḥ śruto bhavati ya evaṃ veda ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: The one who knows this in this way becomes fit to be seen and renowned; the one who knows this in this way, the one who knows this in this way.

children.text: sarvaṃ khalv idaṃ brahma tajjalān iti śānta upāsīta
children.translated_text: All this, indeed, is <s>brahman</s>. As 'arising from that, dissolving into that, breathing by that,' one should meditate in tranquility.

children.text: atha khalu kratumayaḥ puruṣo yathākratur asmiṃl loke puruṣo bhavati tathetaḥ pretya bhavati
children.translated_text: Now, indeed, a person is made of resolve: as a person's resolve is in this world, so he becomes after departing from here.
He should form a resolve.

children.text: manomayaḥ prāṇaśarīro bhārūpaḥ satyasaṃkalpa ākāśātmā sarvakarmā sarvakāmaḥ sarvagandhaḥ sarvarasaḥ sarvam idam abhyatto 'vāky anādaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: He is made of mind, has <s>prāṇa</s> as his body, has light as his form, has true resolve, has space as his self, performs all actions, possesses all desires, all fragrances, and all tastes, embraces all this, is without speech, and is unconcerned.

children.text: eṣa ma ātmā antarhṛdaye 'ṇīyān vrīher vā yavād vā sarṣapād vā śyāmākād vā śyāmākataṇḍulād vā
children.translated_text: This <s>ātman</s> (self) of mine within the heart is smaller than a rice grain, or a barley grain, or a mustard seed, or a millet grain, or the kernel of a millet grain.

children.text: eṣa ma ātmā antarhṛdaye jyāyān pṛthivyā jyāyān antarikṣāj jyāyān divo jyāyān ebhyo lokebhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This <s>ātman</s> of mine within the heart is greater than the earth, greater than the midspace, greater than heaven, greater than these worlds.

children.text: sarvakarmā sarvakāmaḥ sarvagandhaḥ sarvarasaḥ sarvam idam abhyatto 'vākyanādaraḥ
children.translated_text: Having all actions, all desires, all smells, and all tastes, containing all this, speechless and unconcerned,
this is my <s>ātman</s> within the heart.
This is <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: etam itaḥ pretyābhisaṃbhavitā asmīti yasya syād addhā na vicikitsā asti
children.translated_text: If someone has the firm thought, 'After departing from here I shall attain him,' and has no doubt,
so indeed said <s>Śāṇḍilya</s>, <s>Śāṇḍilya</s>.
The vessel whose belly is the atmosphere and whose bottom is the earth does not decay.

children.text: diśo hy asya sraktayo dyaur asyottaraṃ bilam
children.translated_text: For the directions are its corners, and heaven is its upper opening.

children.text: sa eṣa kośo vasudhānas tasmin viśvam idaṃ śritam ||
children.translated_text: This vessel is a treasury; in it this whole universe is lodged.
Its eastern direction is named <s>Juhū</s>.
The southern one is named <s>Sahamānā</s>.
The western one is named <s>Rājñī</s>.
The northern one is named <s>Subhūtā</s>.
Of these, wind is the calf.

children.text: sa ya etam evaṃ vāyuṃ diśāṃ vatsaṃ veda na putrarodaṃ roditi
