children.translated_text: He who knows this wind thus as the calf of the directions does not weep the weeping for a son.

children.text: so 'ham etam evaṃ vāyuṃ diśāṃ vatsaṃ veda
children.translated_text: I know this wind thus as the calf of the directions.
May I not weep the weeping for a son.
I resort to the uninjured vessel, with this one, with this one, with this one.
I resort to <s>prāṇa</s>, with this one, with this one, with this one.
I resort to <s>bhūḥ</s>, with this one, with this one, with this one.
I resort to <s>bhuvaḥ</s>, with this one, with this one, with this one.
I resort to <s>svaḥ</s>, with this one, with this one, with this one.

children.text: sa yad avocaṃ prāṇaṃ prapadya iti
children.translated_text: Now when I said, 'I resort to <s>prāṇa</s>,'

children.text: prāṇo vā idaṃ sarvaṃ bhūtaṃ yad idaṃ kiṃca
children.translated_text: <s>Prāṇa</s> is indeed all this that has come into being, whatever there is here.
That indeed was what he resorted to.

children.text: atha yad avocaṃ bhuvaḥ prapadya ity agniṃ prapadye vāyuṃ prapadya ādityaṃ prapadya ity eva tad avocam ||
children.translated_text: And when I said, 'I resort to <s>bhuvaḥ</s>,' it was just this that I said: 'I resort to fire, I resort to wind, I resort to the sun.'

children.text: atha yad avocaṃ svaḥ prapadya ity ṛgvedaṃ prapadye yajurvedaṃ prapadye sāmavedaṃ prapadya ity eva tad avocam ||
children.translated_text: And when I said, 'I resort to <s>svaḥ</s>,' it was just this that I said: 'I resort to the <s>Ṛgveda</s>, I resort to the <s>Yajurveda</s>, I resort to the <s>Sāmaveda</s>.'
The person is indeed the sacrifice.
Of him, those twenty-four years are the morning pressing.
The <s>Gāyatrī</s> has twenty-four syllables.
The morning pressing is in the <s>Gāyatrī</s> meter.
The <s>Vasus</s> are assigned to this of his.
The <s>prāṇas</s> are indeed the <s>Vasus</s>.
For these cause all this to dwell.

children.text: taṃ ced etasmin vayasi kiṃcid upatapet sa brūyāt
children.translated_text: If anything should afflict him at this age, he should say:

children.text: prāṇā vasava idaṃ me prātaḥsavanaṃ mādhyaṃdinaṃ savanam anusaṃtanuteti māhaṃ prāṇānāṃ vasūnāṃ madhye yajño vilopsīyeti
children.translated_text: O <s>prāṇas</s>, O <s>Vasus</s>, extend this morning pressing of mine to the midday pressing, so that I, the sacrifice, may not be interrupted in the midst of the <s>prāṇas</s>, the <s>Vasus</s>.

children.text: uddhaiva tata ety agado ha bhavati ||
children.translated_text: He rises up from that very condition and becomes free from disease.

children.text: atha yāni catuścatvāriṃśadvarṣāṇi tan mādhyaṃdinaṃ savanam
children.translated_text: Now those forty-four years are the midday pressing.
The <s>Triṣṭubh</s> has forty-four syllables.
The midday pressing is in the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> meter.
The <s>Rudras</s> are assigned to this of his.
The <s>prāṇas</s> are indeed the <s>Rudras</s>.
For these make all this cry out.

children.text: taṃ ced etasmin vayasi kiṃcid upatapet sa brūyāt
children.translated_text: If anything should afflict him at this age, he should say:

children.text: prāṇā rudrā idaṃ me mādhyaṃdinaṃ savanaṃ tṛtīyasavanam anusaṃtanuteti māhaṃ prāṇānāṃ rudrāṇāṃ madhye yajño vilopsīyeti
children.translated_text: O <s>prāṇas</s>, O <s>Rudras</s>, extend this midday pressing of mine to the third pressing, so that I, the sacrifice, may not be interrupted in the midst of the <s>prāṇas</s>, the <s>Rudras</s>.

children.text: uddhaiva tata ety agado ha bhavati ||
children.translated_text: He rises up from that very condition and becomes free from disease.
Now those forty-eight years are the third pressing.
The <s>Jagatī</s> has forty-eight syllables.
The third pressing is in the <s>Jagatī</s> meter.
The <s>Ādityas</s> are assigned to this of his.
The <s>prāṇas</s> are indeed the <s>Ādityas</s>.
For these take all this up.

children.text: taṃ ced etasmin vayasi kiṃcid upatapet sa brūyāt
children.translated_text: If anything should afflict him at this age, he should say:

children.text: prāṇā ādityā idaṃ me tṛtīyasavanam āyur anusaṃtanuteti māhaṃ prāṇānām ādityānāṃ madhye yajño vilopsīyeti
children.translated_text: O <s>prāṇas</s>, O <s>Ādityas</s>, extend this third pressing of mine to the full span of life, so that I, the sacrifice, may not be interrupted in the midst of the <s>prāṇas</s>, the <s>Ādityas</s>.

children.text: uddhaiva tata ety agado haiva bhavati ||
children.translated_text: He rises up from that very condition and indeed becomes free from disease.

children.text: etaddha sma vai tad vidvān āha mahidāsa aitareyaḥ
children.translated_text: Knowing this, <s>Mahidāsa Aitareya</s> used to say:

children.text: sa kiṃ ma etad upatapasi yo 'ham anena na preṣyām iti
children.translated_text: 'Why do you afflict me with this, since I shall not die from it?'
He lived one hundred and sixteen years.

children.text: pra ha ṣoḍaśaṃ varṣaśataṃ jīvati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He who knows thus indeed lives one hundred and sixteen years.

children.text: sa yad aśiśiṣati yat pipāsati yan na ramate tā asya dīkṣāḥ ||
children.translated_text: When he wishes to eat, when he thirsts, and when he does not enjoy himself, those are his consecrations.

children.text: atha yad aśnāti yat pibati yad ramate tad upasadair eti ||
children.translated_text: Now when he eats, when he drinks, and when he enjoys himself, he approaches the <s>upasad</s> rites.

children.text: atha yaddhasati yaj jakṣati yan maithunaṃ carati stutaśastrair eva tad eti ||
children.translated_text: Now when he laughs, when he eats heartily, and when he has sexual intercourse, thereby he approaches the chants and recitations.

children.text: atha yat tapo dānam ārjavam ahiṃsā satyavacanam iti tā asya dakṣiṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now austerity, giving, straightforwardness, non-injury, and truth-speaking: these are his sacrificial fees.
Therefore they say, 'He will bring forth,' and 'he has brought forth.'
That is precisely his producing again.
Death itself is the final bath.
After <s>Ghora Āṅgirasa</s> had taught this to <s>Kṛṣṇa Devakīputra</s>, he said:
He became free from thirst.

children.text: so 'ntavelāyām etat trayaṃ pratipadyetākṣitam asy acyutam asi prāṇasaṃśitam asīti
children.translated_text: At the final hour one should resort to these three: 'You are imperishable; you are unfailing; you are fixed in <s>prāṇa</s>.'
On this there are these two <s>ṛc</s> verses.
At first, from the ancient seed,
up beyond the darkness,
seeing the higher light,
seeing the higher heaven,

children.text: devaṃ devatrā sūryam aganma jyotir uttamam iti jyotir uttamam iti ||
children.translated_text: we have gone to the god <s>Sūrya</s> among the gods, to the highest light, to the highest light.
One should meditate on the mind as <s>Brahman</s>.
Thus with reference to the self.
Now with reference to the deities.
<s>Ākāśa</s> (space) is <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: ity ubhayam ādiṣṭaṃ bhavaty adhyātmaṃ cādhidaivataṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: Thus both have been indicated, that with reference to the self and that with reference to the deities.
That <s>Brahman</s> is four-footed.

children.text: vāk pādaḥ prāṇaḥ pādaś cakṣuḥ pādaḥ śrotraṃ pādaḥ
children.translated_text: Speech is one foot, <s>prāṇa</s> is one foot, the eye is one foot, and the ear is one foot.
Thus with reference to the self.
Now with reference to the deities.

children.text: agniḥ pādo vāyuḥ pāda ādityaḥ pādo diśaḥ pādaḥ
children.translated_text: Fire is one foot, wind is one foot, the sun is one foot, and the directions are one foot.

children.text: ity ubhayam evādiṣṭaṃ bhavaty adhyātmaṃ cādhidaivataṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: Thus both have been indicated, that with reference to the self and that with reference to the deities.
Speech indeed is the fourth foot of <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: so 'gninā jyotiṣā bhāti ca tapati ca
children.translated_text: It shines and gives heat by the light of fire.

children.text: bhāti ca tapati ca kīrtyā yaśasā brahmavarcasena ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: And it shines and burns with renown, fame, and the radiance of sacred knowledge, whoever knows thus.
Breath is indeed the fourth foot of Brahman.

children.text: sa vāyunā jyotiṣā bhāti ca tapati ca
children.translated_text: It shines and burns by wind as its light.

children.text: bhāti ca tapati ca kīrtyā yaśasā brahmavarcasena ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: It shines and burns with renown, fame, and the radiance of sacred knowledge, whoever knows thus.
The eye is indeed the fourth foot of Brahman.

children.text: sa ādityena jyotiṣā bhāti ca tapati ca
children.translated_text: It shines and burns by the sun as its light.

children.text: bhāti ca tapati ca kīrtyā yaśasā brahmavarcasena ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: It shines and burns with renown, fame, and the radiance of sacred knowledge, whoever knows thus.
The ear is indeed the fourth foot of Brahman.

children.text: sa digbhir jyotiṣā bhāti ca tapati ca
children.translated_text: It shines and burns by the directions as its light.

children.text: bhāti ca tapati ca kīrtyā yaśasā brahmavarcasena ya evaṃ veda ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: It shines and burns with renown, fame, and the radiance of sacred knowledge, whoever knows thus, whoever knows thus.
The instruction is: the sun is Brahman.
Its further explanation is this.
In the beginning this was only non-being.
That became being.
That came into being.
From that an egg came forth.
It lay for the measure of a year.
It split open.

children.text: te āṇḍakapāle rajataṃ ca suvarṇaṃ cābhavatām ||
children.translated_text: The two shells of the egg became silver and gold.
Of these, what was silver is this earth.
What was gold is the heaven.
What was the outer membrane, those are the mountains.
What was the inner membrane became cloud and mist.
What were the veins, those are the rivers.
What was the fluid in the bladder, that is the ocean.

children.text: atha yat tad ajāyata so 'sāv ādityaḥ
children.translated_text: Then what was born from it was that sun yonder.

children.text: taṃ jāyamānaṃ ghoṣā ulūlavo 'nūdatiṣṭhant sarvāṇi ca bhūtāni sarve ca kāmāḥ
children.translated_text: As it was being born, cries and ululations arose after it, and all beings and all desires arose too.

children.text: tasmāt tasyodayaṃ prati pratyāyanaṃ prati ghoṣā ulūlavo 'nūttiṣṭhanti sarvāṇi ca bhūtāni sarve ca kāmāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, at its rising and at its returning, cries and ululations arise after it, and all beings and all desires arise too.

children.text: sa ya etam evaṃ vidvān ādityaṃ brahmety upāste
children.translated_text: He who, knowing this, worships that sun as Brahman

children.text: abhyāśo ha yad enaṃ sādhavo ghoṣā ā ca gaccheyur upa ca nimreḍeran nimreḍeran ||
children.translated_text: for him it is likely that auspicious cries will come near and close upon him, close upon him.

children.text: jānaśrutir ha pautrāyaṇaḥ śraddhādeyo bahudāyī bahupākya āsa
children.translated_text: <s>Jānaśruti Pautrāyaṇa</s> was devout, generous in giving, and liberal in distributing food.

children.text: sa ha sarvata āvasathān māpayāṃcakre sarvata eva me 'nnam atsyantīti ||
children.translated_text: He had rest-houses built everywhere, thinking, 'Everywhere people will eat my food.'
Now swans flew past in the night.
Then one swan addressed another swan in this way:

children.text: ho ho 'yi bhallākṣa bhallākṣa jānaśruteḥ pautrāyaṇasya samaṃ divā jyotir ātataṃ tan mā prasāṅkṣīs tat tvāṃ mā pradhākṣīr iti ||
children.translated_text: 'Ho, ho, <s>Bhallākṣa</s>, <s>Bhallākṣa</s>! The light of <s>Jānaśruti Pautrāyaṇa</s> is spread out evenly like the sky. Do not come into contact with it, lest it burn you.'

children.text: tam u ha paraḥ pratyuvāca kam v ara enam etat santaṃ sayugvānam iva raikvam āttha iti
children.translated_text: The other replied to him, 'Who, pray, is this person whom you speak of as if he were <s>Raikva</s> with the cart?'

children.text: yo nu kathaṃ sayugvā raikva iti ||
children.translated_text: 'But who is this <s>Raikva</s> with the cart?'

children.text: yathā kṛtāya vijitāyādhareyāḥ saṃyanty evam enaṃ sarvaṃ tad abhisameti yat kiṃca prajāḥ sādhu kurvanti
children.translated_text: 'Just as, when the winning throw called <s>kṛta</s> has been won, the lower throws come together into it, so all this comes together into him, whatever good people do.

children.text: yas tad veda yat sa veda sa mayaitad ukta iti ||
children.translated_text: Whoever knows what he knows, he is such a one. That is what I have said.'

children.text: tad u ha jānaśrutiḥ pautrāyaṇa upaśuśrāva
children.translated_text: <s>Jānaśruti Pautrāyaṇa</s> overheard this.

children.text: sa ha saṃjihāna eva kṣattāram uvācāṅgāre ha sayugvānam iva raikvam āttheti
children.translated_text: Just as he was rising, he said to his chamberlain, 'Friend, you spoke as if of <s>Raikva</s> with the cart.'

children.text: yo nu kathaṃ sayugvā raikva iti ||
children.translated_text: 'But who is this <s>Raikva</s> with the cart?'

children.text: yathā kṛtāya vijitāyādhareyāḥ saṃyanty evam enaṃ sarvaṃ tad abhisameti yat kiṃca prajāḥ sādhu kurvanti
children.translated_text: 'Just as, when the winning throw called <s>kṛta</s> has been won, the lower throws come together into it, so all this comes together into him, whatever good people do.

children.text: yas tad veda yat sa veda sa mayaitad ukta iti ||
children.translated_text: Whoever knows what he knows, he is such a one. That is what I have said.'

children.text: sa ha kṣattānviṣya nāvidam iti pratyeyāya
children.translated_text: The chamberlain searched for him and came back, saying, 'I have not found him.'

children.text: taṃ hovāca yatrāre brāhmaṇasyānveṣaṇā tad enam arccheti ||
children.translated_text: He said to him, 'Where one should search for a Brahmin, there seek him.'
He approached and sat near a man below a cart, scratching his skin disease.

children.text: taṃ hābhyuvāda tvaṃ nu bhagavaḥ sayugvā raikva iti
children.translated_text: He addressed him: 'Are you, reverend sir, <s>Raikva</s> with the cart?'
'I am indeed,' he acknowledged.
The chamberlain came back, saying, 'I have found him.'

children.text: tad u ha jānaśrutiḥ pautrāyaṇaḥ ṣaṭ śatāni gavāṃ niṣkam aśvatarīrathaṃ tad ādāya praticakrame
children.translated_text: Then <s>Jānaśruti Pautrāyaṇa</s> took six hundred cows, a necklace, and a mule-drawn chariot, and went forth.
He addressed him:

children.text: raikvemāni ṣaṭ śatāni gavām ayaṃ niṣko 'yam aśvatarīrathaḥ
children.translated_text: '<s>Raikva</s>, here are six hundred cows, this necklace, and this mule-drawn chariot.

children.text: anu ma etāṃ bhagavo devatāṃ śādhi yāṃ devatām upāssa iti ||
children.translated_text: Reverend sir, teach me that deity which you worship.'

children.text: tam u ha paraḥ pratyuvācāha hāretvā śūdra tavaiva saha gobhir astv iti
children.translated_text: The other replied to him, 'Ah, take them away, śūdra; let them remain yours along with the cows.'

children.text: tad u ha punar eva jānaśrutiḥ pautrāyaṇaḥ sahasraṃ gavāṃ niṣkam aśvatarīrathaṃ duhitaraṃ tad ādāya praticakrame ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Jānaśruti Pautrāyaṇa</s> again took a thousand cows, a necklace, a mule-drawn chariot, and his daughter, and went forth.
He addressed him:

children.text: raikvedaṃ sahasraṃ gavām ayaṃ niṣko 'yam aśvatarīratha iyaṃ jāyāyaṃ grāmo yasminn āsse 'nv eva mā bhagavaḥ śādhīti ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Raikva</s>, here are a thousand cows, this necklace, this mule-drawn chariot, this wife, and this village in which you dwell. Reverend sir, please teach me.'

children.text: tasyā ha mukham upodgṛhṇann uvācājahāremāḥ śūdrānenaiva mukhenālāpayiṣyathā iti
children.translated_text: Lifting up her face, he said, 'You have brought these, śūdra; by this very face you will make me speak.'

children.text: te haite raikvaparṇā nāma mahāvṛṣeṣu yatrāsmā uvāsa
children.translated_text: These are the places called <s>Raikvaparṇa</s> among the <s>Mahāvṛṣas</s>, where he dwelt.
He said to him:
'Wind, indeed, is the absorber.

children.text: yadā vā agnir udvāyati vāyum evāpyeti
children.translated_text: When fire goes out, it goes into wind alone.
When the sun sets, it goes into wind alone.
When the moon sets, it goes into wind alone.
When the waters dry up, they go into wind alone.
For wind alone absorbs all these.
So much with reference to the deities.
Now with reference to the self.
Breath, indeed, is the absorber.

children.text: sa yadā svapiti prāṇam eva vāg apyeti
children.translated_text: When one sleeps, speech goes into breath alone.
The eye goes into breath.
The ear goes into breath.
The mind goes into breath.

children.text: prāṇo hy evaitān sarvān saṃvṛṅkta iti ||
children.translated_text: For breath alone absorbs all these.'
These, then, are the two absorbers:
wind among the gods, and breath among the vital powers.

children.text: atha ha śaunakaṃ ca kāpeyam abhipratāriṇaṃ ca kākṣaseniṃ pariviṣyamāṇau brahmacārī bibhikṣe
children.translated_text: Then, while <s>Śaunaka Kāpeya</s> and <s>Abhipratārin Kākṣaseni</s> were being served, a brahmacārin begged for alms.
They did not give to him.
He said:

children.text: mahātmanaś caturo deva ekaḥ kaḥ sa jagāra bhuvanasya gopāḥ
children.translated_text: The one god has swallowed the four great-souled ones. Who is he, the guardian of the world, who has awakened?

children.text: taṃ kāpeya nābhipaśyanti martyā abhipratārin bahudhā vasantam
children.translated_text: O <s>Kāpeya</s>, mortals do not perceive him, O <s>Abhipratārin</s>, though he dwells in many forms.

children.text: yasmai vā etad annaṃ tasmā etan na dattam iti ||
children.translated_text: The food has not been given to the one to whom this food belongs.

children.text: tad u ha śaunakaḥ kāpeyaḥ pratimanvānaḥ pratyeyāya
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śaunaka Kāpeya</s>, reflecting on it, understood and replied:

children.text: ātmā devānāṃ janitā prajānāṃ hiraṇyadaṃṣṭro babhaso 'nasūriḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>ātman</s> (self) is the begetter of the gods and of creatures, golden-toothed, a devourer, without an enemy.

children.text: mahāntam asya mahimānam āhur anadyamāno yad anannam atti
children.translated_text: They speak of this great greatness of his: not being eaten, he eats what is uneaten.

children.text: iti vai vayam brahmacārin nedam upāsmahe dattāsmai bhikṣām iti ||
children.translated_text: In this way, brahmacārin, we meditate on this. Give alms to him.
So they gave to him.

children.text: te vā ete pañcānye pañcānye daśa santas tat kṛtam
children.translated_text: Now these are five and another five; being ten, that is the <s>kṛta</s>.

children.text: tasmāt sarvāsu dikṣv annam eva daśa kṛtam
children.translated_text: Therefore in all directions food itself is the tenfold <s>kṛta</s>.
This is the <s>Virāj</s>, the eater of food.
Through her all this is seen.

children.text: sarvam asya idaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ bhavaty annādo bhavati ya evaṃ veda ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: All this becomes seen by him; he becomes an eater of food, the one who knows this in this way, the one who knows this in this way.

children.text: satyakāmo ha jābālo jabālāṃ mātaram āmantrayāṃcakre
children.translated_text: <s>Satyakāma Jābāla</s> addressed his mother <s>Jabālā</s>:

children.text: brahmacaryaṃ bhavati vivatsyāmi kiṃgotro nv aham asmīti ||
children.translated_text: Madam, I wish to live as a brahmacārin. Of what <s>gotra</s> (lineage) am I?
She said to him:

children.text: nāham etad veda tāta yadgotras tvam asi
children.translated_text: I do not know this, dear, of what <s>gotra</s> you are.

children.text: bahv aham carantī paricāriṇī yauvane tvām alabhe
children.translated_text: In my youth, while moving about much as a serving woman, I obtained you.

children.text: sāham etan na veda yadgotras tvam asi
children.translated_text: So I do not know this, of what <s>gotra</s> you are.
But my name is <s>Jabālā</s>.
Your name is <s>Satyakāma</s>.

children.text: sa satyakāma eva jābālo bruvīthā iti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore you should say, 'I am <s>Satyakāma Jābāla</s>.'
He went to <s>Gautama Hāridrumata</s> and said:
Venerable sir, I wish to live as a brahmacārin.
May I approach the venerable one as a student.
He said to him, 'Of what <s>gotra</s> are you, dear one?'
He said:

children.text: nāham etad veda bho yadgotro 'ham asmi
children.translated_text: Sir, I do not know this, of what <s>gotra</s> I am.
I asked my mother.

children.text: sā mā pratyabravīd bahv aham carantī paricāriṇī yauvane tvām alabhe
children.translated_text: She answered me, 'In my youth, while moving about much as a serving woman, I obtained you.

children.text: sāham etan na veda yadgotras tvam asi
children.translated_text: So I do not know this, of what <s>gotra</s> you are.
But my name is <s>Jabālā</s>.
Your name is <s>Satyakāma</s>.'
Thus, sir, I am <s>Satyakāma Jābāla</s>.
He said to him:
No one who is not a brahmin could declare this.
Bring fuel, dear one.

children.text: upa tvā neṣye na satyād agā iti
children.translated_text: I shall initiate you; you have not departed from truth.

children.text: tam upanīya kṛśānām abalānāṃ catuḥśatā gā nirākṛtya uvācemāḥ somyānusaṃvrajeti
children.translated_text: After initiating him, he set apart four hundred lean, weak cows and said, 'Follow these, dear one.'
As he drove them away, he said:
I will not return with fewer than a thousand.
He stayed away for a number of years.
When they had become a thousand,
then a bull addressed him, 'Satyakāma!'
'Venerable one,' he answered.
Dear one, we have reached a thousand.
Take us to the teacher's household.

children.text: brahmaṇaś ca te pādaṃ bravāṇi iti
children.translated_text: And I shall tell you a quarter of <s>brahman</s>.
'May the venerable one tell me,' he said.
It said to him:
The eastern direction is one part.
The western direction is one part.
The southern direction is one part.
The northern direction is one part.

children.text: eṣa vai somya catuṣkalaḥ pādo brahmaṇaḥ prakāśavān nāma ||
children.translated_text: This, dear one, is the four-part quarter of <s>brahman</s> called <s>Prakāśavān</s> (luminous).

children.text: sa ya etam evaṃ vidvāṃś catuṣkalaṃ pādaṃ brahmaṇaḥ prakāśavān ity upāste prakāśavān asmiṃl loke bhavati
children.translated_text: The one who, knowing this in this way, meditates on this four-part quarter of <s>brahman</s> as <s>Prakāśavān</s> becomes luminous in this world.

children.text: prakāśavato ha lokāñ jayati ya etam evaṃ vidvāṃś catuṣkalaṃ pādaṃ brahmaṇaḥ prakāśavān ity upāste ||
children.translated_text: The one who, knowing this in this way, meditates on this four-part quarter of <s>brahman</s> as <s>Prakāśavān</s> wins luminous worlds.
Fire will tell you a quarter.

children.text: sa ha śvo bhūte gā abhiprasthāpayāṃcakāra
children.translated_text: On the next day he drove the cows onward.

children.text: tā yatrābhisāyaṃ babhūvus tatrāgnim upasamādhāya gā uparudhya samidham ādhāya paścād agneḥ prāṅ upopaviveśa ||
children.translated_text: Where they came together toward evening, there he laid the fire, penned the cows, placed fuel on the fire, and sat down behind the fire facing east.
Fire addressed him, 'Satyakāma!'
'Venerable one,' he answered.
Dear one, I shall tell you a quarter of <s>brahman</s>.
'May the venerable one tell me,' he said.
It said to him:
The earth is one part.
The midspace is one part.
Heaven is one part.
The ocean is one part.

children.text: eṣa vai somya catuṣkalaḥ pādo brahmaṇo 'nantavān nāma ||
children.translated_text: This, dear one, is the four-part quarter of <s>brahman</s> called <s>Anantavān</s> (endless).

children.text: sa ya etam evaṃ vidvāṃś catuṣkalaṃ pādaṃ brahmaṇo 'nantavān ity upāste 'nantavān asmiṃl loke bhavati
children.translated_text: The one who, knowing this in this way, meditates on this four-part quarter of <s>brahman</s> as <s>Anantavān</s> becomes endless in this world.

children.text: anantavato ha lokāñ jayati ya etam evaṃ vidvāṃś catuṣkalaṃ pādaṃ brahmaṇo 'nantavān ity upāste ||
children.translated_text: The one who, knowing this in this way, meditates on this four-part quarter of <s>brahman</s> as <s>Anantavān</s> wins endless worlds.
Dear one, I shall tell you a quarter of <s>brahman</s>.
'May the venerable one tell me,' he said.
It said to him:
Fire is one part.
The sun is one part.
The moon is one part.
Lightning is one part.

children.text: eṣa vai somya catuṣkalaḥ pādo brahmaṇo jyotiṣmān nāma ||
children.translated_text: This, dear one, is the four-part quarter of <s>brahman</s> called <s>Jyotiṣmān</s> (shining).

children.text: sa ya etam evaṃ vidvāṃś catuṣkalaṃ pādaṃ brahmaṇo jyotiṣmān ity upāste jyotiṣmān asmiṃl loke bhavati
children.translated_text: The one who, knowing this in this way, meditates on this four-part quarter of <s>brahman</s> as <s>Jyotiṣmān</s> becomes shining in this world.

children.text: jyotiṣmato ha lokāñ jayati ya etam evaṃ vidvāṃś catuṣkalaṃ pādaṃ brahmaṇo jyotiṣmān ity upāste ||
children.translated_text: The one who, knowing this in this way, meditates on this four-part quarter of <s>brahman</s> as <s>Jyotiṣmān</s> wins shining worlds.
A water bird will tell you a quarter.

children.text: sa ha śvo bhūte gā abhiprasthāpayāṃcakāra
children.translated_text: On the next day he drove the cows onward.

children.text: tā yatrābhisāyaṃ babhūvus tatrāgnim upasamādhāya gā uparudhya samidham ādhāya paścād agneḥ prāṅ upopaviveśa ||
children.translated_text: Where they came together toward evening, there he laid the fire, penned the cows, placed fuel on the fire, and sat down behind the fire facing east.
A water bird, flying down to him, addressed him, 'Satyakāma!'
'Venerable one,' he answered.
Dear one, I shall tell you a quarter of <s>brahman</s>.
"May the revered sir tell me," he said.
To him he said:
"<s>Prāṇa</s> is one part;
the eye is one part;
the ear is one part;
the mind is one part.

children.text: eṣa vai somya catuṣkalaḥ pādo brahmaṇa āyatanavān nāma ||
children.translated_text: This, dear one, is the four-part quarter of <s>brahman</s> called 'possessing a support.'

children.text: sa ya etam evaṃ vidvāṃś catuṣkalaṃ pādaṃ brahmaṇa āyatanavān ity upāsta āyatanavān asmiṃl loke bhavati
children.translated_text: The one who, knowing this in this way, meditates on this four-part quarter of <s>brahman</s> as 'possessing a support' becomes possessed of a support in this world.

children.text: āyatanavato ha lokāñ jayati ya etam evaṃ vidvāṃś catuṣkalaṃ pādaṃ brahmaṇa āyatanavān ity upāste ||
children.translated_text: The one who, knowing this in this way, meditates on this four-part quarter of <s>brahman</s> as 'possessing a support' wins worlds possessed of support."
He then reached the teacher's household.
The teacher called out to him, "<s>Satyakāma</s>!"
"Revered sir," he replied.
"Dear one, you shine like a knower of <s>brahman</s>.
Who, then, instructed you?"
"Others than human beings," he acknowledged.

children.text: bhagavāṃs tv eva me kāme brūyāt ||
children.translated_text: "But let the revered sir himself tell me what I desire.

children.text: śrutaṃ hy eva me bhagavaddṛśebhya ācāryāddhaiva vidyā viditā sādhiṣṭhaṃ prāpatīti
children.translated_text: For I have heard from those like your honor that knowledge learned from a teacher reaches its highest good."
So he taught him this very same thing.

children.text: atra ha na kiṃcana vīyāyeti vīyāyeti ||
children.translated_text: Here, indeed, nothing at all was lacking, nothing was lacking.

children.text: upakosalo ha vai kāmalāyanaḥ satyakāme jābāle brahmacaryam uvāsa
children.translated_text: Now <s>Upakosala Kāmalāyana</s> lived as a celibate student with <s>Satyakāma Jābāla</s>.

children.text: tasya ha dvādaśa vārṣāny agnīn paricacāra
children.translated_text: For twelve years he tended his fires.

children.text: sa ha smānyān antevāsinaḥ samāvartayaṃs taṃ ha smaiva na samāvartayati ||
children.translated_text: When the teacher was sending the other pupils home after completion of study, he alone he did not send home.

children.text: taṃ jāyovāca tapto brahmacārī kuśalam agnīn paricacārīt
children.translated_text: The teacher's wife said to him, "This celibate student, worn by austerity, has tended the fires well.
May the fires not speak against you.
Teach him."
But without teaching him, he went away on a journey.
Because of distress he resolved not to eat.
The teacher's wife said to him, "Student, eat.
Why do you not eat?"

children.text: sa ha uvāca bahava ime 'smin puruṣe kāmā nānātyāyāḥ
children.translated_text: He said, "Many desires, going in many directions, are in this person.
I am filled with afflictions.
I shall not eat."
Then the fires spoke among themselves:
"This celibate student, worn by austerity, has tended us well.
Come, let us teach him." They said to him:

children.text: prāṇo brahma kaṃ brahma khaṃ brahmeti ||
children.translated_text: "<s>Prāṇa</s> is <s>brahman</s>; joy is <s>brahman</s>; space is <s>brahman</s>."
He said:
"I understand that <s>prāṇa</s> is <s>brahman</s>,

children.text: kaṃ ca tu khaṃ ca na vijānāmīti
children.translated_text: but I do not understand joy and space."
They said:

children.text: yad vāva kaṃ tad eva kham
children.translated_text: "What joy is, that indeed is space;

children.text: yad eva khaṃ tad eva kam iti
children.translated_text: what space is, that indeed is joy."

children.text: prāṇaṃ ca hāsmai tad ākāśaṃ cocuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus they taught him <s>prāṇa</s> and space.

children.text: atha hainaṃ gārhapatyo 'nuśaśāsa pṛthivy agnir annam āditya iti
children.translated_text: Then the <s>gārhapatya</s> fire instructed him: "Earth, fire, food, and the sun.

children.text: ya eṣa āditye puruṣo dṛśyate so 'ham asmi sa eva aham asmi iti ||
children.translated_text: The person who is seen in the sun, I am he; I myself am that one."

children.text: sa ya etam evaṃ vidvān upāste
children.translated_text: The one who, knowing this in this way, meditates on it
strikes away evil action.
He becomes possessed of a world.
He attains the full length of life.
He lives long.
His descendants do not perish.

children.text: upa vayaṃ taṃ bhuñjāmo 'smiṃś ca loke 'muṣmiṃś ca
children.translated_text: We sustain him in this world and in the next,
the one who, knowing this in this way, meditates on it.

children.text: atha ha enam anvāhāryapacano 'nuśaśāsa āpo diśo nakṣatrāṇi candramā iti
children.translated_text: Then the <s>anvāhāryapacana</s> fire instructed him: "The waters, the directions, the stars, and the moon.

children.text: ya eṣa candramasi puruṣo dṛśyate so 'ham asmi sa eva aham asmi iti ||
children.translated_text: The person who is seen in the moon, I am he; I myself am that one."

children.text: sa ya etam evaṃ vidvān upāste
children.translated_text: The one who, knowing this in this way, meditates on it
strikes away evil action.
He becomes possessed of a world.
He attains the full length of life.
He lives long.
His descendants do not perish.

children.text: upa vayaṃ taṃ bhuñjāmo 'smiṃś ca loke 'muṣmiṃś ca
children.translated_text: We sustain him in this world and in the next,
the one who, knowing this in this way, meditates on it.

children.text: atha hainam āhavanīyo 'nuśaśāsa prāṇa ākāśo dyaur vidyud iti
children.translated_text: Then the <s>āhavanīya</s> fire instructed him: "<s>Prāṇa</s>, space, heaven, and lightning.

children.text: ya eṣa vidyuti puruṣo dṛśyate so 'ham asmi sa evāham asmīti ||
children.translated_text: The person who is seen in lightning, I am he; I myself am that one."

children.text: sa ya etam evaṃ vidvān upāste
children.translated_text: The one who, knowing this in this way, meditates on it
strikes away evil action.
He becomes possessed of a world.
He attains the full length of life.
He lives long.
His descendants do not perish.

children.text: upa vayaṃ taṃ bhuñjāmo 'smiṃś ca loke 'muṣmiṃś ca
children.translated_text: We sustain him in this world and in the next,
the one who, knowing this in this way, meditates on it.
They said:
"<s>Upakosala</s>, dear one, this is our knowledge and the knowledge of the self for you.
But your teacher will tell you the way."
Then his teacher returned.
The teacher called out to him, "<s>Upakosala</s>!"
"Revered sir," he replied.
"Dear one, your face shines like that of a knower of <s>brahman</s>.
Who, then, instructed you?"

children.text: ko nu mānuśiśyād bho itīhāpeva nihnute
children.translated_text: "Who would have instructed me, sir?" he said, as if concealing it.

children.text: ime nūnam īdṛśā anyādṛśā itīhāgnīn abhyūde
children.translated_text: "These fires, surely, were formerly of one appearance and now are of another," he said, pointing to the fires.
"What, then, dear one, did they tell you?"
"This," he acknowledged.
"Dear one, they apparently told you about the worlds.

children.text: ahaṃ tu te tad vakṣyāmi yathā puṣkarapalāśa āpo na śliṣyanta evam evaṃvidi pāpaṃ karma na śliṣyata iti
children.translated_text: But I shall tell you this: just as water does not cling to a lotus leaf, so evil action does not cling to one who knows in this way."
"May the revered sir tell me," he said.
To him he said:

children.text: ya eṣo 'kṣiṇi puruṣo dṛśyata eṣa ātmeti hovāca
children.translated_text: "This person who is seen in the eye: he is the <s>ātman</s> (self)," he said.
"This is the immortal, the fearless; this is <s>brahman</s>.

children.text: tad yady apy asmin sarpir vodakaṃ vā siñcati vartmanī eva gacchati ||
children.translated_text: Even if one pours ghee or water into this eye, it goes only to the eyelashes.
They call this one <s>Saṃyadvāma</s>, 'the one to whom all goods come together,'
for all desirable goods come together toward him.

children.text: sarvāṇy enaṃ vāmāny abhisaṃyanti ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: All desirable goods come together toward the one who knows this.
This very one is <s>Vāmanī</s>, 'the bearer of goods,'
for he leads all desirable goods.

children.text: sarvāṇi vāmāni nayati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: The one who knows this leads all desirable goods.
This very one is <s>Bhāmanī</s>, 'the shining one,'
for he shines in all worlds.

children.text: sarveṣu lokeṣu bhāti ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: The one who knows this shines in all worlds.

children.text: atha yad u caivāsmiñchavyaṃ kurvanti yadi ca nārciṣam evābhisaṃbhavanti
children.translated_text: Now whether they perform funeral offerings for him or not, they go to the flame.
From the flame, to the day;
from the day, to the waxing fortnight.

children.text: āpūryamāṇapakṣād yān ṣaḍ udaṅ eti māsāṃs tān
children.translated_text: from the bright fortnight to those six months during which it goes northward;
from the months to the year;
from the year to the sun;
from the sun to the moon;
from the moon to lightning.
There is a person who is not human.
He leads them to <s>brahman</s>.
This is the path of the gods, the path of <s>brahman</s>.

children.text: etena pratipadyamānā imaṃ mānavam āvartaṃ nāvartante nāvartante ||
children.translated_text: Those who proceed by it do not return to this human round; they do not return.

children.text: eṣa ha vai yajño yo 'yaṃ pavate
children.translated_text: This indeed is the sacrifice, namely this one here that purifies as it blows.

children.text: eṣa ha yann idaṃ sarvaṃ punāti
children.translated_text: For this one purifies all this.

children.text: yad eṣa yann idaṃ sarvaṃ punāti
children.translated_text: Because this one purifies all this,
therefore this itself is the sacrifice.

children.text: tasya manaś ca vāk ca vartanī ||
children.translated_text: Mind and speech are its two tracks.
Of these two, the Brahman-priest perfects one by mind;
the hotṛ, the adhvaryu, and the udgātṛ perfect the other by speech.

children.text: sa yatropākṛte prātaranuvāke purā paridhānīyāyā brahmā vyavavadati ||
children.translated_text: When, after the morning recitation has been begun and before the closing verse, the Brahman-priest speaks out,
he perfects only one of the two tracks;
the other is left deficient.

children.text: sa yathaikapād vrajan ratho vaikena cakreṇa vartamāno riṣyaty evam asya yajño riṣyati
children.translated_text: Just as a one-footed man walking, or a chariot moving on one wheel, surely comes to grief, so his sacrifice comes to grief.
When the sacrifice comes to grief, the sacrificer comes to grief after it.
Having sacrificed, he becomes worse off.

children.text: atha yatra upākṛte prātaranuvāke na purā paridhānīyāyā brahmā vyavavadaty ubhe eva vartanī saṃskurvanti
children.translated_text: But when, after the morning recitation has been begun, the Brahman-priest does not speak out before the closing verse, both tracks are perfected.
Neither of the two is left deficient.

children.text: sa yathobhayapād vrajan ratho vobhābhyāṃ cakrābhyāṃ vartamānaḥ pratitiṣṭhaty evam asya yajñaḥ pratitiṣṭhati yajñaṃ pratitiṣṭhantaṃ yajamāno 'nu pratitiṣṭhati
children.translated_text: Just as a man walking on both feet, or a chariot moving on both wheels, stands firm, so his sacrifice stands firm; when the sacrifice stands firm, the sacrificer stands firm after it.
Having sacrificed, he becomes better off.
<s>Prajāpati</s> brooded with heat over the worlds.
From them, as they were being heated, he drew out their essences:
fire from the earth,
wind from the midspace,
and the sun from heaven.
He brooded with heat over these three deities.
From them, as they were being heated, he drew out their essences:
the Ṛg-verses from fire,
the Yajus-formulas from wind,
and the Sāmans from the sun.
He brooded with heat over this threefold knowledge.
From it, as it was being heated, he drew out its essences:
'bhūr' from the Ṛg-verses,
'bhuvar' from the Yajus-formulas,
and 'svar' from the Sāmans.

children.text: tad yady ṛkto riṣyed bhūḥ svāheti gārhapatye juhuyāt
children.translated_text: So if the sacrifice should be damaged on the Ṛg side, he should offer in the gārhapatya fire with, 'bhūḥ, svāhā.'

children.text: ṛcām eva tadrasenarcāṃ vīryeṇarcāṃ yajñasya viriṣṭaṃ saṃdadhāti ||
children.translated_text: With the very essence of the Ṛg-verses, with the vigor of the Ṛg-verses, he joins together what is damaged in the sacrifice on the Ṛg side.

children.text: atha yadi yajuṣṭo riṣyed bhuvaḥ svāheti dakṣiṇāgnau juhuyāt
children.translated_text: Then, if it should be damaged on the Yajus side, he should offer in the southern fire with, 'bhuvaḥ, svāhā.'

children.text: yajuṣām eva tadrasena yajuṣāṃ vīryeṇa yajuṣāṃ yajñasya viriṣṭaṃ saṃdadhāti ||
children.translated_text: With the very essence of the Yajus-formulas, with the vigor of the Yajus-formulas, he joins together what is damaged in the sacrifice on the Yajus side.

children.text: atha yadi sāmato riṣyet svaḥ svāhety āhavanīye juhuyāt
children.translated_text: Then, if it should be damaged on the Sāman side, he should offer in the āhavanīya fire with, 'svaḥ, svāhā.'

children.text: sāmnām eva tadrasena sāmnāṃ vīryeṇa sāmnāṃ yajñasya viriṣṭaṃ saṃdadhāti ||
children.translated_text: With the very essence of the Sāmans, with the vigor of the Sāmans, he joins together what is damaged in the sacrifice on the Sāman side.
That is like joining gold with salt as a flux,

children.text: suvarṇena rajataṃ rajatena trapu trapuṇā sīsaṃ sīsena lohaṃ lohena dāru dāru carmaṇā ||
children.translated_text: silver with gold, tin with silver, lead with tin, iron with lead, wood with iron, and wood with leather.

children.text: evam eṣāṃ lokānām āsāṃ devatānām asyās trayyā vidyāyā vīryeṇa yajñasya viriṣṭaṃ saṃdadhāti
children.translated_text: In just this way, through the vigor of these worlds, of these deities, and of this threefold knowledge, he joins together what is damaged in the sacrifice.

children.text: bheṣajakṛto ha vā eṣa yajño yatraivaṃvid brahmā bhavati ||
children.translated_text: The sacrifice is indeed made healed where the Brahman-priest is one who knows in this way.

children.text: eṣa ha vā udakpravaṇo yajño yatraivaṃvid brahmā bhavati
children.translated_text: The sacrifice is indeed sloping northward where the Brahman-priest is one who knows in this way.

children.text: evaṃvidaṃ ha vā eṣā brahmāṇam anu gāthā
children.translated_text: There is a verse about a Brahman-priest who knows in this way:

children.text: yato yata āvartate tat tad gacchati ||
children.translated_text: Wherever and wherever he turns, there and there he goes,
the human being.
The Brahman-priest alone, as the single priest, protects the <s>Kurus</s> and the horses.

children.text: evaṃviddha vai brahmā yajñaṃ yajamānaṃ sarvāṃś cartvijo 'bhirakṣati
children.translated_text: Just so, a Brahman-priest who knows in this way protects the sacrifice, the sacrificer, and all the priests.

children.text: tasmād evaṃvidam eva brahmāṇaṃ kurvīta nānevaṃvidaṃ nānevaṃvidam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore one should appoint only such a knowing Brahman-priest, not one who does not know in this way, not one who does not know in this way.

children.text: yo ha vai jyeṣṭhaṃ ca śreṣṭhaṃ ca veda jyeṣṭhaś ca ha vai śreṣṭhaś ca bhavati
children.translated_text: The one who knows the eldest and the best becomes eldest and best.

children.text: prāṇo vāva jyeṣṭhaś ca śreṣṭhaś ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Prāṇa</s> is indeed the eldest and the best.

children.text: yo ha vai vasiṣṭhaṃ veda vasiṣṭho ha svānāṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: The one who knows the most excellent becomes most excellent among his own people.
Speech is indeed the most excellent.

children.text: yo ha vai pratiṣṭhāṃ veda prati ha tiṣṭhaty asmiṃś ca loke 'muṣmiṃś ca
children.translated_text: The one who knows the foundation stands firm in this world and in the other world.
The eye is indeed the foundation.

children.text: yo ha vai saṃpadaṃ veda saṃ hāsmai kāmāḥ padyante daivāś ca mānuṣāś ca
children.translated_text: The one who knows prosperity has desires, both divine and human, come together for him.
The ear is indeed prosperity.

children.text: yo ha vā āyatanaṃ vedāyatanaṃ ha svānāṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: The one who knows the abode becomes the abode of his own people.
The mind is indeed the abode.
Then the vital faculties quarreled over who was superior.

children.text: ahaṃ śreyān asmy ahaṃ śreyān asmīti ||
children.translated_text: 'I am better; I am better,' each said.

children.text: te ha prāṇāḥ prajāpatiṃ pitaram etyocuḥ bhagavan ko naḥ śreṣṭha iti
children.translated_text: Those vital faculties went to their father <s>Prajāpati</s> and said, 'Blessed one, which of us is the best?'
He said to them:

children.text: yasmin va utkrānte śarīraṃ pāpiṣṭhataram iva dṛśyeta sa vaḥ śreṣṭha iti ||
children.translated_text: 'The one of you on whose departure the body would appear as if in the worst condition, that one is the best among you.'
Then speech departed.
After staying away for a year, it returned and said,
'How were you able to live without me?'

children.text: yathā kalā avadantaḥ prāṇantaḥ prāṇena paśyantaś cakṣuṣā śṛṇvantaḥ śrotreṇa dhyāyanto manasaivam iti
children.translated_text: 'Like mute people, not speaking, breathing with <s>prāṇa</s>, seeing with the eye, hearing with the ear, and thinking with the mind; just so,' they said.
Then speech entered back in.
Then the eye departed.
After staying away for a year, it returned and said,
'How were you able to live without me?'

children.text: yathāndhā apaśyantaḥ prāṇantaḥ prāṇena vadanto vācā śṛṇvantaḥ śrotreṇa dhyāyanto manasaivam iti
children.translated_text: 'Like blind people, not seeing, breathing with <s>prāṇa</s>, speaking with speech, hearing with the ear, and thinking with the mind; just so,' they said.
Then the eye entered back in.
Then the ear departed.

children.text: tat saṃvatsaraṃ proṣya paryetyovāca katham aśakatarte maj jīvitum iti
children.translated_text: Then, after being away for a year, he returned and said, 'How were you able to live without me?'

children.text: yathā badhirā aśṛṇvantaḥ prāṇantaḥ prāṇena vadanto vācā paśyantaś cakṣuṣā dhyāyanto manasaivam iti
children.translated_text: 'As deaf people, not hearing, still breathe with breath, speak with speech, see with the eye, and think with the mind, so we lived.'
Then hearing entered back in.
The mind went out.
After being away for a year, it returned and said,
'How were you able to live without me?'

children.text: yathā bālā amanasaḥ prāṇantaḥ prāṇena vadanto vācā paśyantaś cakṣuṣā śṛṇvantaḥ śrotreṇaivam iti
children.translated_text: 'As children, without full use of mind, still breathe with breath, speak with speech, see with the eye, and hear with hearing, so we lived.'
Then the mind entered back in.

children.text: atha ha prāṇa uccikramiṣan sa yathā suhayaḥ paḍvīśaśaṅkūn saṃkhided evam itarān prāṇān samakhidat
children.translated_text: Then, when <s>prāṇa</s> was about to go out, just as a fine horse might tear up the pegs of its tether, so it tore up the other vital powers.
They gathered around him and said,
'Reverend sir, remain.
You are the best among us.
Do not depart.'
Then speech said to him,
'Insofar as I am the most excellent, you are that most excellent one.'
Then the eye said to him,
'Insofar as I am the foundation, you are that foundation.'
Then hearing said to him,

children.text: yad ahaṃ saṃpad asmi tvaṃ tatsaṃpad asīti
children.translated_text: 'Insofar as I am prosperity, you are that prosperity.'
Then the mind said to him,

children.text: yad aham āyatanam asmi tvaṃ tadāyatanam asīti ||
children.translated_text: 'Insofar as I am the abode, you are that abode.'

children.text: na vai vāco na cakṣūṃṣi na śrotrāṇi na manāṃsīty ācakṣate
children.translated_text: Indeed, people do not call them speeches, or eyes, or ears, or minds.
They call them simply <s>prāṇas</s> (vital powers).
For <s>prāṇa</s> itself becomes all these.
He said, 'What will be my food?'

children.text: yat kiṃcid idam ā śvabhya ā śakunibhya iti hocuḥ
children.translated_text: They said, 'Whatever there is here, even down to dogs and birds.'
That, indeed, is the food of <s>ana</s> (breath).
For <s>ana</s> is plainly its name.

children.text: na ha vā evaṃvidi kiṃcanānannaṃ bhavatīti ||
children.translated_text: For one who knows this, nothing at all is not food.

children.text: sa hovāca kiṃ me vāso bhaviṣyatīti
children.translated_text: He said, 'What will be my garment?'
They said, 'Water.'

children.text: tasmād vā etad aśiṣyantaḥ purastāc copariṣṭāc cādbhiḥ paridadhati
children.translated_text: Therefore, when people are about to eat, they surround it with water before and after.
A garment is thereby obtained for him.
He is not naked.
This very teaching <s>Satyakāma Jābāla</s> told to <s>Gośruti Vaiyāghrapadya</s>, and then said,

children.text: yady apy enac chuṣkāya sthāṇave brūyāj jāyerann evāsmiñchākhāḥ praroheyuḥ palāśānīti ||
children.translated_text: 'Even if one were to tell this to a dry stump, branches would arise on it and leaves would sprout.'

children.text: atha yadi mahaj jigamiṣet amāvāsyāyām dīkṣitvā paurṇamāsyāṃ rātrau sarvauṣadhasya mantham dadhimadhunor upamathya jyeṣṭhāya śreṣṭhāya svāhety agnāv ājyasya hutvā manthe saṃpātam avanayet ||
children.translated_text: Now if one should wish to attain greatness, then, having consecrated himself on the new-moon day, on the night of the full moon he should prepare a mash of all herbs mixed with curds and honey; having offered ghee in the fire with 'Svāhā to the eldest and best,' he should pour the remainder into the mash.

children.text: vasiṣṭhāya svāhety agnāv ājyasya hutvā manthe saṃpātam avanayet
children.translated_text: Having offered ghee in the fire with 'Svāhā to the most excellent,' he should pour the remainder into the mash.

children.text: pratiṣṭhāyai svāhety agnāv ājyasya hutvā manthe saṃpātam avanayet
children.translated_text: Having offered ghee in the fire with 'Svāhā to the foundation,' he should pour the remainder into the mash.

children.text: saṃpade svāhety agnāv ājyasya hutvā manthe saṃpātam avanayet
children.translated_text: Having offered ghee in the fire with 'Svāhā to prosperity,' he should pour the remainder into the mash.

children.text: āyatanāya svāhety agnāv ājyasya hutvā manthe saṃpātam avanayet ||
children.translated_text: Having offered ghee in the fire with 'Svāhā to the abode,' he should pour the remainder into the mash.
Then, withdrawing, placing the mash in his joined hands, he mutters,
'You are named <s>amo</s>.
For all this is <s>ama</s> for you.
He indeed is the eldest, the best, the king, the overlord.

children.text: sa mā jyaiṣṭhyaṃ śraiṣṭhyaṃ rājyam ādhipatyaṃ gamayatu
children.translated_text: May he lead me to eldership, excellence, kingship, and overlordship.
May I myself become all this.'
Then, with this verse, he sips it quarter by quarter.
With 'We choose that of <s>Savitṛ</s>,' he sips.
With 'May we be the food of the god,' he sips.
With 'The best, the all-supporting,' he sips.
With 'May we meditate on the swift impulse of <s>Bhaga</s>,' he drinks it all.

children.text: nirṇijya kaṃsaṃ camasaṃ vā paścād agneḥ saṃviśati
children.translated_text: Having washed the bowl or cup, he lies down behind the fire.
He lies either on a hide or on the bare ground, restraining his speech and without carelessness.

children.text: sa yadi striyaṃ paśyet samṛddhaṃ karmeti vidyāt ||
children.translated_text: If he should see a woman, he should know, 'The rite has succeeded.'
On this there is the following verse:

children.text: yadā karmasu kāmyeṣu striyaṃ svapneṣu paśyati
children.translated_text: When, in rites performed for desires, one sees a woman in dreams,

children.text: samṛddhiṃ tatra jānīyāt tasmin svapnanidarśane tasmin svapnanidarśane ||
children.translated_text: one should know success there, in that dream-vision, in that dream-vision.
<s>Śvetaketu Hāruṇeya</s> went to the assembly of the <s>Pañcālas</s>.
<s>Pravāhaṇa Jaivali</s> said to him,
'Young man, did your father instruct you?'
'Yes, reverend sir,' he said.
'Do you know where beings go from here?'
'No, reverend sir,' he said.
'Do you know how they return again?'
'No, reverend sir,' he said.

children.text: vettha pathor devayānasya pitṛyāṇasya ca vyāvartanā 3 iti
children.translated_text: 'Do you know the separation of the two paths, the path of the gods and the path of the ancestors?'
'No, reverend sir,' he said.

children.text: vettha yathāsau loko na sampūryate 3 iti
children.translated_text: 'Do you know why that world does not become filled?'
'No, reverend sir,' he said.

children.text: vettha yathā pañcamyām āhutāv āpaḥ puruṣavacaso bhavantīti
children.translated_text: 'Do you know how, at the fifth oblation, the waters come to be called a person?'
'No indeed, reverend sir,' he said.

children.text: athānu kim anu śiṣṭho 'vocathā yo hīmāni na vidyāt
children.translated_text: 'Then why did you say that you had been instructed?
For how could someone who does not know these things say, "I have been instructed"?'
Distressed, he went to his father's place.

children.text: taṃ hovācānanuśiṣya vāva kila mā bhagavān abravīd anu tvāśiṣam iti ||
children.translated_text: He said to him, 'Without having instructed me, sir, you said, "I have instructed you."'
'A kinsman of the ruling class asked me five questions.
I was not able to explain even one of them.'

children.text: sa hovāca yathā mā tvaṃ tadaitān avado yathāham eṣāṃ naikaṃcana veda
children.translated_text: He said, 'Just as you have now told these to me, so I do not know even one of them.

children.text: yady aham imān avediṣyaṃ kathaṃ te nāvakṣyam iti ||
children.translated_text: If I had known them, how would I not have told you?'
Then <s>Gautama</s> went to the king's place.
When he arrived, the king paid him proper honor.
In the morning he came into the assembly.
The king said to him,

children.text: mānuṣasya bhagavan gautama vittasya varaṃ vṛṇīthā iti
children.translated_text: 'Reverend <s>Gautama</s>, choose a boon of human wealth.'
He said,
'Your human wealth is yours alone, O king.'

children.text: yām eva kumārasyānte vācam abhāṣathās tām eva me brūhīti
children.translated_text: "Tell me the very speech that you spoke to the boy at the end."
He became distressed.
He ordered him to stay for a long time.
He said to him:
"As you said to me, O <s>Gautama</s>,

children.text: yatheyaṃ na prāk tvattaḥ purā vidyā brāhmaṇān gacchati
children.translated_text: that this knowledge had not previously, before you, gone to the brahmins,

children.text: tasmād u sarveṣu lokeṣu kṣatrasyaiva praśāsanam abhūd iti
children.translated_text: therefore in all the worlds rulership belonged to the <s>kṣatra</s> (warrior power) alone."
He said to him:
"That world there, O <s>Gautama</s>, is indeed a fire.
Its fuel is the sun itself.
The rays are its smoke.
Day is its flame.
The moon is its coals.
The stars are its sparks.

children.text: tasminn etasminn agnau devāḥ śraddhāṃ juhvati
children.translated_text: In this fire the gods offer <s>śraddhā</s> (faith).
From that oblation King <s>Soma</s> arises.
<s>Parjanya</s>, O <s>Gautama</s>, is indeed a fire.
Its fuel is the wind itself.
The cloud is its smoke.
Lightning is its flame.
The thunderbolt is its coals.
The thunderclaps are its sparks.

children.text: tasminn etasminn agnau devāḥ somaṃ rājānaṃ juhvati
children.translated_text: In this fire the gods offer King <s>Soma</s>.
From that oblation rain arises.
The earth, O <s>Gautama</s>, is indeed a fire.
Its fuel is the year itself.
Space is its smoke.
Night is its flame.
The directions are its coals.
The intermediate directions are its sparks.

children.text: tasminn etasminn agnau devā varṣaṃ juhvati
children.translated_text: In this fire the gods offer rain.
From that oblation food arises.
A man, O <s>Gautama</s>, is indeed a fire.
His fuel is speech itself.
<s>Prāṇa</s> (vital breath) is his smoke.
The tongue is his flame.
The eye is his coals.
The ear is his sparks.

children.text: tasminn etasminn agnau devā annaṃ juhvati
children.translated_text: In this fire the gods offer food.
From that oblation semen arises.
A woman, O <s>Gautama</s>, is indeed a fire.
Her fuel is the sexual organ itself.
When he invites her, that is the smoke.
The womb is the flame.
What he does inside, those are the coals.
The pleasures are the sparks.

children.text: tasminn etasminn agnau devā reto juhvati
children.translated_text: In this fire the gods offer semen.
From that oblation an embryo arises.

children.text: iti tu pañcamyām āhutāv āpaḥ puruṣavacaso bhavantīti
children.translated_text: Thus, at the fifth oblation, the waters come to be called a person.

children.text: sa ulbāvṛto garbho daśa vā nava vā māsān antaḥ śayitvā yāvad vātha jāyate ||
children.translated_text: That embryo, enclosed in the membrane, lies within for ten months or nine months, or for as long as it does, and then it is born.
Once born, it lives for the length of its life.

children.text: taṃ pretaṃ diṣṭam ito 'gnaya eva haranti yata eveto yataḥ sambhūto bhavati ||
children.translated_text: When it has died, the fires themselves carry it from here, as ordained, to the place from which it came here, from which it arose.
Those who know this in this way,

children.text: ye ceme 'raṇye śraddhā tapa ity upāsate
children.translated_text: and those here in the forest who worship <s>śraddhā</s> (faith) and austerity,
enter into the flame.
From the flame they go to the day,
from the day to the waxing fortnight,

children.text: āpūryamāṇapakṣād yān ṣaḍ udaṅ eti māsāṃs tān ||
children.translated_text: from the waxing fortnight to the six months during which the sun goes north.
From the months they go to the year,
from the year to the sun,
from the sun to the moon,
from the moon to lightning.
There is a person there, not human.
He leads them to <s>brahman</s>.
This is the path of the gods, the <s>devayāna</s>.

children.text: atha ya ime grāma iṣṭāpūrte dattam ity upāsate
children.translated_text: But those here in the village who worship sacrifice, public works, and giving,
enter into smoke.
From smoke they go to night,
from night to the waning fortnight,

children.text: aparapakṣād yān ṣaḍ dakṣiṇaiti māsāṃs tān
children.translated_text: from the waning fortnight to the six months during which the sun goes south.
These do not reach the year.
From the months they go to the world of the fathers,
from the world of the fathers to space,
from space to the moon.
This is King <s>Soma</s>.
That is the food of the gods.
The gods consume it.

children.text: tasmin yavātsaṃpātam uṣitvāthaitam evādhvānaṃ punar nivartante
children.translated_text: After dwelling there as long as there is a remaining store, they then return again by this very path:
to space,
from space to wind.
Having become wind, one becomes smoke.
Having become smoke, one becomes cloud.
Having become cloud, one becomes a rain-cloud.
Having become a rain-cloud, one rains down.

children.text: ta iha vrīhiyavā oṣadhivanaspatayas tilamāsā iti jāyante 'to vai khalu durniṣprapataram
children.translated_text: Here they are born as rice and barley, herbs and trees, sesame and beans; from this, indeed, escape is much harder.

children.text: yo yo hy annam atti yo retaḥ siñcati tad bhūya eva bhavati ||
children.translated_text: For whichever person eats the food and emits semen, into that one he becomes again.

children.text: tad ya iha ramaṇīyacaraṇā abhyāśo ha yat te ramaṇīyāṃ yonim āpadyeran brāhmaṇayoniṃ vā kṣatriyayoniṃ vā vaiśyayoniṃ vā
children.translated_text: So those here whose conduct is pleasant are likely to enter a pleasant womb, either the womb of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, or the womb of a <s>kṣatriya</s>, or the womb of a <s>vaiśya</s>.

children.text: atha ya iha kapūyacaraṇā abhyāśo ha yat te kapūyāṃ yonim āpadyerañ śvayonim vā sūkarayoniṃ vā caṇḍālayoniṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: But those here whose conduct is foul are likely to enter a foul womb, either the womb of a dog, or the womb of a pig, or the womb of a <s>caṇḍāla</s>.

children.text: athaitayoḥ pathor na katareṇa ca na tānīmāni kṣudrāṇy asakṛdāvartīni bhūtāni bhavanti jāyasva mriyasveti
children.translated_text: But those who go by neither of these two paths become these small beings, repeatedly returning, to whom it is said, 'Be born; die.'
This is the third state.
For this reason that world is not filled up.
Therefore one should guard oneself against it.
On this there is this verse:
"The thief of gold and the drinker of liquor,
the one who lies in the teacher's bed, and the killer of a brahmin:

children.text: ete patanti catvāraḥ pañcamaś cācaraṃs tair iti ||
children.translated_text: these four fall, and as a fifth, one who associates with them."

children.text: atha ha ya etān evaṃ pañcāgnīn veda na saha tair apy ācaran pāpmanā lipyate
children.translated_text: Now one who knows these five fires in this way is not stained by evil, even if he lives among such people.

children.text: śuddhaḥ pūtaḥ puṇyaloko bhavati ya evaṃ veda ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He becomes pure, purified, and possessed of a meritorious world, the one who knows in this way, the one who knows in this way.

children.text: prācīnaśāla aupamanyavaḥ satyayajñaḥ pauluṣir indradyumno bhāllaveyo janaḥ śārkarākṣyo buḍila āśvatarāśvis te haite mahāśālā mahāśrotriyāḥ sametya mīmāṃsāṃ cakruḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Prācīnaśāla Aupamanyava</s>, <s>Satyayajña Pauluṣi</s>, <s>Indradyumna Bhāllaveya</s>, <s>Jana Śārkarākṣya</s>, and <s>Buḍila Āśvatarāśvi</s>: these great householders, great Vedic scholars, came together and held a deliberation.
"What is our <s>ātman</s>? What is <s>brahman</s>?"
They reached an agreement:

children.text: uddālako vai bhagavanto 'yam āruṇiḥ saṃpratīmam ātmānaṃ vaiśvānaram adhyeti
children.translated_text: "Venerable sirs, this <s>Uddālaka Āruṇi</s> is now studying this <s>Vaiśvānara</s> <s>ātman</s>.
Come, let us go to him."
They went to him.
He came to a conclusion:
"These great householders, great Vedic scholars, will question me.
I will not fully be able to explain it to them."
Come, I will have someone else teach us.
He said to them:

children.text: aśvapatir vai bhagavanto 'yaṃ kaikeyaḥ saṃpratīmam ātmānaṃ vaiśvānaram adhyeti
children.translated_text: This <s>Aśvapati Kaikeya</s>, revered sirs, is now studying the self as <s>Vaiśvānara</s>.
Come, let us approach him.
They approached him.

children.text: tebhyo ha prāptebhyaḥ pṛthag arhāṇi kārayāṃcakāra
children.translated_text: When they had arrived, he had honors prepared separately for them.
In the morning, as he was rising, he said:

children.text: na me steno janapade na kadaryo na madyapaḥ
children.translated_text: In my kingdom there is no thief, no miser, no drunkard.

children.text: nānāhitāgnir nāvidvān na svairī svairiṇī kutaḥ
children.translated_text: There is no one who has not established the sacred fires, no unlearned man, no libertine; how then could there be a libertine woman?
Revered sirs, I am about to perform a sacrifice.

children.text: yāvad ekaikasmā ṛtvije dhanaṃ dāsyāmi tāvad bhagavadbhyo dāsyāmi
children.translated_text: As much wealth as I shall give to each officiating priest, so much I shall give to you reverend ones.
Let the reverend ones stay.
They said:

children.text: yena haivārthena puruṣaś caret taṃ haiva vadet
children.translated_text: Whatever purpose a man comes for, that very thing he should state.
You are now studying this self as <s>Vaiśvānara</s>.
Teach that very one to us.
He said to them:
In the morning I shall answer you.
Then, in the forenoon, they came back with fuel-sticks in their hands.
Without formally initiating them as pupils, he spoke this to them.

children.text: aupamanyava kaṃ tvam ātmānam upāssa iti
children.translated_text: O <s>Aupamanyava</s>, what self do you worship?

children.text: divam eva bhagavo rājann iti hovāca
children.translated_text: He said: Heaven itself, revered king.

children.text: eṣa vai sutejā ātmā vaiśvānaro yaṃ tvam ātmānam upāsse
children.translated_text: This is indeed the self <s>Vaiśvānara</s> called <s>Sutejas</s>, which you worship as the self.

children.text: tasmāt tava sutaṃ prasutam āsutaṃ kule dṛśyate ||
children.translated_text: Therefore in your family pressed, well-pressed, and fully pressed soma is seen.
You eat food and see what is dear.

children.text: atty annaṃ paśyati priyam bhavaty asya brahmavarcasaṃ kule ye etam evam ātmānaṃ vaiśvānaram upāste
children.translated_text: He who worships this self <s>Vaiśvānara</s> in this way eats food, sees what is dear, and in his family there comes the radiance of sacred knowledge.

children.text: mūdhā tv eṣa ātmana iti hovāca
children.translated_text: But this is only the head of the self, he said.

children.text: mūrdhā te vyapatiṣyad yan māṃ nāgamiṣya iti ||
children.translated_text: Your head would have fallen off if you had not come to me.
Then he spoke to <s>Satyayajña Pauluṣi</s>:

children.text: prācīnayogya kaṃ tvam ātmānam upāssa iti
children.translated_text: O <s>Prācīnayogya</s>, what self do you worship?

children.text: ādityam eva bhagavo rājann iti hovāca
children.translated_text: He said: The sun itself, revered king.

children.text: eṣa vai viśvarūpa ātmā vaiśvānaro yaṃ tvam ātmānam upāste
children.translated_text: This is indeed the self <s>Vaiśvānara</s> called <s>Viśvarūpa</s>, which you worship as the self.

children.text: tasmāt tava bahu viśvarūpaṃ kule dṛśyate ||
children.translated_text: Therefore much manifold wealth is seen in your family.
A mule-carriage is at hand, along with maidservants and a gold necklace.
You eat food and see what is dear.

children.text: atty annaṃ paśyati priyaṃ bhavaty asya brahmavarcasaṃ kule ya etam evam ātmānaṃ vaiśvānaram upāste
children.translated_text: He who worships this self <s>Vaiśvānara</s> in this way eats food, sees what is dear, and in his family there comes the radiance of sacred knowledge.

children.text: cakṣuṣ ṭv etad ātmana iti hovāca
children.translated_text: But this is only the eye of the self, he said.
You would have become blind if you had not come to me.
Then he spoke to <s>Indradyumna Bhāllaveya</s>:

children.text: vaiyāghrapadya kaṃ tvam ātmānam upāssa iti
children.translated_text: O <s>Vaiyāghrapadya</s>, what self do you worship?

children.text: vāyum eva bhagavo rājann iti hovāca
children.translated_text: He said: Wind itself, revered king.

children.text: eṣa vai pṛthagvartmātmā vaiśvānaro yaṃ tvam ātmānam upāsse
children.translated_text: This is indeed the self <s>Vaiśvānara</s> called <s>Pṛthagvartman</s>, which you worship as the self.

children.text: tasmāt tvāṃ pṛthag balaya āyanti pṛthag rathaśreṇayo 'nuyanti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore separate tributes come to you, and separate lines of chariots follow you.
You eat food and see what is dear.

children.text: atty annaṃ paśyati priyaṃ bhavaty asya brahmavarcasaṃ kule ya etam evam ātmānaṃ vaiśvānaram upāste
children.translated_text: He who worships this self <s>Vaiśvānara</s> in this way eats food, sees what is dear, and in his family there comes the radiance of sacred knowledge.

children.text: prāṇas tv eṣa ātmana iti hovāca
children.translated_text: But this is only the breath of the self, he said.

children.text: prāṇas ta udakramiṣyad yan māṃ nāgamiṣya iti ||
children.translated_text: Your breath would have gone out if you had not come to me.
Then he spoke to <s>Jana Śārkarākṣya</s>:

children.text: śārkarākṣya kaṃ tvam ātmānam upāssa iti
children.translated_text: O <s>Śārkarākṣya</s>, what self do you worship?

children.text: ākāśam eva bhagavo rājann iti hovāca
children.translated_text: He said: Space itself, revered king.

children.text: eṣa vai bahula ātmā vaiśvānaro yaṃ tvam ātmānam upāsse
children.translated_text: This is indeed the self <s>Vaiśvānara</s> called <s>Bahula</s>, which you worship as the self.

children.text: tasmāt tvaṃ bahulo 'si prajayā ca dhanena ca ||
children.translated_text: Therefore you are abundant in offspring and in wealth.
You eat food and see what is dear.

children.text: atty annaṃ paśyati priyaṃ bhavaty asya brahmavarcasaṃ kule ya etam evam ātmānaṃ vaiśvānaram upāste
children.translated_text: He who worships this self <s>Vaiśvānara</s> in this way eats food, sees what is dear, and in his family there comes the radiance of sacred knowledge.

children.text: saṃdehas tv eṣa ātmana iti hovāca
children.translated_text: But this is only the trunk of the self, he said.

children.text: saṃdehas te vyaśīryad yan māṃ nāgamiṣya iti ||
children.translated_text: Your trunk would have fallen apart if you had not come to me.
Then he spoke to <s>Buḍila Āśvatarāśvi</s>:

children.text: vaiyāghrapadya kaṃ tvam ātmānam upāssa iti
children.translated_text: O <s>Vaiyāghrapadya</s>, what self do you worship?

children.text: apa eva bhagavo rājann iti hovāca
children.translated_text: He said: The waters themselves, revered king.

children.text: eṣa vai rayir ātmā vaiśvānaro yaṃ tvam ātmānam upāsse
children.translated_text: This is indeed the self <s>Vaiśvānara</s> called wealth, which you worship as the self.
Therefore you are wealthy and well-nourished.
You eat food and see what is dear.

children.text: atty annaṃ paśyati priyaṃ bhavaty asya brahmavarcasaṃ kule ya etam evam ātmānaṃ vaiśvānaram upāste
children.translated_text: He who worships this self <s>Vaiśvānara</s> in this way eats food, sees what is dear, and in his family there comes the radiance of sacred knowledge.

children.text: bastis tv eṣa ātmana iti hovāca
children.translated_text: But this is only the bladder of the self, he said.

children.text: bastis te vyabhetsyad yan māṃ nāgamiṣya iti ||
children.translated_text: Your bladder would have burst if you had not come to me.
Then he spoke to <s>Uddālaka Āruṇi</s>:

children.text: gautama kaṃ tvam ātmānam upāssa iti
children.translated_text: O <s>Gautama</s>, what self do you worship?

children.text: pṛthivīm eva bhagavo rājann iti hovāca
children.translated_text: He said: Earth itself, revered king.

children.text: eṣa vai pratiṣṭhātmā vaiśvānaro yaṃ tvam ātmānam upāsse
children.translated_text: This is indeed the self <s>Vaiśvānara</s> called foundation, which you worship as the self.

children.text: tasmāt tvaṃ pratiṣṭhito 'si prajayā ca paśubhiś ca ||
children.translated_text: Therefore you are firmly established in offspring and in cattle.
You eat food and see what is dear.

children.text: atty annaṃ paśyati priyaṃ bhavaty asya brahmavarcasaṃ kule ya etam evam ātmānaṃ vaiśvānaram upāste
children.translated_text: He who worships this self <s>Vaiśvānara</s> in this way eats food, sees what is dear, and in his family there comes the radiance of sacred knowledge.

children.text: pādau tv etāv ātmana iti hovāca
children.translated_text: But these are only the feet of the self, he said.

children.text: pādau te vyamlāsyetāṃ yan māṃ nāgamiṣya iti ||
children.translated_text: Your feet would have withered if you had not come to me.
He said to them:

children.text: ete vai khalu yūyaṃ pṛthag ivemam ātmānaṃ vaiśvānaraṃ vidvāṃso 'nnam attha
children.translated_text: You indeed, knowing this self <s>Vaiśvānara</s> as if separately, eat food.

children.text: yas tv etam evaṃ prādeśamātram abhivimānam ātmānaṃ vaiśvānaram upāste
children.translated_text: But whoever worships this self <s>Vaiśvānara</s> as measured by a span and as encompassing all measure,

children.text: sa sarveṣu lokeṣu sarveṣu bhūteṣu sarveṣv ātmasv annam atti ||
children.translated_text: he eats food in all worlds, in all beings, and in all selves.

children.text: tasya ha vā etasyātmano vaiśvānarasya mūrdhaiva sutejāś cakṣur viśvarūpaḥ prāṇaḥ pṛthagvartmātmā saṃdeho bahulo bastir eva rayiḥ pṛthivy eva pādāv ura eva vedir lomāṇi barhir hṛdayaṃ gārhapatyo mano 'nvāhāryapacana āsyam āhavanīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now, of this very self <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, the head is <s>Sutejas</s>, the eye is <s>Viśvarūpa</s>, the breath is <s>Pṛthagvartman</s>, the trunk is the broad mass, the bladder is indeed wealth, the feet are the earth, the chest is the altar, the hairs are the sacred grass, the heart is the gārhapatya fire, the mind is the anvāhāryapacana fire, and the mouth is the āhavanīya fire.

children.text: tad yad bhaktaṃ prathamam āgacchet taddhomīyam
children.translated_text: Therefore whatever food first comes to him is fit for offering.

children.text: sa yāṃ prathamām āhutiṃ juhuyāt tāṃ juhuyāt prāṇāya svāheti
children.translated_text: The first oblation that he offers, he should offer with, "To <s>prāṇa</s>, svāhā."
<s>Prāṇa</s> is satisfied.
When <s>prāṇa</s> is satisfied, the eye is satisfied.
When the eye is satisfied, the sun is satisfied.
When the sun is satisfied, heaven is satisfied.

children.text: divi tṛpyantyāṃ yat kiṃca dyauś cādityaś cādhitiṣṭhatas tat tṛpyati
children.translated_text: When heaven is satisfied, whatever heaven and the sun preside over is satisfied.

children.text: tasyānu tṛptiṃ tṛpyati prajayā paśubhir annādyena tejasā brahmavarcaseneti ||
children.translated_text: Following its satisfaction, he is satisfied with offspring, cattle, food and eating, splendor, and brahmanic radiance.

children.text: atha yāṃ dvitīyāṃ juhuyāt tāṃ juhuyād vyānāya svāheti
children.translated_text: Then the second oblation that he offers, he should offer with, "To <s>vyāna</s>, svāhā."
<s>Vyāna</s> is satisfied.
When <s>vyāna</s> is satisfied, the ear is satisfied.
When the ear is satisfied, the moon is satisfied.
When the moon is satisfied, the directions are satisfied.

children.text: dikṣu tṛpyantīṣu yat kiṃca diśaś candramāś cādhitiṣṭhanti tat tṛpyati
children.translated_text: When the directions are satisfied, whatever the directions and the moon preside over is satisfied.

children.text: tasyānu tṛptiṃ tṛpyati prajayā paśubhir annādyena tejasā brahmavarcaseneti ||
children.translated_text: Following its satisfaction, he is satisfied with offspring, cattle, food and eating, splendor, and brahmanic radiance.

children.text: atha yāṃ tṛtīyāṃ juhuyāt tāṃ juhuyād apānāya svāheti
children.translated_text: Then the third oblation that he offers, he should offer with, "To <s>apāna</s>, svāhā."
<s>Apāna</s> is satisfied.
When <s>apāna</s> is satisfied, speech is satisfied.
When speech is satisfied, fire is satisfied.
When fire is satisfied, the earth is satisfied.

children.text: pṛthivyāṃ tṛpyantyāṃ yat kiṃca pṛthivī cāgniś cādhitiṣṭhatas tat tṛpyati
children.translated_text: When the earth is satisfied, whatever the earth and fire preside over is satisfied.

children.text: tasyānutṛptiṃ tṛpyati prajayā paśubhir annādyena tejasā brahmavarcaseneti ||
children.translated_text: Following its satisfaction, he is satisfied with offspring, cattle, food and eating, splendor, and brahmanic radiance.

children.text: atha yāṃ caturthīṃ juhuyāt tāṃ juhuyāt samānāya svāheti
children.translated_text: Then the fourth oblation that he offers, he should offer with, "To <s>samāna</s>, svāhā."
<s>Samāna</s> is satisfied.
When <s>samāna</s> is satisfied, the mind is satisfied.
When the mind is satisfied, rain-cloud is satisfied.
When rain-cloud is satisfied, lightning is satisfied.

children.text: vidyuti tṛpyantyāṃ yat kiṃca vidyuc ca parjanyaś cādhitiṣṭhatas tat tṛpyati
children.translated_text: When lightning is satisfied, whatever lightning and rain-cloud preside over is satisfied.

children.text: tasyānu tṛptiṃ tṛpyati prajayā paśubhir annādyena tejasā brahmavarcaseneti ||
children.translated_text: Following its satisfaction, he is satisfied with offspring, cattle, food and eating, splendor, and brahmanic radiance.

children.text: atha yām pañcamīṃ juhuyāt tāṃ juhuyāt udānāya svāheti
children.translated_text: Then the fifth oblation that he offers, he should offer with, "To <s>udāna</s>, svāhā."
<s>Udāna</s> is satisfied.

children.text: udāne tṛpyati tvak tṛpyati tvaci tṛpyantyāṃ vāyus tṛpyati
children.translated_text: When <s>udāna</s> is satisfied, the skin is satisfied; when the skin is satisfied, wind is satisfied.
When wind is satisfied, space is satisfied.

children.text: ākāśe tṛpyati yat kiṃca vāyuś cākāśaś cādhitiṣṭhatas tat tṛpyati
children.translated_text: When space is satisfied, whatever wind and space preside over is satisfied.

children.text: tasyānu tṛptiṃ tṛpyati prajayā paśubhir annādyena tejasā brahmavarcaseneti ||
children.translated_text: Following its satisfaction, he is satisfied with offspring, cattle, food and eating, splendor, and brahmanic radiance.

children.text: sa ya idam avidvān agnihotraṃ juhoti yathāṅgārān apohya bhasmani juhuyāt tādṛk tat syāt ||
children.translated_text: One who offers the agnihotra without knowing this would be as if he had brushed the embers aside and offered into ashes.

children.text: atha ya etad evaṃ vidvān agnihotraṃ juhoti tasya sarveṣu lokeṣu sarveṣu bhūteṣu sarveṣv ātmasu hutaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: But one who offers the agnihotra knowing this in just this way has made an offering in all worlds, in all beings, and in all selves.

children.text: tad yatheṣīkātūlam agnau protaṃ pradūyetaivaṃ hāsya sarve pāpmānaḥ pradūyante ya etad evaṃ vidvān agnihotraṃ juhoti ||
children.translated_text: Just as the down of a reed, when thrown into fire, would be completely burned up, so all the sins of one who offers the agnihotra knowing this in just this way are completely burned up.

children.text: tasmād u haivaṃvid yady api caṇḍālāya ucchiṣṭaṃ prayacchet
children.translated_text: Therefore, even if one who knows in this way should give leftovers to a <s>Caṇḍāla</s>,

children.text: ātmani haivāsya tad vaiśvānare hutaṃ syād iti
children.translated_text: that would be offered in his own <s>Vaiśvānara</s> self.
On this there is this verse:
As hungry children here sit around their mother,
so all beings sit around the agnihotra.
<s>Śvetaketu Hāruṇeya</s> was.

children.text: taṃ ha pitovāca śvetaketo vasa brahmacaryam
children.translated_text: His father said to him, "<s>Śvetaketu</s>, live the life of a brahmacārin.

children.text: na vai somyāsmat kulīno 'nanūcya brahmabandhur iva bhavatīti ||
children.translated_text: Surely, dear one, no one born in our family becomes, while unlearned, like a mere kinsman of Brahmins."

children.text: sa ha dvādaśavarṣa upetya caturviṃśativarṣaḥ sarvān vedān adhītya mahāmanā anūcānamānī stabdha eyāya
children.translated_text: He, having gone to a teacher at twelve years old and having studied all the Vedas by the age of twenty-four, came back proud, thinking himself learned, and arrogant.
His father said to him:

children.text: śvetaketo yan nu somyedaṃ mahāmanā anūcānamānī stabdho 'si
children.translated_text: "<s>Śvetaketu</s>, since, dear one, you are proud, thinking yourself learned, and arrogant,

children.text: uta tam ādeśam aprākṣyaḥ yenāśrutaṃ śrutaṃ bhavaty amataṃ matam avijñātaṃ vijñātam iti
children.translated_text: did you ask for that instruction by which what has not been heard becomes heard, what has not been thought becomes thought, and what has not been known becomes known?"

children.text: kathaṃ nu bhagavaḥ sa ādeśo bhavatīti ||
children.translated_text: "How, venerable sir, does that instruction work?"

children.text: yathā somyaikena mṛtpiṇḍena sarvaṃ mṛnmayaṃ vijñātaṃ syāt
children.translated_text: "Just as, dear one, by a single lump of clay everything made of clay would be known,

children.text: vācārambhaṇaṃ vikāro nāmadheyaṃ mṛttikety eva satyam ||
children.translated_text: a modification is a verbal undertaking, a name; clay alone is the reality.

children.text: yathā somyaikena lohamaṇinā sarvaṃ lohamayaṃ vijñātaṃ syāt
children.translated_text: Just as, dear one, by a single piece of copper everything made of copper would be known,

children.text: vācārambhaṇaṃ vikāro nāmadheyaṃ loham ity eva satyam ||
children.translated_text: a modification is a verbal undertaking, a name; copper alone is the reality.

children.text: yathā somyaikena nakhanikṛntanena sarvaṃ kārṣṇāyasaṃ vijñātaṃ syāt
children.translated_text: Just as, dear one, by a single nail-cutter everything made of black iron would be known,

children.text: vācārambhaṇaṃ vikāro nāmadheyaṃ kṛṣṇāyasam ity eva satyam
children.translated_text: a modification is a verbal undertaking, a name; black iron alone is the reality.
In this way, dear one, that instruction works."

children.text: na vai nūnaṃ bhagavantas ta etad avediṣuḥ
children.translated_text: "Surely those venerable teachers did not know this.

children.text: yaddhy etad avediṣyan kathaṃ me nāvakṣyan
children.translated_text: For if they had known it, how could they not have told me?

children.text: iti bhagavāṃs tv eva me bravītv iti
children.translated_text: So let your venerable self tell it to me."
"So be it, dear one," he said.

children.text: sad eva somyedam agra āsīd ekam evādvitīyam
children.translated_text: "Being alone, dear one, was this in the beginning, one alone without a second.

children.text: taddhaika āhur asad evedam agra āsīd ekam evādvitīyam
children.translated_text: Some indeed say, "Non-being alone was this in the beginning, one alone without a second.
From that non-being, being was born."

children.text: kutas tu khalu somyaivaṃ syād iti hovāca
children.translated_text: But how, dear one, could it be so?" he said.
"How could being be born from non-being?

children.text: sat tv eva somyedam agra āsīd ekam evādvitīyam ||
children.translated_text: Being alone, dear one, was this in the beginning, one only, without a second.
It thought:
'May I become many; may I be born forth.'
It created fiery heat.
That fiery heat thought:
'May I become many; may I be born forth.'
It created waters.

children.text: tasmād yatra kva ca śocati svedate vā puruṣas tejasa eva tad adhy āpo jāyante ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, wherever a person becomes hot or sweats, waters are born there from fiery heat itself.
