children.text: teṣāṃ khalv eṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ trīṇy eva bījāni bhavanty āṇḍajaṃ jīvajam udbhijjam iti ||
children.translated_text: Of these beings, indeed, there are just three seeds: egg-born, live-born, and sprout-born.
This deity thought:

children.text: hantāham imās tisro devatā anena jīvenātmanānupraviśya nāmarūpe vyākaravāṇīti ||
children.translated_text: 'Come, having entered these three deities with this living self, let me differentiate name and form.'
'Let me make each one of them threefold, threefold.'

children.text: seyaṃ devatemās tisro devatā anenaiva jīvenātmanānupraviśya nāmarūpe vyākarot ||
children.translated_text: This deity, having entered these three deities with this very living self, differentiated name and form.
It made each one of them threefold, threefold.

children.text: yathā tu khalu somyemās tisro devatās trivṛt trivṛd ekaikā bhavati tan me vijānīhīti ||
children.translated_text: But how, dear one, each of these three deities becomes threefold, threefold, learn that from me.

children.text: yad agne rohitaṃ rūpaṃ tejasas tad rūpam
children.translated_text: The red appearance in fire is the appearance of fiery heat.
What is white is that of waters.
What is black is that of food.
The fireness of fire has gone away.

children.text: vācārambhaṇaṃ vikāro nāmadheyaṃ trīṇi rūpāṇīty eva satyam ||
children.translated_text: A modification is a verbal handle, a mere name; the three appearances alone are the reality.

children.text: yad ādityasya rohitaṃ rūpaṃ tejasas tad rūpam
children.translated_text: The red appearance in the sun is the appearance of fiery heat.
What is white is that of waters.
What is black is that of food.
The sunness of the sun has gone away.

children.text: vācārambhaṇaṃ vikāro nāmadheyaṃ trīṇi rūpāṇīty eva satyam ||
children.translated_text: A modification is a verbal handle, a mere name; the three appearances alone are the reality.

children.text: yac candramaso rohitaṃ rūpaṃ tejasas tad rūpam
children.translated_text: The red appearance in the moon is the appearance of fiery heat.
What is white is that of waters.
What is black is that of food.
The moonness of the moon has gone away.

children.text: vācārambhaṇaṃ vikāro nāmadheyaṃ trīṇi rūpāṇīty eva satyam ||
children.translated_text: A modification is a verbal handle, a mere name; the three appearances alone are the reality.

children.text: yad vidyuto rohitaṃ rūpaṃ tejasas tad rūpam
children.translated_text: The red appearance in lightning is the appearance of fiery heat.
What is white is that of waters.
What is black is that of food.
The lightningness of lightning has gone away.

children.text: vācārambhaṇaṃ vikāro nāmadheyaṃ trīṇi rūpāṇīty eva satyam ||
children.translated_text: A modification is a verbal handle, a mere name; the three appearances alone are the reality.

children.text: etaddha sma vai tadvidvāṃsa āhuḥ pūrve mahāśālā mahāśrotriyāḥ
children.translated_text: Former great householders and great Vedic scholars who knew this used to say:

children.text: na no 'dya kaścanāśrutam amatam avijñātam udāhariṣyati
children.translated_text: 'Today no one will bring forward to us anything unheard, unthought, or unknown.'
For they had come to know from these very things.

children.text: yad u rohitam ivābhūd iti tejasas tad rūpam iti tad vidāṃcakruḥ
children.translated_text: If something seemed red, they knew, 'That is the appearance of fiery heat.'

children.text: yad u śuklam ivābhūd ity apāṃ rūpam iti tad vidāṃcakruḥ
children.translated_text: If something seemed white, they knew, 'That is the appearance of waters.'

children.text: yad u kṛṣṇam ivābhūd ity annasya rūpam iti tad vidāṃcakruḥ ||
children.translated_text: If something seemed black, they knew, 'That is the appearance of food.'

children.text: yad v avijñātam ivābhūd ity etāsām eva devatānāṃ samāsa iti tad vidāṃcakruḥ
children.translated_text: And if something seemed unknown, they knew, 'That is a combination of just these deities.'

children.text: yathā nu khalu somyemās tisro devatāḥ puruṣaṃ prāpya trivṛt trivṛd ekaikā bhavati tan me vijānīhīti ||
children.translated_text: Now how, dear one, these three deities, having reached a person, each become threefold, threefold, learn that from me.
Food that is eaten is divided three ways.

children.text: tasya yaḥ sthaviṣṭho dhātus tat purīṣaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: Its coarsest constituent becomes feces.
The middle one becomes flesh.
The subtlest one becomes mind.
Waters that are drunk are divided three ways.

children.text: tāsāṃ yaḥ sthaviṣṭho dhātus tan mūtraṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: Their coarsest constituent becomes urine.
The middle one becomes blood.
The subtlest one becomes <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath).
Fiery heat that is consumed is divided three ways.

children.text: tasya yaḥ sthaviṣṭho dhātus tad asthi bhavati
children.translated_text: Its coarsest constituent becomes bone.
The middle one becomes marrow.
The subtlest one becomes speech.
For mind, dear one, is made of food,
<s>prāṇa</s> is made of waters,
and speech is made of fiery heat.

children.text: bhūya eva mā bhagavān vijñāpayatv iti
children.translated_text: 'May the blessed one make me understand still further,' he said.
'So be it, dear one,' he said.

children.text: dadhnaḥ somya mathyamānasya yo 'ṇimā sa ūrdhvaḥ samudīṣati
children.translated_text: Dear one, when curds are being churned, the subtle essence that rises upward
becomes butter.

children.text: evam eva khalu somyānnasyāśyamānasya yo 'ṇimā sa ūrdhvaḥ samudīṣati
children.translated_text: In just this way, dear one, when food is being eaten, the subtle essence that rises upward
becomes mind.

children.text: apāṃ somya pīyamānānāṃ yo 'ṇimā sa ūrdhvaḥ samudīṣati
children.translated_text: Dear one, when waters are being drunk, the subtle essence that rises upward
becomes <s>prāṇa</s>.

children.text: tejasaḥ somyāśyamānasya yo 'ṇimā sa ūrdhvaḥ samudīṣati
children.translated_text: Dear one, when fiery heat is being consumed, the subtle essence that rises upward
becomes speech.
For mind, dear one, is made of food,
<s>prāṇa</s> is made of waters,
and speech is made of fiery heat.

children.text: bhūya eva mā bhagavān vijñāpayatv iti
children.translated_text: 'May the blessed one make me understand still further,' he said.
'So be it, dear one,' he said.
A person, dear one, consists of sixteen parts.
For fifteen days do not eat.
Drink waters as much as you wish.

children.text: āpomayaḥ prāṇo na pibato vicchetsyata iti ||
children.translated_text: <s>Prāṇa</s>, being made of waters, will not be cut off in one who drinks.
He did not eat for fifteen days.

children.text: atha hainam upasasāda kiṃ bravīmi bho iti
children.translated_text: Then he approached him and said, 'What shall I recite, sir?'
'The Ṛg-verses, dear one, the Yajus-formulas, and the Sāmans.'

children.text: sa hovāca na vai mā pratibhānti bho iti ||
children.translated_text: He said, 'They do not come to mind for me, sir.'

children.text: taṃ hovāca yathā somya mahato 'bhyāhitasyaiko 'ṅgāraḥ khadyotamātraḥ pariśiṣṭaḥ syāt
children.translated_text: He said to him, 'Dear one, suppose from a great kindled fire a single coal, the size of a firefly, were left.
With that it would not burn much more than that.

children.text: evaṃ somya te ṣoḍaśānāṃ kalānām ekā kalā atiśiṣṭā syāt
children.translated_text: In just this way, dear one, of your sixteen parts one part would be left over.
By that, at present, you do not apprehend the Vedas.
Eat.
Then you will understand me.'
He ate.
Then he approached him.

children.text: taṃ ha yat kiṃca papraccha sarvaṃ ha pratipede ||
children.translated_text: Whatever he asked him, he grasped it all.
He said to him:

children.text: yathā somya mahato 'bhyāhitasyaikam aṅgāraṃ khadyotamātraṃ pariśiṣṭaṃ taṃ tṛṇair upasamādhāya prajvālayet tena tato 'pi bahu dahet ||
children.translated_text: 'Dear one, suppose from a great kindled fire one coal, the size of a firefly, were left, and someone were to feed it with grasses and make it blaze up; with that it would burn much more than that.

children.text: evaṃ somya te ṣoḍaśānāṃ kalānām ekā kalātiśiṣṭābhūt
children.translated_text: In just this way, dear one, of your sixteen parts one part had remained over.
Strengthened by food, it blazed up.
With that, then, you now comprehend the Vedas.
For, dear one, the mind is made of food.
The <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath) is made of water.
Speech is made of fire.
He understood this from him; he understood it.

children.text: uddālako hāruṇiḥ śvetaketuṃ putram uvāca svapnāntaṃ me somya vijānīhīti
children.translated_text: <s>Uddālaka Hāruṇi</s> said to his son <s>Śvetaketu</s>, "Dear one, understand from me the state of sleep."

children.text: yatraitat puruṣaḥ svapiti nāma satā somya tadā sampanno bhavati
children.translated_text: When this person is said to sleep, dear one, then he has become united with being.
He has gone into his own self.
Therefore they say of him, "He sleeps."
For he has gone into his own self.

children.text: sa yathā śakuniḥ sūtreṇa prabaddho diśaṃ diśaṃ patitvānyatrāyatanam alabdhvā bandhanam evopaśrayate
children.translated_text: Just as a bird tied with a cord, after flying in every direction and finding no resting place elsewhere, settles down upon its very bond,

children.text: evam eva khalu somya tan mano diśaṃ diśaṃ patitvānyatrāyatanam alabdhvā prāṇam evopaśrayate
children.translated_text: so indeed, dear one, that mind, after flying in every direction and finding no resting place elsewhere, settles down upon the <s>prāṇa</s>.
For, dear one, the mind has the <s>prāṇa</s> as its bond.
"Dear one, understand from me hunger and thirst."

children.text: yatraitat puruṣo 'śiśiṣati nāmāpa eva tad aśitaṃ nayante
children.translated_text: When this person is said to be hungry, water itself leads away what has been eaten.

children.text: tad yathā gonāyo 'śvanāyaḥ puruṣanāya ity evaṃ tad apa ācakṣate 'śanāyeti
children.translated_text: Just as they speak of a cow-leader, a horse-leader, or a man-leader, so they speak of water as "food-leader."
There, dear one, understand this shoot that has sprung up.
This will not be without a root.
Where could its root be, except in food?

children.text: evam eva khalu somyānnena śuṅgenāpo mūlam anviccha
children.translated_text: In just this way, dear one, through food as the shoot, seek water as the root.

children.text: adbhiḥ somya śuṅgena tejo mūlam anviccha
children.translated_text: Through water, dear one, as the shoot, seek fire as the root.
Through fire, dear one, as the shoot, seek being as the root.

children.text: sanmūlāḥ somyemāḥ sarvāḥ prajāḥ sadāyatanāḥ satpratiṣṭhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Dear one, all these creatures have being as their root, being as their abode, and being as their foundation.

children.text: atha yatraitat puruṣaḥ pipāsati nāma teja eva tat pītaṃ nayate
children.translated_text: And when this person is said to be thirsty, fire itself leads away what has been drunk.

children.text: tad yathā gonāyo 'śvanāyaḥ puruṣanāya ity evaṃ tat teja ācaṣṭa udanyeti
children.translated_text: Just as they speak of a cow-leader, a horse-leader, or a man-leader, so they speak of fire as "water-leader."

children.text: tatraitad eva śuṅgam utpatitaṃ somya vijānīhi
children.translated_text: There, dear one, understand this very shoot that has sprung up.
This will not be without a root.
Where could its root be, except in water?

children.text: adbhiḥ somya śuṅgena tejo mūlam anviccha
children.translated_text: Through water, dear one, as the shoot, seek fire as the root.
Through fire, dear one, as the shoot, seek being as the root.

children.text: sanmūlāḥ somyemāḥ sarvāḥ prajāḥ sadāyatanāḥ satpratiṣṭhāḥ
children.translated_text: Dear one, all these creatures have being as their root, being as their abode, and being as their foundation.

children.text: yathā nu khalu somyemās tisro devatāḥ puruṣaṃ prāpya trivṛt trivṛd ekaikā bhavati tad uktaṃ purastād eva bhavati
children.translated_text: Now, dear one, as each of these three deities, having reached a person, becomes threefold, each one threefold, that has already been stated before.

children.text: asya somya puruṣasya prayato vāṅ manasi saṃpadyate manaḥ prāṇe prāṇas tejasi tejaḥ parasyāṃ devatāyām ||
children.translated_text: Dear one, when this person is departing, speech merges into mind, mind into <s>prāṇa</s>, <s>prāṇa</s> into fire, and fire into the highest deity.

children.text: sa ya eṣo 'ṇimaitad ātmyam idaṃ sarvam
children.translated_text: That which is this subtle essence: this whole world has that as its self.
That is the real.
That is the self.
That you are, <s>Śvetaketu</s>.

children.text: bhūya eva mā bhagavān vijñāpayatv iti
children.translated_text: "May your venerable self explain it to me further."
"So be it, dear one," he said.

children.text: yathā somya madhu madhukṛto nistiṣṭhanti nānātyayānāṃ vṛkṣāṇāṃ rasān samavahāram ekatāṃ rasaṃ gamayanti ||
children.translated_text: Just as, dear one, honey-makers collect honey by gathering the juices of various trees and bringing them into unity as a single juice,

children.text: te yathā tatra na vivekaṃ labhante 'muṣyāhaṃ vṛkṣasya raso 'smy amuṣyāhaṃ vṛkṣasya raso 'smīti
children.translated_text: and just as they do not find distinction there, thinking, "I am the juice of that tree; I am the juice of that tree,"

children.text: evam eva khalu somyemāḥ sarvāḥ prajāḥ sati saṃpadya na viduḥ sati saṃpadyāmaha iti ||
children.translated_text: so indeed, dear one, all these creatures, after merging into being, do not know, "We are merging into being."

children.text: ta iha vyaghro vā siṃho vā vṛko vā varāho vā kīṭo vā pataṅgo vā daṃśo vā maśako vā yad yad bhavanti tad ābhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Whatever they are here, whether tiger, lion, wolf, boar, worm, moth, gnat, or mosquito, that they become again.

children.text: sa ya eṣo 'ṇimaitad ātmyam idaṃ sarvam
children.translated_text: That which is this subtle essence: this whole world has that as its self.
That is the real.
That is the self.
That you are, <s>Śvetaketu</s>.

children.text: bhūya eva mā bhagavān vijñāpayatv iti
children.translated_text: "May your venerable self explain it to me further."
"So be it, dear one," he said.

children.text: imāḥ somya nadyaḥ purastāt prācyaḥ syandante paścāt pratīcyaḥ
children.translated_text: These rivers, dear one, flow eastward from the east and westward from the west.
They go from the ocean into the ocean itself.
It becomes the ocean itself.

children.text: tā yathā tatra na vidur iyam aham asmīyam aham asmīti ||
children.translated_text: Just as there they do not know, "I am this one; I am that one,"

children.text: evam eva khalu somyemāḥ sarvāḥ prajāḥ sata āgamya na viduḥ sata āgacchāmaha iti
children.translated_text: so indeed, dear one, all these creatures, having come from being, do not know, "We are coming from being."

children.text: ta iha vyāghro vā siṃho vā vṛko vā varāho vā kīṭo vā pataṅgo vā daṃśo vā maśako vā yad yad bhavanti tad ābhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Whatever they are here, whether tiger, lion, wolf, boar, worm, moth, gnat, or mosquito, that they become again.

children.text: sa ya eṣo 'ṇimaitad ātmyam idaṃ sarvam
children.translated_text: That which is this subtle essence: this whole world has that as its self.
That is the real.
That is the self.
That you are, <s>Śvetaketu</s>.

children.text: bhūya eva mā bhagavān vijñāpayatv iti
children.translated_text: "May your venerable self explain it to me further."
"So be it, dear one," he said.

children.text: asya somya mahato vṛkṣasya yo mūle 'bhyāhanyāj jīvan sraved yo madhye 'bhyāhanyāj jīvan sraved yo 'gre 'bhyāhanyāj jīvan sravet
children.translated_text: Dear one, if someone were to strike this great tree at the root, it would bleed while living; if he were to strike it in the middle, it would bleed while living; if he were to strike it at the top, it would bleed while living.

children.text: sa eṣa jīvenātmanānuprabhūtaḥ pepīyamāno modamānas tiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: This tree, pervaded by the living self, stands drinking and rejoicing.

children.text: asya yad ekāṃ śākhāṃ jīvo jahāty atha sā śuṣyati
children.translated_text: If the living self leaves one of its branches, then that branch dries up.
If it leaves a second, then that one dries up.
If it leaves a third, then that one dries up.
If it leaves the whole, the whole dries up.

children.text: evam eva khalu somya viddhīti ha uvāca
children.translated_text: "In just this way, dear one, understand," he said.

children.text: jīvāpetaṃ vāva kiledaṃ mriyate na jīvo mriyata iti
children.translated_text: "This body indeed dies when bereft of life; the living self does not die."

children.text: sa ya eṣo 'ṇimaitad ātmyam idaṃ sarvam
children.translated_text: That which is this subtle essence: this whole world has that as its self.
That is the real.
That is the self.
That you are, <s>Śvetaketu</s>.

children.text: bhūya eva mā bhagavān vijñāpayatv iti
children.translated_text: "May your venerable self explain it to me further."
"So be it, dear one," he said.
"Bring a fruit of the banyan tree from there."
"Here it is, venerable sir."
"Break it."
"It is broken, venerable sir."
"What do you see in it?"
"These tiny seeds, venerable sir."
"Please break one of them."
"It is split, venerable sir," he said.
"What do you see here?"
"Nothing at all, venerable sir," he said.

children.text: taṃ hovāca yaṃ vai somyaitam aṇimānaṃ na nibhālayasa etasya vai somyaiṣo 'ṇimna evaṃ mahānyagrodhas tiṣṭhati
children.translated_text: He said to him, "That subtle essence, dear one, which you do not perceive: from that very subtle essence, dear one, this great nyagrodha tree stands.
Have faith, dear one."

children.text: sa ya eṣo 'ṇimaitad ātmyam idaṃ sarvam
children.translated_text: "That which is this subtle essence: all this has that as its self.
That is the real.
That is the self.
You are that, <s>Śvetaketu</s>," he said.

children.text: bhūya eva mā bhagavān vijñāpayatv iti
children.translated_text: "May your venerable self make me understand further, venerable sir," he said.
"So be it, dear one," he said.

children.text: lavaṇam etad udake 'vadhāyātha mā prātar upasīdathā iti
children.translated_text: "Put this salt in water, and then come to me in the morning," he said.
He did so.
He said to him:

children.text: yad doṣā lavaṇam udake 'vādhā aṅga tad āhareti
children.translated_text: "The salt that you put in the water last night, dear one, bring it here."
Having felt for it, he did not find it.
It was just as if dissolved.
"Dear one, taste from this end of it."
"How is it?"
"Salty," he said.
"Taste from the middle."
"How is it?"
"Salty," he said.
"Taste from the far end."
"How is it?"
"Salty," he said.
"Throw this away, and then come to me," he said.
He did so.
That remains there always.

children.text: taṃ hovācātra vāva kila tat somya na nibhālayase 'traiva kileti ||
children.translated_text: He said to him, "Here indeed, dear one, you do not perceive that; yet here indeed it is."

children.text: sa ya eṣo 'ṇimaitad ātmyam idaṃ sarvam
children.translated_text: "That which is this subtle essence: all this has that as its self.
That is the real.
That is the self.
You are that, <s>Śvetaketu</s>," he said.

children.text: bhūya eva mā bhagavān vijñāpayatv iti
children.translated_text: "May your venerable self make me understand further, venerable sir," he said.
"So be it, dear one," he said.

children.text: yathā somya puruṣaṃ gandhārebhyo 'bhinaddhākṣam ānīya taṃ tato 'tijane visṛjet
children.translated_text: "Just as, dear one, if someone brought a man from the <s>Gandhāras</s> with his eyes bound and released him in a deserted place,

children.text: sa yathā tatra prāṅ vodaṅ vā adharāṅ vā pratyaṅ vā pradhmāyītābhinaddhākṣa ānīto 'bhinaddhākṣo visṛṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he would cry out there toward the east, or toward the north, or toward the south, or toward the west: 'I was brought with my eyes bound; I have been released with my eyes bound.'

children.text: tasya yathābhinahanaṃ pramucya prabrūyād etāṃ diśaṃ gandhārā etāṃ diśaṃ vrajeti
children.translated_text: Just as someone might remove his blindfold and tell him, 'The <s>Gandhāras</s> are in this direction; go in this direction,'

children.text: sa grāmād grāmaṃ pṛcchan paṇḍito medhāvī gandhārān evopasaṃpadyeta
children.translated_text: and he, asking from village to village, being wise and intelligent, would reach the <s>Gandhāras</s> themselves,
so too here a person who has a teacher comes to know.

children.text: tasya tāvad eva ciraṃ yāvan na vimokṣye 'tha sampatsya iti ||
children.translated_text: For him there is only so much delay as until he is released; then he will attain."

children.text: sa ya eṣo 'ṇimaitad ātmyam idaṃ sarvam
children.translated_text: "That which is this subtle essence: all this has that as its self.
That is the real.
That is the self.
You are that, <s>Śvetaketu</s>," he said.

children.text: bhūya eva mā bhagavān vijñāpayatv iti
children.translated_text: "May your venerable self make me understand further, venerable sir," he said.
"So be it, dear one," he said.

children.text: puruṣaṃ somyotopatāpinaṃ jñātayaḥ paryupāsate jānāsi māṃ jānāsi mām iti
children.translated_text: "Dear one, relatives sit around a man who is severely ill, saying, 'Do you know me? Do you know me?'

children.text: tasya yāvan na vāṅ manasi sampadyate manaḥ prāṇe prāṇas tejasi tejaḥ parasyāṃ devatāyāṃ tāvaj jānāti ||
children.translated_text: So long as his speech has not merged into mind, mind into breath, breath into heat, and heat into the highest deity, so long he knows.

children.text: atha yadāsya vāṅ manasi sampadyate manaḥ prāṇe prāṇas tejasi tejaḥ parasyāṃ devatāyām atha na jānāti ||
children.translated_text: But when his speech has merged into mind, mind into breath, breath into heat, and heat into the highest deity, then he does not know.

children.text: sa ya eṣo 'ṇimaitad ātmyam idaṃ sarvam
children.translated_text: "That which is this subtle essence: all this has that as its self.
That is the real.
That is the self.
You are that, <s>Śvetaketu</s>," he said.

children.text: bhūya eva mā bhagavān vijñāpayatv iti
children.translated_text: "May your venerable self make me understand further, venerable sir," he said.
"So be it, dear one," he said.
"Dear one, they bring a man with his hand grasped,

children.text: apahārṣīt steyam akārṣīt paraśum asmai tapateti
children.translated_text: saying, 'He has stolen; he has committed theft. Heat the axe for him.'

children.text: sa yadi tasya kartā bhavati tata evānṛtam ātmānaṃ kurute
children.translated_text: If he is the doer of that, then by that very fact he makes himself false.
Intent on falsehood, covering himself with falsehood, he grasps the heated axe.
He is burned.
Then he is punished.
But if he is not the doer of that,
then by that very fact he makes himself true.

children.text: sa satyābhisaṃdhaḥ satyenātmānam antardhāya paraśuṃ taptaṃ pratigṛhṇāti
children.translated_text: Intent on truth, covering himself with truth, he grasps the heated axe.
He is not burned.
Then he is released.
Just as he would not be burned there,
all this has that as its self.
That is the real.
That is the self.
You are that, <s>Śvetaketu</s>," he said.
Then he understood it; he understood it indeed.

children.text: adhīhi bhagava iti hopasasāda sanatkumāraṃ nāradaḥ
children.translated_text: "Teach me, venerable sir," said <s>Nārada</s>, approaching <s>Sanatkumāra</s>.

children.text: taṃ hovāca yad vettha tena mopasīda
children.translated_text: He said to him, "Come to me with what you know.
Then I shall tell you what is beyond that."
He said:

children.text: ṛgvedaṃ bhagavo 'dhyemi yajurvedaṃ sāmavedam ātharvaṇaṃ caturtham itihāsapurāṇaṃ pañcamaṃ vedānāṃ vedaṃ pitryaṃ rāśiṃ daivaṃ nidhiṃ vākovākyam ekāyanaṃ devavidyāṃ brahmavidyāṃ bhūtavidyāṃ kṣatravidyāṃ nakṣatravidyāṃ sarpadevajanavidyām etad bhagavo 'dhyemi ||
children.translated_text: "Venerable sir, I study the <s>Ṛgveda</s>, the <s>Yajurveda</s>, the <s>Sāmaveda</s>, the <s>Ātharvaṇa</s> as the fourth, <s>Itihāsapurāṇa</s> as the fifth, the Veda of the Vedas, ancestral lore, mathematics, divine lore, treasure lore, dialogue and logic, the single path, knowledge of the gods, knowledge of <s>brahman</s>, knowledge of beings, warrior science, knowledge of the constellations, and knowledge of serpents and divine beings. This, venerable sir, I study.
So I, venerable sir, am only a knower of mantras, not a knower of the self.

children.text: śrutaṃ hy eva me bhagavaddṛśebhyas tarati śokam ātmavid iti
children.translated_text: For I have heard from men like your venerable self that one who knows the self crosses beyond sorrow.
So I, venerable sir, grieve.

children.text: taṃ mā bhagavāñchokasya pāraṃ tārayatv iti
children.translated_text: May your venerable self carry me across to the far shore of sorrow."

children.text: taṃ hovāca yad vai kiṃcaitad adhyagīṣṭhā nāmaivaitat ||
children.translated_text: He said to him, "Whatever of this you have studied is only name.

children.text: nāma vā ṛgvedo yajurvedaḥ sāmaveda ātharvaṇaś caturtha itihāsapurāṇaḥ pañcamo vedānāṃ vedaḥ pitryo rāśir daivo nidhir vākovākyam ekāyanaṃ devavidyā brahmavidyā bhūtavidyā kṣatravidyā nakṣatravidyā sarpadevajanavidyā
children.translated_text: Name, indeed, is the <s>Ṛgveda</s>, the <s>Yajurveda</s>, the <s>Sāmaveda</s>, the <s>Ātharvaṇa</s> as the fourth, <s>Itihāsapurāṇa</s> as the fifth, the Veda of the Vedas, ancestral lore, mathematics, divine lore, treasure lore, dialogue and logic, the single path, knowledge of the gods, knowledge of <s>brahman</s>, knowledge of beings, warrior science, knowledge of the constellations, and knowledge of serpents and divine beings.
All this is only name.
Meditate upon name."
One who meditates upon name as <s>brahman</s>

children.text: yāvan nāmno gataṃ tatrāsya yathākāmacāro bhavati yo nāma brahmety upāste
children.translated_text: has freedom to move as he wishes as far as name reaches, if he meditates upon name as <s>brahman</s>.
"Is there, venerable sir, something greater than name?"
"There is indeed something greater than name," he said.
"May your venerable self tell that to me," he said.
"Speech, indeed, is greater than name.

children.text: vāg vā ṛgvedaṃ vijñāpayati yajurvedaṃ sāmavedam ātharvaṇaṃ caturtham itihāsapurāṇaṃ pañcamaṃ vedānāṃ vedaṃ pitryaṃ rāśiṃ daivaṃ nidhiṃ vākovākyam ekāyanaṃ devavidyāṃ brahmavidyāṃ bhūtavidyāṃ kṣatravidyāṃ nakṣatravidyāṃ sarpadevajanavidyāṃ divaṃ ca pṛthivīṃ ca vāyuṃ cākāśaṃ cāpaś ca tejaś ca devāṃś ca manuṣyāṃś ca paśūṃś ca vayāṃsi ca tṛṇavanaspatīñ śvāpadāny ā kīṭapataṅgapipīlakaṃ dharmaṃ cādharmaṃ
children.translated_text: Speech indeed makes known the <s>Ṛgveda</s>, the <s>Yajurveda</s>, the <s>Sāmaveda</s>, the <s>Ātharvaṇa</s> as the fourth, history and ancient lore as the fifth Veda among the Vedas, ancestral lore, arithmetic, divination, treasure-lore, dialectic, the single path, knowledge of the gods, knowledge of <s>brahman</s>, knowledge of beings, knowledge of warriors, knowledge of the stars, knowledge of serpents and divine beings, heaven and earth, wind and space, waters and fire, gods and human beings, cattle and birds, grasses and forest trees, wild animals down to insects, moths, and ants, and <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>.

children.text: ca satyaṃ cānṛtaṃ ca sādhu cāsādhu ca hṛdayajñaṃ cāhṛdayajñaṃ ca
children.translated_text: And also truth and untruth, what is good and what is not good, what is known by the heart and what is not known by the heart.

children.text: yad vai vāṅ nābhaviṣyan na dharmo nādharmo vyajñāpayiṣyan na satyaṃ nānṛtaṃ na sādhu nāsādhu na hṛdayajño nāhṛdayajñaḥ
children.translated_text: If speech did not exist, it would make known neither <s>dharma</s> nor <s>adharma</s>, neither truth nor untruth, neither what is good nor what is not good, neither what is known by the heart nor what is not known by the heart.

children.text: vāg evaitat sarvaṃ vijñāpayati vācam upāssveti ||
children.translated_text: Speech alone makes all this known. Meditate on speech.
One who meditates on speech as <s>brahman</s>

children.text: yāvad vāco gataṃ tatrāsya yathākāmacāro bhavati yo vācaṃ brahmety upāste
children.translated_text: has freedom to move as he wishes as far as speech extends, he who meditates on speech as <s>brahman</s>.
"Venerable sir, is there something greater than speech?"
"There is indeed something greater than speech."
"Let your venerable self tell that to me."
Mind is indeed greater than speech.

children.text: yathā vai dve vāmalake dve vā kole dvau vākṣau muṣṭir anubhavaty evaṃ vācaṃ ca nāma ca mano 'nubhavati
children.translated_text: Just as a fist encloses two āmalakas, two kolas, or two akṣas, so the mind encloses both speech and name.

children.text: sa yadā manasā manasyati mantrān adhīyīyety athādhīte
children.translated_text: When a person thinks with the mind, "May I study the mantras," then he studies them.
When he thinks, "May I perform rites," then he performs them.
When he thinks, "May I desire sons and cattle," then he desires them.

children.text: imaṃ ca lokam amuṃ ceccheyety athecchate
children.translated_text: When he thinks, "May I desire this world and the other world," then he desires them.
For mind is the self.
Mind is the world.
Mind is <s>brahman</s>.
Meditate on mind.
One who meditates on mind as <s>brahman</s>

children.text: yāvan manaso gataṃ tatrāsya yathākāmacāro bhavati yo mano brahmety upāste
children.translated_text: has freedom to move as he wishes as far as mind extends, he who meditates on mind as <s>brahman</s>.
"Venerable sir, is there something greater than mind?"
"There is indeed something greater than mind."
"Let your venerable self tell that to me."
<s>Saṃkalpa</s> (resolve) is indeed greater than mind.
When a person resolves, then he thinks.
Then he sets speech in motion.
And he directs that speech into name.
In name, the mantras become one.
In the mantras, the rites become one.

children.text: tāni ha vā etāni saṃkalpaikāyanāni saṃkalpātmakāni saṃkalpe pratiṣṭhitāni
children.translated_text: All these are indeed rooted in <s>saṃkalpa</s>, made of <s>saṃkalpa</s>, and established in <s>saṃkalpa</s>.
Heaven and earth came into ordered resolve.
Wind and space came into ordered resolve.
Waters and fire came into ordered resolve.
Through their ordered resolve, rain is resolved.
Through the ordered resolve of rain, food is resolved.
Through the ordered resolve of food, the vital breaths are resolved.
Through the ordered resolve of the vital breaths, the mantras are resolved.
Through the ordered resolve of the mantras, rites are resolved.
Through the ordered resolve of rites, the world is resolved.
Through the ordered resolve of the world, everything is resolved.
This, then, is <s>saṃkalpa</s>.
Meditate on <s>saṃkalpa</s>.
One who meditates on <s>saṃkalpa</s> as <s>brahman</s>

children.text: kﾱptān vai sa lokān dhruvān dhruvaḥ pratiṣṭhitān pratiṣṭhito 'vyathamānān avyathamāno 'bhisidhyati
children.translated_text: surely attains worlds that are ordered, firm, established, and unshaken; being firm, established, and unshaken himself, he attains them.

children.text: yāvat saṃkalpasya gataṃ tatrāsya yathākāmacāro bhavati yaḥ saṃkalpaṃ brahmety upāste
children.translated_text: He has freedom to move as he wishes as far as <s>saṃkalpa</s> extends, he who meditates on <s>saṃkalpa</s> as <s>brahman</s>.
"Venerable sir, is there something greater than <s>saṃkalpa</s>?"
"There is indeed something greater than <s>saṃkalpa</s>."
"Let your venerable self tell that to me."
<s>Citta</s> (conscious thought) is indeed greater than <s>saṃkalpa</s>.
When a person is conscious and attentive, then he resolves.
Then he thinks.
Then he sets speech in motion.
And he directs that speech into name.
In name, the mantras become one.
In the mantras, the rites become one.

children.text: tāni ha vā etāni cittaikāyanāni cittātmāni citte pratiṣṭhitāni
children.translated_text: All these are indeed rooted in <s>citta</s>, made of <s>citta</s>, and established in <s>citta</s>.

children.text: tasmād yady api bahuvid acitto bhavati nāyam astīty evainam āhuḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, even if a man is very learned but lacks <s>citta</s>, people say of him, "This one does not really exist."

children.text: yad ayaṃ veda yad vā ayaṃ vidvān nettham acittaḥ syād iti
children.translated_text: "If what this man knows, or what this learned man knows, were otherwise, he would not be so lacking in <s>citta</s>."

children.text: atha yady alpavic cittavān bhavati tasmā evota śuśrūṣante
children.translated_text: But if someone with little learning possesses <s>citta</s>, people are eager to listen even to him.
For <s>citta</s> alone is the one path of these.
<s>Citta</s> is the self.
<s>Citta</s> is the foundation.
Meditate on <s>citta</s>.
One who meditates on <s>citta</s> as <s>brahman</s>

children.text: cittān vai sa lokān dhruvān dhruvaḥ pratiṣṭhitān pratiṣṭhito 'vyathamānān avyathamāno 'bhisidhyati
children.translated_text: surely attains worlds belonging to <s>citta</s>, firm, established, and unshaken; being firm, established, and unshaken himself, he attains them.

children.text: yāvac cittasya gataṃ tatrāsya yathākāmacāro bhavati yaś cittaṃ brahmety upāste
children.translated_text: He has freedom to move as he wishes as far as <s>citta</s> extends, he who meditates on <s>citta</s> as <s>brahman</s>.
"Venerable sir, is there something greater than <s>citta</s>?"
"There is indeed something greater than <s>citta</s>."
"Let your venerable self tell that to me."
<s>Dhyāna</s> (meditation) is indeed greater than <s>citta</s>.
The earth seems to meditate.
The atmosphere seems to meditate.
Heaven seems to meditate.
The waters seem to meditate.
The mountains seem to meditate.
Gods and human beings seem to meditate.

children.text: tasmād ya iha manuṣyāṇāṃ mahattāṃ prāpnuvanti dhyānāpādāṃśā ivaiva te bhavanti
children.translated_text: Therefore, those among human beings here who attain greatness seem to possess a share of <s>dhyāna</s>.

children.text: atha ye 'lpāḥ kalahinaḥ piśunā upavādinas te
children.translated_text: But those who are small are quarrelsome, slanderous, and abusive.

children.text: atha ye prabhavo dhyānāpādāṃśā ivaiva te bhavanti
children.translated_text: Those who are powerful, however, seem to possess a share of <s>dhyāna</s>.
Meditate on <s>dhyāna</s>.
One who meditates on <s>dhyāna</s> as <s>brahman</s>

children.text: yāvad dhyānasya gataṃ tatrāsya yathākāmacāro bhavati yo dhyānaṃ brahmety upāste
children.translated_text: has freedom to move as he wishes as far as <s>dhyāna</s> extends, he who meditates on <s>dhyāna</s> as <s>brahman</s>.
"Venerable sir, is there something greater than <s>dhyāna</s>?"
"There is indeed something greater than <s>dhyāna</s>."
May the venerable sir tell that to me.
Knowledge indeed is greater than meditation.

children.text: vijñānena vā ṛgvedaṃ vijānāti yajurvedaṃ sāmavedam ātharvaṇaṃ caturtham itihāsapurāṇaṃ pañcamaṃ vedānāṃ vedaṃ pitryaṃ rāśiṃ daivaṃ nidhiṃ vākovākyam ekāyanaṃ devavidyāṃ brahmavidyāṃ bhūtavidyāṃ kṣatravidyāṃ nakṣatravidyāṃ sarpadevajanavidyāṃ divaṃ ca pṛthivīṃ ca vāyuṃ cākāśaṃ cāpaś ca tejaś ca devāṃś ca manuṣyāṃś ca paśūṃś ca vayāṃsi ca tṛṇavanaspatīñchvāpadāny ā kīṭapataṅgapipīlakam
children.translated_text: By knowledge one knows the <s>Ṛgveda</s>, the <s>Yajurveda</s>, the <s>Sāmaveda</s>, the <s>Ātharvaṇa</s> as the fourth, <s>itihāsa-purāṇa</s> as the fifth, the Veda of the Vedas, ancestral lore, calculation, divine lore, treasure lore, dialogue, the single path, divine science, brahma-knowledge, knowledge of beings, kṣatra-knowledge, star-lore, serpent and divine-being lore, heaven and earth, wind and space, waters and fire, gods and human beings, cattle and birds, grasses and trees, wild animals down to worms, insects, flying insects, and ants.

children.text: dharmaṃ cādharmaṃ ca satyaṃ cānṛtaṃ ca sādhu cāsādhu ca hṛdayajñaṃ cāhṛdayajñaṃ cānnaṃ ca rasaṃ cemaṃ ca lokam amuṃ ca vijñānenaiva vijānāti
children.translated_text: And <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, truth and falsehood, good and bad, what is known by the heart and what is not known by the heart, food and flavor, this world and that world: by knowledge alone one knows them.
Meditate on knowledge.
One who meditates on knowledge as brahman
attains, indeed, the worlds of those possessed of knowledge and possessed of knowing.

children.text: yāvad vijñānasya gataṃ tatrāsya yathākāmacāro bhavati yo vijñānaṃ brahmety upāste
children.translated_text: As far as knowledge extends, there he has freedom to move as he wishes, he who meditates on knowledge as brahman.
Venerable sir, is there anything greater than knowledge?
There is indeed something greater than knowledge.
May the venerable sir tell that to me.
Strength indeed is greater than knowledge.

children.text: api ha śataṃ vijñānavatām eko balavān ākampayate
children.translated_text: For a single strong man can shake a hundred men of knowledge.

children.text: sa yadā balī bhavaty athotthātā bhavati
children.translated_text: When he becomes strong, then he becomes one who rises up.
Rising up, he becomes one who attends on another.
Attending, he becomes one who sits near.

children.text: upasīdan draṣṭā bhavati śrotā bhavati mantā bhavati boddhā bhavati kartā bhavati vijñātā bhavati
children.translated_text: Sitting near, he becomes a seer, a hearer, a thinker, an understander, a doer, and a knower.

children.text: balena vai pṛthivī tiṣṭhati balenāntarikṣaṃ balena dyaur balena parvatā balena devamanuṣyā balena paśavaś ca vayāṃsi ca tṛṇavanaspatayaḥ śvāpadāny ā kīṭapataṅgapipīlakam
children.translated_text: By strength the earth stands; by strength the atmosphere stands; by strength heaven stands; by strength the mountains stand; by strength gods and human beings stand, and cattle, birds, grasses and trees, wild animals down to worms, insects, flying insects, and ants.
By strength the world stands.
Meditate on strength.
One who meditates on strength

children.text: yāvad balasya gataṃ tatrāsya yathākāmacāro bhavati yo balaṃ brahmety upāste
children.translated_text: as far as strength extends, there he has freedom to move as he wishes, he who meditates on strength as brahman.
Venerable sir, is there anything greater than strength?
There is indeed something greater than strength.
May the venerable sir tell that to me.
Food indeed is greater than strength.

children.text: tasmād yady api daśa rātrīr nāśnīyāt
children.translated_text: Therefore, if one were not to eat for ten nights,
and if he were still to live,
then he would become one who does not see, does not hear, does not think, does not understand, does not act, and does not know.

children.text: athānnasyāye draṣṭā bhavati śrotā bhavati mantā bhavati boddhā bhavati kartā bhavati vijñātā bhavati
children.translated_text: But when food comes to him, he becomes a seer, a hearer, a thinker, an understander, a doer, and a knower.
Meditate on food.
One who meditates on food as brahman
attains, indeed, worlds that have food and worlds that have drink.

children.text: yāvad annasya gataṃ tatrāsya yathākāmacāro bhavati yo 'nnaṃ brahmety upāste
children.translated_text: As far as food extends, there he has freedom to move as he wishes, he who meditates on food as brahman.
Venerable sir, is there anything greater than food?
There is indeed something greater than food.
May the venerable sir tell that to me.
Waters indeed are greater than food.

children.text: tasmād yadā suvṛṣṭir na bhavati vyādhīyante prāṇā annaṃ kanīyo bhaviṣyatīti
children.translated_text: Therefore, when there is not good rain, the life-breaths become distressed, thinking, 'Food will become scarce.'

children.text: atha yadā suvṛṣṭir bhavaty ānandinaḥ prāṇā bhavanty annaṃ bahu bhaviṣyatīti
children.translated_text: But when there is good rain, the life-breaths become joyful, thinking, 'There will be abundant food.'

children.text: āpa evemā mūrtā yeyaṃ pṛthivī yad antarikṣaṃ yad dyaur yat parvatā yad devamanuṣyā yat paśavaś ca vayāṃsi ca tṛṇavanaspatayaḥ śvāpadāny ā kīṭapataṅgapipīlakam
children.translated_text: Waters alone are these embodied forms: this earth, the atmosphere, heaven, the mountains, gods and human beings, cattle, birds, grasses and trees, wild animals down to worms, insects, flying insects, and ants.
Waters alone are these embodied forms.
Meditate on waters.
One who meditates on waters as brahman
obtains all desires and becomes satisfied.

children.text: yāvad apāṃ gataṃ tatrāsya yathākāmacāro bhavati yo 'po brahmety upāste
children.translated_text: As far as waters extend, there he has freedom to move as he wishes, he who meditates on waters as brahman.
Venerable sir, is there anything greater than waters?
There is indeed something greater than waters.
May the venerable sir tell that to me.
Fire indeed is greater than waters.

children.text: tad vā etad vāyum āgṛhyākāśam abhitapati tadāhur niśocati nitapati varṣiṣyati vā iti
children.translated_text: That fire, grasping the wind, heats the space; then people say, 'It is scorching, it is burning; perhaps it will rain.'
Having first shown fire, it then releases the waters.

children.text: tad etad ūrdhvābhiś ca tiraścībhiś ca vidyudbhir āhrādāś caranti tasmād āhur vidyotate stanayati varṣiṣyati vā iti
children.translated_text: Those thunderclaps move about with upward and sideways flashes of lightning; therefore people say, 'It is flashing, it is thundering; perhaps it will rain.'
Having first shown fire, it then releases the waters.
Meditate on fire.
One who meditates on fire as brahman

children.text: tejasvī vai sa tejasvato lokān bhāsvato 'pahatatamaskān abhisidhyati
children.translated_text: being fiery himself, attains fiery worlds, shining worlds, worlds whose darkness has been driven away.

children.text: yāvat tejaso gataṃ tatrāsya yathākāmacāro bhavati yas tejo brahmety upāste
children.translated_text: As far as fire extends, there he has freedom to move as he wishes, he who meditates on fire as brahman.
Venerable sir, is there anything greater than fire?
There is indeed something greater than fire.
May the venerable sir tell that to me.
Space indeed is greater than fire.

children.text: ākāśe vai sūryācandramasāv ubhau vidyun nakṣatrāṇy agniḥ
children.translated_text: In space, indeed, are both the sun and moon, lightning, the stars, and fire.
Through space one calls out.
Through space one hears.
Through space one answers back.
In space one rejoices.
In space one does not rejoice.
In space one is born.
Into space one is born forth.
Meditate on space.
One who meditates on space as brahman

children.text: ākāśavato vai sa lokān prakāśavato 'saṃbādhān urugāyavato 'bhisidhyati
children.translated_text: attains, indeed, spacious worlds, luminous worlds, unobstructed worlds, and wide-ranging worlds.

children.text: yāvad ākāśasya gataṃ tatrāsya yathākāmacāro bhavati ya ākāśaṃ brahmety upāste
children.translated_text: As far as space extends, there he has freedom to move as he wishes, he who meditates on space as brahman.
Is there, sir, something greater than space?
There is indeed something greater than space.
Let the blessed one tell me that.
Memory indeed is greater than space.

children.text: tasmād yady api bahava āsīrann asmaranto naiva te kaṃcana śṛṇuyur na manvīran na vijānīran
children.translated_text: Therefore, even if many people were present, if they did not remember, they would not hear anyone at all, nor think, nor understand.

children.text: yadā vāva te smareyur atha śṛṇuyur atha manvīrann atha vijānīran
children.translated_text: But when they remember, then they hear, then they think, then they understand.

children.text: smareṇa vai putrān vijānāti smareṇa paśūn
children.translated_text: By memory one recognizes sons; by memory, cattle.
Meditate upon memory.
The one who meditates upon memory as <s>brahman</s>

children.text: yāvat smarasya gataṃ tatrāsya yathākāmacāro bhavati yaḥ smaraṃ brahmety upāste
children.translated_text: as far as memory extends, there he has freedom to move as he wishes, he who meditates upon memory as <s>brahman</s>.
Is there, sir, something greater than memory?
There is indeed something greater than memory.
Let the blessed one tell me that.
Hope indeed is greater than memory.

children.text: āśeddho vai smaro mantrān adhīte karmāṇi kurute putrāṃś ca paśūṃś cecchata imaṃ ca lokaṃ amuṃ cecchate
children.translated_text: Kindled by hope, memory indeed studies mantras, performs rites, desires sons and cattle, and desires this world and the other.
Meditate upon hope.
The one who meditates upon hope as <s>brahman</s>
through hope all his desires are fulfilled.
His blessings become unfailing.

children.text: yāvad āśāyā gataṃ tatrāsya yathākāmacāro bhavati ya āśāṃ brahmety upāste
children.translated_text: As far as hope extends, there he has freedom to move as he wishes, he who meditates upon hope as <s>brahman</s>.
Is there, sir, something greater than hope?
There is something greater than hope.
Let the blessed one tell me that.
<s>Prāṇa</s> is indeed greater than hope.

children.text: yathā vā arā nābhau samarpitā evam asmin prāṇe sarvaṃ samarpitam
children.translated_text: Just as spokes are fixed in a nave, so all this is fixed in this <s>prāṇa</s>.
<s>Prāṇa</s> moves through <s>prāṇa</s>.
<s>Prāṇa</s> gives <s>prāṇa</s>.
One gives to <s>prāṇa</s>.
<s>Prāṇa</s> is the father.
<s>Prāṇa</s> is the mother.
<s>Prāṇa</s> is the brother.
<s>Prāṇa</s> is the sister.
<s>Prāṇa</s> is the teacher.
<s>Prāṇa</s> is the brahmin.

children.text: sa yadi pitaraṃ vā mātaraṃ vā bhrātaraṃ vā svasāraṃ vācāryaṃ vā brāhmaṇaṃ vā kiṃcid bhṛśam iva pratyāha
children.translated_text: If someone answers father or mother or brother or sister or teacher or brahmin with words that are, as it were, somewhat harsh,
they say to him simply, 'Shame on you!'

children.text: pitṛhā vai tvam asi mātṛhā vai tvam asi bhrātṛhā vai tvam asi svasṛhā vai tvam asy ācāryahā vai tvam asi brāhmaṇahā vai tvam asīti ||
children.translated_text: 'You are a killer of your father; you are a killer of your mother; you are a killer of your brother; you are a killer of your sister; you are a killer of your teacher; you are a killer of a brahmin.'

children.text: atha yady apy enān utkrāntaprāṇāñchūlena samāsaṃ vyatisaṃdahet
children.translated_text: But if, when their <s>prāṇas</s> had departed, he were even to gather them together and pierce them through with a spit,

children.text: naivainaṃ brūyuḥ pitṛhāsīti na mātṛhāsīti na bhrātṛhāsīti na svasṛhāsīti nācāryahāsīti na brāhmaṇahāsīti ||
children.translated_text: they would not say to him, 'You are a killer of your father,' nor 'a killer of your mother,' nor 'a killer of your brother,' nor 'a killer of your sister,' nor 'a killer of your teacher,' nor 'a killer of a brahmin.'
For <s>prāṇa</s> itself becomes all these.

children.text: sa vā eṣa evaṃ paśyann evaṃ manvāna evaṃ vijānann ativādī bhavati
children.translated_text: One who sees thus, thinks thus, and understands thus becomes an <s>ativādin</s> (one who speaks beyond).
If they should say to him, 'You are an <s>ativādin</s>,'
he should say, 'I am an <s>ativādin</s>.'
He should not deny it.

children.text: yadā vai vijānāty atha satyaṃ vadati
children.translated_text: When one understands, then one speaks truth.
One who does not understand does not speak truth.
Only one who understands speaks truth.
But understanding itself must be sought to be known.
Sir, I wish to know understanding.
When one thinks, then one understands.
Without thinking, one does not understand.
Only by thinking does one understand.
But thought itself must be sought to be known.
Sir, I wish to know thought.
When one has faith, then one thinks.
One without faith does not think.
Only one who has faith thinks.
But faith itself must be sought to be known.
Sir, I wish to know faith.
When one stands firm, then one has faith.
One who does not stand firm does not have faith.
Only one who stands firm has faith.
But steadfastness itself must be sought to be known.
Sir, I wish to know steadfastness.
When one acts, then one stands firm.
Without acting, one does not stand firm.
Only after acting does one stand firm.
But action itself must be sought to be known.
Sir, I wish to know action.
When one obtains happiness, then one acts.
Without obtaining happiness, one does not act.
Only after obtaining happiness does one act.
But happiness itself must be sought to be known.
Sir, I wish to know happiness.
That which is <s>bhūman</s> (fullness) is happiness.
There is no happiness in what is small.
<s>Bhūman</s> alone is happiness.
But <s>bhūman</s> itself must be sought to be known.
Sir, I wish to know <s>bhūman</s>.

children.text: yatra nānyat paśyati nānyacchṛṇoti nānyad vijānāti sa bhūmā
children.translated_text: Where one sees nothing else, hears nothing else, and understands nothing else, that is <s>bhūman</s>.

children.text: atha yatrānyat paśyaty anyacchṛṇoty anyad vijānāti tad alpam
children.translated_text: But where one sees something else, hears something else, and understands something else, that is the small.
That which is <s>bhūman</s> is the immortal.
But what is small is mortal.
'Sir, in what is it established?'

children.text: sve mahimni yadi vā na mahimnīti ||
children.translated_text: 'In its own greatness, or else not in greatness.'

children.text: go'śvam iha mahimety ācakṣate hastihiraṇyaṃ dāsabhāryaṃ kṣetrāṇy āyatanānīti
children.translated_text: Cows and horses here people call greatness, also elephants and gold, servants and wives, fields and dwellings.
I do not speak in this way.
'I do speak of it,' he said.
For one thing is established in another.

children.text: sa evādhastāt sa upariṣṭāt sa paścāt sa purastāt sa dakṣiṇataḥ sa uttarataḥ
children.translated_text: He alone is below; he is above; he is behind; he is in front; he is to the south; he is to the north.
He alone is all this.
Now therefore there is the instruction in terms of the I-maker.

children.text: aham evādhastād aham upariṣṭād ahaṃ paścād ahaṃ purastād ahaṃ dakṣiṇato 'ham uttarato 'ham evedaṃ sarvam iti ||
children.translated_text: I alone am below; I am above; I am behind; I am in front; I am to the south; I am to the north; I alone am all this.
Now therefore there is the instruction in terms of the Self.

children.text: ātmaivādhastād ātmopariṣṭād ātmā paścād ātmā purastād ātmā dakṣiṇata ātmottarata ātmaivedaṃ sarvam iti
children.translated_text: <s>Ātman</s> (the Self) alone is below; <s>ātman</s> is above; <s>ātman</s> is behind; <s>ātman</s> is in front; <s>ātman</s> is to the south; <s>ātman</s> is to the north; <s>ātman</s> alone is all this.

children.text: sa vā eṣa evaṃ paśyann evaṃ manvāna evaṃ vijānann ātmaratir ātmakrīḍa ātmamithuna ātmānandaḥ sa svarāḍ bhavati
children.translated_text: Truly, one who sees thus, thinks thus, and understands thus, whose delight is in the Self, whose play is in the Self, whose partner is the Self, whose bliss is the Self, becomes self-ruling.
He has freedom to move as he wishes in all worlds.

children.text: atha ye 'nyathāto vidur anyarājānas te kṣayyalokā bhavanti
children.translated_text: But those who know otherwise, who have other kings, have perishable worlds.
For them there is no freedom to move as they wish in all worlds.

children.text: tasya ha vā etasyaivaṃ paśyata evaṃ manvānasyaivaṃ vijānata ātmataḥ prāṇa ātmata āśātmataḥ smara ātmata ākāśa ātmatas teja ātmata āpa ātmata āvirbhāvatirobhāvāv ātmato 'nnam ātmato balam ātmato vijñānam ātmato dhyānam ātmataś cittam ātmataḥ saṃkalpa ātmato mana ātmato vāg ātmato nāmātmato mantrā ātmataḥ karmāṇy ātmata evedaṃ sarvam iti ||
children.translated_text: For this very person, seeing thus, thinking thus, and knowing thus, from the self comes the vital breath; from the self, hope; from the self, memory; from the self, space; from the self, heat; from the self, waters; from the self, manifestation and disappearance; from the self, food; from the self, strength; from the self, understanding; from the self, meditation; from the self, consciousness; from the self, resolve; from the self, mind; from the self, speech; from the self, name; from the self, mantras; from the self, rites. From the self alone is all this.
On this there is this verse:

children.text: na paśyo mṛtyuṃ paśyati na rogaṃ nota duḥkhatām
children.translated_text: The seeing one does not see death, nor disease, nor even suffering.

children.text: sarvaṃ ha paśyaḥ paśyati sarvam āpnoti sarvaśaḥ
children.translated_text: The seeing one sees everything; he obtains everything in every way.
Thus.

children.text: sa ekadhā bhavati tridhā bhavati pañcadhā
children.translated_text: He becomes onefold, he becomes threefold, fivefold,

children.text: saptadhā navadhā caiva punaś caikādaśa smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: sevenfold and also ninefold; again he is remembered as elevenfold.

children.text: śataṃ ca daśa caikaś ca sahasrāṇi ca viṃśatiḥ
children.translated_text: And as a hundred, and ten, and one, and as twenty thousand.
When food is pure, being becomes pure.
When being is pure, memory is firm.
When memory is obtained, there is release from all knots.

children.text: tasmai mṛditakaṣāyāya tamasas pāraṃ darśayati bhagavān sanatkumāraḥ
children.translated_text: To him whose impurities have been rubbed away, the venerable <s>Sanatkumāra</s> shows the far shore of darkness.
They call him <s>Skanda</s>.

children.text: atha yad idam asmin brahmapure daharaṃ puṇḍarīkaṃ veśma daharo 'sminn antarākāśaḥ
children.translated_text: Now, this small lotus-like dwelling here in this city of <s>brahman</s>: within it there is a small inner space.

children.text: tasmin yad antas tad anveṣṭavyaṃ tad vāva vijijñāsitavyam iti ||
children.translated_text: What is inside it is to be sought; that indeed is to be desired to know.

children.text: taṃ ced brūyur yad idam asmin brahmapure daharaṃ puṇḍarīkaṃ veśma daharo 'sminn antarākāśaḥ kiṃ tad atra vidyate yad anveṣṭavyaṃ yad vāva vijijñāsitavyam iti
children.translated_text: If they should say to him, "This small lotus-like dwelling here in this city of <s>brahman</s>, and the small inner space within it: what is found there that is to be sought, that indeed is to be desired to know?"
he should say:

children.text: yāvān vā ayam ākāśas tāvān eṣo 'ntarhṛdaya ākāśaḥ
children.translated_text: As vast as this space is, so vast is this space within the heart.
Both heaven and earth are contained within it.

children.text: ubhāv agniś ca vāyuś ca sūryācandramasāv ubhau vidyun nakṣatrāṇi
children.translated_text: Both fire and wind, both sun and moon, lightning and the stars are there.

children.text: yac cāsyehāsti yac ca nāsti sarvaṃ tad asmin samāhitam iti ||
children.translated_text: Whatever of his exists here, and whatever does not exist, all that is contained in it.

children.text: taṃ ced brūyur asmiṃś cedaṃ brahmapure sarvaṃ samāhitaṃ sarvāṇi ca bhūtāni sarve ca kāmā yad enaj jarā vāpnoti pradhvaṃsate vā kiṃ tato 'tiśiṣyata iti ||
children.translated_text: If they should say to him, "If in this city of <s>brahman</s> all this is contained, and all beings and all desires, then when old age overtakes it or it is destroyed, what remains of it?"
he should say:

children.text: nāsya jarayaitaj jīryati na vadhenāsya hanyate
children.translated_text: This is not worn out by his old age, nor is it killed by his being slain.

children.text: etat satyaṃ brahmapuram asmin kāmāḥ samāhitāḥ
children.translated_text: This is the true city of <s>brahman</s>; in it desires are contained.

children.text: eṣa ātmāpahatapāpmā vijaro vimṛtyur viśoko vijighatso 'pipāsaḥ satyakāmaḥ satyasaṃkalpaḥ
children.translated_text: This is the self, free from evil, ageless, deathless, sorrowless, without hunger and thirst, whose desire is true and whose resolve is true.

children.text: yathā hy eveha prajā anvāviśanti yathānuśāsanam
children.translated_text: For just as here people enter according to instruction,

children.text: yaṃ yam antam abhikāmā bhavanti yaṃ janapadaṃ yaṃ kṣetrabhāgaṃ taṃ tam evopajīvanti ||
children.translated_text: whatever place they desire, whatever country, whatever portion of land, that very thing they live upon.

children.text: tad yatheha karmajito lokaḥ kṣīyata evam evāmutra puṇyajito lokaḥ kṣīyate
children.translated_text: Just as here the world won by action is exhausted, so there too the world won by merit is exhausted.

children.text: tad ya ihātmānam ananuvidya vrajanty etāṃś ca satyān kāmāṃs teṣāṃ sarveṣu lokeṣv akāmacāro bhavati
children.translated_text: Those who depart from here without discovering the self and these true desires have no freedom to move as they wish in all worlds.

children.text: atha ya ihātmānam anivudya vrajanty etaṃś ca satyān kāmāṃs teṣāṃ sarveṣu lokeṣu kāmacāro bhavati ||
children.translated_text: But those who depart from here having discovered the self and these true desires have freedom to move as they wish in all worlds.
If he desires the world of the fathers,
from his resolve alone his fathers arise.
Endowed with that world of the fathers, he is honored.
And if he desires the world of the mothers,
from his resolve alone his mothers arise.
Endowed with that world of the mothers, he is honored.
And if he desires the world of the brothers,
from his resolve alone his brothers arise.
Endowed with that world of the brothers, he is honored.
And if he desires the world of the sisters,
from his resolve alone his sisters arise.
Endowed with that world of the sisters, he is honored.
And if he desires the world of friends,
from his resolve alone his friends arise.
Endowed with that world of friends, he is honored.
And if he desires the world of perfumes and garlands,
from his resolve alone perfumes and garlands arise.
Endowed with that world of perfumes and garlands, he is honored.
And if he desires the world of food and drink,
from his resolve alone food and drink arise.
Endowed with that world of food and drink, he is honored.
And if he desires the world of song and instrumental music,
from his resolve alone song and instrumental music arise.
Endowed with that world of song and instrumental music, he is honored.
And if he desires the world of women,
from his resolve alone women arise.
Endowed with that world of women, he is honored.
Whatever place he desires,
whatever desire he desires,
that arises for him from resolve alone.
Endowed with it, he is honored.
These true desires are covered by the untrue.
Though they are true, an untruth is their covering.

children.text: yo yo hy asyetaḥ praiti na tam iha darśanāya labhate ||
children.translated_text: For whoever of his has departed from here, he does not obtain that one here for seeing.

children.text: atha ye cāsyeha jīvā ye ca pretā yac cānyad icchan na labhate sarvaṃ tad atra gatvā vindate
children.translated_text: But those of his who are alive here, those who are dead, and whatever else he desires but does not obtain, all that he finds after going there.

children.text: atra hy asyaite satyāḥ kāmā anṛtāpidhānāḥ
children.translated_text: For here these true desires of his are covered by the unreal.

children.text: tad yathāpi hiraṇyanidhiṃ nihitam akṣetrajñā upary upari saṃcaranto na vindeyuḥ
children.translated_text: Just as people who do not know the place might pass again and again over a hidden treasure of gold and not find it,

children.text: evam evemāḥ sarvāḥ prajā ahar ahar gacchantya etaṃ brahmalokaṃ na vindanty anṛtena hi pratyūḍhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: so indeed all these beings go day after day to this <s>brahmaloka</s> and do not find it, for they are obstructed by the unreal.
This very <s>ātman</s> is in the heart.

children.text: tasyaitad eva niruktaṃ hṛdy ayam iti tasmāddhṛd ayam
children.translated_text: Of it this is the etymological explanation: "this one is in the heart"; therefore it is called the heart.

children.text: ahar ahar vā evaṃvit svargaṃ lokam eti ||
children.translated_text: Day after day, one who knows in this way reaches the heavenly world.

children.text: atha ya eṣa saṃprasādo 'smāccharīrāt samutthāya paraṃ jyotir upasaṃpadya svena rūpenābhiniṣpadyata eṣa ātmeti hovāca
children.translated_text: Now this <s>saṃprasāda</s> (serene self), rising up from this body, attaining the supreme light, and manifesting in its own form, is the <s>ātman</s>, he said.
This is immortal and fearless; this is <s>brahman</s>.

children.text: tasya ha vā etasya brahmaṇo nāma satyam iti ||
children.translated_text: The name of this <s>brahman</s> is indeed "truth."

children.text: atha ya ātmā sa setur dhṛtir eṣāṃ lokānām asaṃbhedāya
children.translated_text: Now that <s>ātman</s> is the bridge, the support of these worlds, so that they do not become intermixed.

children.text: naitaṃ setum ahorātre tarato na jarā na mṛtyur na śoko na sukṛtam
children.translated_text: Day and night do not cross this bridge, nor old age, nor death, nor sorrow, nor merit.
All evils turn back from it.
For this <s>brahmaloka</s> is free from evil.

children.text: tasmād vā etaṃ setuṃ tīrtvā andhaḥ sann anandho bhavati
children.translated_text: Therefore, having crossed this bridge, though blind, one becomes not blind.
Though pierced, one becomes unpierced.
Though afflicted, one becomes unafflicted.

children.text: tasmād vā etaṃ setuṃ tīrtvā api naktam ahar evābhiniṣpadyate
children.translated_text: Therefore, having crossed this bridge, even night becomes manifest as day.
For this <s>brahmaloka</s> is illuminated once and for all.

children.text: tad ya evaitaṃ brahmalokaṃ brahmacaryeṇānuvindanti teṣām evaiṣa brahmalokaḥ
children.translated_text: Those who discover this <s>brahmaloka</s> through <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibate discipline), to them alone belongs this <s>brahmaloka</s>.
For them there is freedom to move as they wish in all worlds.

children.text: atha yad yajña ity ācakṣate brahmacaryam eva tat
children.translated_text: Now, what people call sacrifice is just <s>brahmacarya</s>.

children.text: brahmacaryeṇa hy eva yo jñātā taṃ vindate
children.translated_text: For through <s>brahmacarya</s> alone the one who knows finds that.

children.text: atha yad iṣṭam ity ācakṣate brahmacaryam eva tat
children.translated_text: Now, what people call worshipful offering is just <s>brahmacarya</s>.
For by offering through <s>brahmacarya</s> alone one discovers the <s>ātman</s>.

children.text: atha yat sattrāyaṇam ity ācakṣate brahmacaryam eva tat
children.translated_text: Now, what people call <s>sattrāyaṇa</s> is just <s>brahmacarya</s>.

children.text: brahmacaryeṇa hy eva sata ātmanas trāṇaṃ vindate
children.translated_text: For through <s>brahmacarya</s> alone one finds protection for the true <s>ātman</s>.

children.text: atha yan maunam ity ācakṣate brahmacaryam eva tat
children.translated_text: Now, what people call silence is just <s>brahmacarya</s>.
For after discovering the <s>ātman</s> through <s>brahmacarya</s> alone, one reflects.

children.text: atha yad anāśakāyanam ity ācakṣate brahmacaryam eva tat
children.translated_text: Now, what people call <s>anāśakāyana</s> is just <s>brahmacarya</s>.

children.text: eṣa hy ātmā na naśyati yaṃ brahmacaryeṇānuvindate
children.translated_text: For this <s>ātman</s>, which one discovers through <s>brahmacarya</s>, does not perish.

children.text: atha yad araṇyāyanam ity ācakṣate brahmacaryam eva tat
children.translated_text: Now, what people call <s>araṇyāyana</s> is just <s>brahmacarya</s>.

children.text: tat araś ca ha vai ṇyaś cārṇavau brahmaloke tṛtīyasyām ito divi
children.translated_text: There, <s>Ara</s> and <s>Ṇya</s> are two oceans in <s>brahmaloka</s>, in the third heaven from here.
There is the lake <s>Airaṃmadīya</s>.
There is the aśvattha tree <s>Somasavana</s>.

children.text: tad aparājitā pūr brahmaṇaḥ prabhuvimitaṃ hiraṇmayam ||
children.translated_text: There is <s>Aparājitā</s>, the city of <s>brahman</s>, and a golden abode measured out by the Lord.

children.text: tad ya evaitāv araṃ ca ṇyaṃ cārṇavau brahmaloke brahmacaryeṇānuvindanti teṣām evaiṣa brahmalokaḥ
children.translated_text: Those who discover these two oceans, <s>Ara</s> and <s>Ṇya</s>, in <s>brahmaloka</s> through <s>brahmacarya</s>, to them alone belongs this <s>brahmaloka</s>.
For them there is freedom to move as they wish in all worlds.

children.text: atha yā etā hṛdayasya nāḍyas tāḥ piṅgalasyāṇimnas tiṣṭhanti śuklasya nīlasya pītasya lohitasyeti
children.translated_text: Now these <s>nāḍīs</s> of the heart consist of a subtle essence that is tawny, white, blue, yellow, and red.

children.text: asau vādityaḥ piṅgala eṣa śukla eṣa nīla eṣa pīta eṣa lohitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That sun there is tawny; it is white, it is blue, it is yellow, it is red.

children.text: tad yathā mahāpatha ātata ubhau grāmau gacchatīmaṃ cāmuṃ caivam evaitā ādityasya raśmaya ubhau lokau gacchantīmaṃ cāmuṃ ca
children.translated_text: Just as a great road, stretched out, goes to both villages, to this one and to that one, so these rays of the sun go to both worlds, to this one and to that one.

children.text: amuṣmād ādityāt pratāyante tā āsu nāḍīṣu sṛptāḥ
children.translated_text: They extend from that sun and are inserted into these <s>nāḍīs</s>.

children.text: ābhyo nāḍībhyaḥ pratāyante te 'muṣminn āditye sṛptāḥ ||
children.translated_text: They extend from these <s>nāḍīs</s> and are inserted into that sun.

children.text: tad yatraitat suptaḥ samastaḥ samprasannaḥ svapnaṃ na vijānāti
children.translated_text: When a person is asleep, fully gathered together and serene, and knows no dream,
then he has entered into these <s>nāḍīs</s>.
No evil at all touches him.
For at that time he is endowed with radiance.
Now, when he has been brought to this state of weakness,

children.text: tam abhita āsīnā āhur jānāsi māṃ jānāsi mām iti
children.translated_text: those sitting around him say, "Do you know me? Do you know me?"
As long as he has not departed from this body,
so long he knows.
But when he departs from this body,
then by these very rays he ascends upward.

children.text: sa om iti vā hod vā mīyate
children.translated_text: Whether he dies saying <s>Om</s>, or even without it,

children.text: sa yāvat kṣipyen manas tāvad ādityaṃ gacchati
children.translated_text: as quickly as the mind may dart, just so quickly he goes to the sun.

children.text: etad vai khalu lokadvāraṃ viduṣāṃ prapadanaṃ nirodho 'viduṣām ||
children.translated_text: This indeed is the doorway to the world, an entrance for those who know and a barrier for those who do not know.
On this there is this verse:

children.text: śataṃ caikā ca hṛdayasya nāḍyas tāsāṃ mūrdhānam abhiniḥsṛtaikā
children.translated_text: There are a hundred and one <s>nāḍīs</s> of the heart; of them, one has gone out to the crown of the head.

children.text: tayordhvam āyann amṛtatvam eti viṣvaṅṅ anyā utkramaṇe bhavanty utkramaṇe bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Going upward by it, one attains immortality; the others serve for departure in different directions, for departure.

children.text: ya ātmā apahatapāpmā vijaro vimṛtyur viśoko vijighatso 'pipāsaḥ satyakāmaḥ satyasaṃkalpaḥ so 'nveṣṭavyaḥ sa vijijñāsitavyaḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>ātman</s> that is free from evil, ageless, deathless, free from sorrow, free from hunger and thirst, whose desire is true and whose resolve is true, is to be sought and is to be understood.

children.text: sa sarvāṃś ca lokān āpnoti sarvāṃś ca kāmān yas tam ātmānam anuvidya vijānātīti ha prajāpatir uvāca ||
children.translated_text: He obtains all worlds and all desires who, after discovering that <s>ātman</s>, knows it; so <s>Prajāpati</s> said.
Both the gods and the asuras learned of this.

children.text: te hocur hanta tam ātmānam anvecchāmo yam ātmānam anviṣya sarvāṃś ca lokān āpnoti sarvāṃś ca kāmān iti
children.translated_text: They said, "Come, let us seek that <s>ātman</s>, by seeking which one obtains all worlds and all desires."
<s>Indra</s> went forth on behalf of the gods, and <s>Virocana</s> on behalf of the asuras.

children.text: tau hāsaṃvidānāv eva samitpāṇī prajāpatisakāśam ājagmatuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Without having arranged it with one another, the two came to <s>Prajāpati</s>, fuel in hand.

children.text: tau ha dvātriṃśataṃ varṣāṇi brahmacaryam ūṣatuḥ
children.translated_text: The two lived as brahmacārins for thirty-two years.
<s>Prajāpati</s> said to them,
"Desiring what have you dwelt here?"

children.text: tau hocatur ya ātmā apahatapāpmā vijaro vimṛtyur viśoko vijighatso 'pipāsaḥ satyakāmaḥ satyasaṃkalpaḥ so 'nveṣṭavyaḥ sa vijijñāsitavyaḥ
children.translated_text: The two said, "The <s>ātman</s> (Self) that is free from evil, ageless, deathless, sorrowless, without hunger, without thirst, whose desire is true and whose resolve is true, that is to be sought; that is to be understood.

children.text: sa sarvāṃś ca lokān āpnoti sarvāṃś ca kāmān yas tam ātmānam anuvidya vijānātīti bhagavato vaco vedayante
children.translated_text: He obtains all worlds and all desires, he who, having discovered that <s>ātman</s>, knows it. They report this as the venerable one's statement.
Desiring that, we have stayed here."

children.text: tau ha prajāpatir uvāca ya eṣo 'kṣiṇi puruṣo dṛśyata eṣa ātmeti hovāca
children.translated_text: Then <s>Prajāpati</s> said to them, "This person who is seen in the eye, this is the <s>ātman</s>," he said.
"This is immortal and fearless; this is <s>brahman</s>."

children.text: atha yo 'yaṃ bhagavo 'psu parikhyāyate yaś cāyam ādarśe katama eṣa iti
children.translated_text: "Then, venerable sir, the one who is perceived in water and the one here in a mirror: which one is he?"

children.text: eṣa u evaiṣu sarveṣvannteṣu parikhyāyata iti hovāca ||
children.translated_text: "This very one is perceived in all these reflecting surfaces," he said.

children.text: udaśarāva ātmānam avekṣya yad ātmano na vijānīthas tan me prabrūtam iti
children.translated_text: "Look at yourselves in a bowl of water, and whatever of the self you do not understand, tell me that."
Then the two looked into a bowl of water.

children.text: tau ha prajāpatir uvāca kiṃ paśyatha iti
children.translated_text: Then <s>Prajāpati</s> said to them, "What do you see?"

children.text: tau hocatuḥ sarvam evedam āvāṃ bhagava ātmānaṃ paśyāva ā lomabhyaḥ ā nakhebhyaḥ pratirūpam iti ||
children.translated_text: The two said, "Venerable sir, we see this whole self of ours, a corresponding likeness down to the hairs and down to the nails."

children.text: tau ha prajāpatir uvāca sādhvalaṃkṛtau suvasanau pariṣkṛtau bhūtvodaśarāve 'vekṣethām iti
children.translated_text: Then <s>Prajāpati</s> said to them, "Having become well adorned, well dressed, and groomed, look into the bowl of water."

children.text: tau ha sādhvalaṃkṛtau suvasanau pariṣkṛtau bhūtvodaśarāve 'vekṣāṃcakrāte
children.translated_text: Then, having become well adorned, well dressed, and groomed, the two looked into the bowl of water.

children.text: tau ha prajāpatir uvāca kiṃ paśyatha iti ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Prajāpati</s> said to them, "What do you see?"

children.text: tau hocatur yathaivedam āvāṃ bhagavaḥ sādhvalaṃkṛtau suvasanau pariṣkṛtau sva evam evemau bhagavaḥ sādhvalaṃkṛtau suvasanau pariṣkṛtāv iti
children.translated_text: The two said, "Just as we ourselves here, venerable sir, are well adorned, well dressed, and groomed, so these two also, venerable sir, are well adorned, well dressed, and groomed."
"This is the <s>ātman</s>," he said.
"This is immortal and fearless; this is <s>brahman</s>."
Then the two went away with peaceful hearts.
Then, after watching them, <s>Prajāpati</s> said,

children.text: anupalabhyātmānam ananuvidya vrajato yatara etadupaniṣado bhaviṣyanti devā vā asurā vā te parābhaviṣyantīti
children.translated_text: "They are going away without obtaining the <s>ātman</s>, without discovering it. Whichever of these, whether gods or asuras, will hold this <s>upaniṣad</s> (teaching), they will be defeated."

children.text: sa ha śāntahṛdaya eva virocano 'surāñ jagāma
children.translated_text: Then, with a peaceful heart, <s>Virocana</s> went to the asuras.

children.text: tebhyo haitām upaniṣadaṃ provāca ātmaiveha mahayya ātmā paricaryaḥ
children.translated_text: He taught them this <s>upaniṣad</s>: "The self alone is to be honored here; the self is to be served."

children.text: ātmānam eveha mahayann ātmānaṃ paricarann ubhau lokāv āpnotīmaṃ cāmuṃ ceti ||
children.translated_text: "By honoring the self here and serving the self, one obtains both worlds, this one and the other."

children.text: tasmād apyaddyehādadānam aśraddadhānam ayajamānam āhur āsuro bateti
children.translated_text: Therefore even today here they call someone who gives no gifts, has no faith, and performs no sacrifice, "Ah, an asura!"
For this is the <s>upaniṣad</s> of the asuras.
They prepare the body of a dead man with food, clothing, and ornament,

children.text: etena hy amuṃ lokaṃ jeṣyanto manyante ||
children.translated_text: for by this they think they will win the other world.

children.text: atha hendro 'prāpyaiva devān etad bhayaṃ dadarśa
children.translated_text: But <s>Indra</s>, before he had even reached the gods, saw this danger:

children.text: yathaiva khalv ayam asmiñcharīre sādhvalaṃkṛte sādhvalaṃkṛto bhavati suvasane suvasanaḥ pariṣkṛte pariṣkṛta evam evāyam asminn andhe 'ndho bhavati srāme srāmaḥ parivṛkṇe parivṛkṇaḥ
children.translated_text: "Just as this one becomes well adorned when this body is well adorned, well dressed when it is well dressed, and groomed when it is groomed, so too, when this body is blind, he is blind; when it is lame, he is lame; when it is mutilated, he is mutilated.

children.text: asyaiva śarīrasya nāśam anv eṣa naśyati
children.translated_text: Upon the destruction of this very body, this one perishes.
I see nothing satisfactory in this."
He came back again, carrying fuel in his hand.
Then <s>Prajāpati</s> said to him,

children.text: maghavan yacchāntahṛdayaḥ prāvrājīḥ sārdhaṃ virocanena kim icchan punar āgama iti
children.translated_text: "<s>Maghavan</s>, since you went away with a peaceful heart together with <s>Virocana</s>, desiring what have you come back?"

children.text: sa hovāca yathā eva khalvayaṃ bhagavo 'smiñcharīre sādhvalaṃkṛte sādhvalaṃkṛto bhavati suvasane suvasanaḥ pariṣkṛte pariṣkṛta evam evāyam asminn andhe 'ndho bhavati srāme srāmaḥ parivṛkṇe parivṛkṇaḥ
children.translated_text: He said, "Venerable sir, just as this one becomes well adorned when this body is well adorned, well dressed when it is well dressed, and groomed when it is groomed, so too, when this body is blind, he is blind; when it is lame, he is lame; when it is mutilated, he is mutilated.

children.text: asyaiva śarīrasya nāśam anv eṣa naśyati
children.translated_text: Upon the destruction of this very body, this one perishes.
I see nothing satisfactory in this."
"This is indeed so, <s>Maghavan</s>," he said.
"But I will explain this further to you.
Live here thirty-two more years."
So he lived there thirty-two more years.
Then he said to him:

children.text: ya eṣa svapne mahīyamānaś caraty eṣa ātmeti hovāca
children.translated_text: "This one who moves about exalted in a dream, this is the <s>ātman</s>," he said.
"This is immortal and fearless; this is <s>brahman</s>."
Then he went away with a peaceful heart.

children.text: sa hāprāpyaiva devān etad bhayaṃ dadarśa
children.translated_text: But before he had even reached the gods, he saw this danger:

children.text: tad yady apīdaṃ śarīram andhaṃ bhavaty anandhaḥ sa bhavati yadi srāmam asrāmaḥ
children.translated_text: "Even if this body is blind, that one is not blind; if it is lame, he is not lame.
He is not tainted by its defect.
He is not killed by the killing of this body.
He is not lame through its lameness.
Yet they seem to kill him.
They seem to strip him.
He seems to become aware of unpleasant things.

children.text: api roditīva nāham atra bhogyaṃ paśyāmīti ||
children.translated_text: He even seems to weep. I see nothing satisfactory in this."
He came back again, carrying fuel in his hand.
Then <s>Prajāpati</s> said to him,

children.text: maghavan yacchāntahṛdayaḥ prāvrājīḥ kim icchan punar āgama iti
children.translated_text: "<s>Maghavan</s>, since you went away with a peaceful heart, desiring what have you come back?"
He said,

children.text: tad yady apīdaṃ bhagavaḥ śarīram andhaṃ bhavaty anandhaḥ sa bhavati yadi srāmam asrāmaḥ
children.translated_text: "Venerable sir, even if this body is blind, that one is not blind; if it is lame, he is not lame.
He is not tainted by its defect.
He is not killed by the killing of this body.
He is not lame through its lameness.
Yet they seem to kill him.
They seem to strip him.
He seems to become aware of unpleasant things.
He even seems to weep.
I see nothing satisfactory in this."
"This is indeed so, <s>Maghavan</s>," he said.
"But I will explain this further to you.
Live here thirty-two more years."
So he lived there thirty-two more years.
Then he said to him:

children.text: tad yatraitat suptaḥ samastaḥ samprasannaḥ svapnaṃ na vijānātyeṣa ātmeti hovāca
children.translated_text: Then, when this one is asleep, fully gathered together and serene, and does not know any dream, this is the <s>ātman</s> (Self), he said.
This is the immortal; this is the fearless; this is <s>brahman</s>.
He went away with a peaceful heart.

children.text: sa hāprāpyaiva devān etad bhayaṃ dadarśa
children.translated_text: But before he had reached the gods, he saw this danger.

children.text: nāha khalv ayam evaṃ saṃpraty ātmānaṃ jānāty ayam aham asmīti
children.translated_text: Surely this one, in this condition, does not know himself as, 'I am this.'
Nor does he know these beings.
He has merely entered into destruction.
I see nothing enjoyable here.
He came back again with fuel in hand.

children.text: taṃ ha prajāpatir uvāca maghavan yacchāntahṛdayaḥ prāvrājīḥ kim icchan punar āgama iti
children.translated_text: <s>Prajāpati</s> said to him, '<s>Maghavan</s>, since you went away with a peaceful heart, desiring what have you come back again?'

children.text: sa hovāca nāha khalv ayaṃ bhagava evaṃ saṃpraty ātmānaṃ jānāty ayam aham asmīti
children.translated_text: He said, 'Sir, surely this one, in this condition, does not know himself as, I am this.
Nor does he know these beings.
He has merely entered into destruction.
I see nothing enjoyable here.'
'Just so, <s>Maghavan</s>,' he said.
'But I shall explain this very one to you further.
Not, however, apart from this one.
Live here another five years.'
So he lived there another five years.
Those years came to one hundred and one.
That is what they refer to when they say:

children.text: ekaśataṃ ha vai varṣāṇi maghavān prajāpatau brahmacaryam uvāsa
children.translated_text: '<s>Maghavan</s> lived as a brahmacārin with <s>Prajāpati</s> for one hundred and one years.'
To him he said:

children.text: maghavan martyaṃ vā idaṃ śarīram āttaṃ mṛtyunā
children.translated_text: '<s>Maghavan</s>, this body is mortal, seized by death.
It is the seat of this immortal, bodiless <s>ātman</s>.
The embodied one is indeed seized by the pleasant and the unpleasant.

children.text: na vai saśarīrasya sataḥ priyāpriyayor apahatir asti
children.translated_text: For while one is embodied, there is no removal of the pleasant and the unpleasant.

children.text: aśarīraṃ vāva santaṃ na priyāpriye spṛśataḥ ||
children.translated_text: But when one is bodiless, the pleasant and the unpleasant do not touch one.
The wind is bodiless.
Cloud, lightning, and thunder are bodiless things.

children.text: tad yathaitāny amuṣmād ākāśāt samutthāya paraṃ jyotir upasaṃpadya svena rūpeṇābhiniṣpadyante ||
