children.translated_text: As these, rising up from that sky and reaching the highest light, appear in their own form,

children.text: evam evaiṣa saṃprasādo 'smāccharīrāt samutthāya paraṃ jyotir upasaṃpadya svena rūpeṇābhiniṣpadyate
children.translated_text: so too this serene one, rising up from this body and reaching the highest light, appears in his own form.
He is the highest person.

children.text: sa tatra paryeti jakṣat krīḍan ramamāṇaḥ strībhir vā yānair vā jñātibhir vā nopajanaṃ smarann idaṃ śarīram
children.translated_text: There he moves about, eating, playing, and rejoicing, whether with women, with vehicles, or with kinsmen, not remembering this body, the appendage of birth.

children.text: sa yathā prayogya ācaraṇe yukta evam evāyam asmiñcharīre prāṇo yuktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: As a draft animal is yoked to a cart, so this <s>prāṇa</s> (life-breath) is yoked to this body.

children.text: atha yatraitad ākāśam anuviṣaṇṇaṃ cakṣuḥ sa cākṣuṣaḥ puruṣo darśanāya cakṣuḥ
children.translated_text: Now where the eye has entered into space, that person in the eye is for seeing; the eye is the instrument of sight.

children.text: atha yo vededaṃ jighrāṇīti sa ātmā gandhāya ghrāṇam
children.translated_text: And the one who knows, 'Let me smell this,' is the <s>ātman</s>; the nose is for smelling.

children.text: atha yo vededam abhivyāharāṇīti sa ātmā abhivyāhārāya vāk
children.translated_text: And the one who knows, 'Let me utter this,' is the <s>ātman</s>; speech is for utterance.

children.text: atha yo vededaṃ śṛṇvānīti sa ātmā śravaṇāya śrotram ||
children.translated_text: And the one who knows, 'Let me hear this,' is the <s>ātman</s>; the ear is for hearing.

children.text: atha yo vededaṃ manvānīti sa ātmā
children.translated_text: And the one who knows, 'Let me think this,' is the <s>ātman</s>.
The mind is his divine eye.

children.text: sa vā eṣa etena daivena cakṣuṣā manasaitān kāmān paśyan ramate ya ete brahmaloke ||
children.translated_text: With this divine eye, the mind, he sees these desires that are in <s>brahmaloka</s> and rejoices.

children.text: taṃ vā etaṃ devā ātmānam upāsate
children.translated_text: The gods worship this very <s>ātman</s>.

children.text: tasmāt teṣāṃ sarve ca lokā āttāḥ sarve ca kāmāḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore all worlds and all desires are obtained for them.

children.text: sa sarvāṃś ca lokān āpnoti sarvāṃś ca kāmān yas tam ātmānam anuvidya vijānāti
children.translated_text: One who finds and knows that <s>ātman</s> obtains all worlds and all desires.

children.text: iti ha prajāpatir uvāca prajāpatir uvāca ||
children.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Prajāpati</s>; <s>Prajāpati</s> spoke thus.
From the dark I take refuge in the variegated.
From the variegated I take refuge in the dark.

children.text: aśva iva romāṇi vidhūya pāpaṃ candra iva rāhor mukhāt pramucya dhūtvā śarīram akṛtaṃ kṛtātmā brahmalokam abhisaṃbhavāmīty abhisaṃbhavāmīti ||
children.translated_text: Shaking off evil as a horse shakes off its hairs, freeing myself as the moon from the mouth of <s>Rāhu</s>, having shaken off the body, made, with the self perfected, I attain <s>brahmaloka</s>; I attain it.
Space, indeed, is called the revealer of name and form.

children.text: te yadantarā tad brahma tad amṛtaṃ sa ātmā
children.translated_text: What is within them is <s>brahman</s>; that is the immortal; that is the <s>ātman</s>.

children.text: prajāpateḥ sabhāṃ veśma prapadye yaśo 'haṃ bhavāmi brāhmaṇānāṃ yaśo rājñām yaśo viśām
children.translated_text: I take refuge in the hall and dwelling of <s>Prajāpati</s>. May I become the fame of the brahmins, the fame of kings, and the fame of the people.
May I attain fame.
So I am the fame of fames.

children.text: śyetam adatkam adatkaṃ śyetaṃ lindu mābhigāṃ lindu mābhigām ||
children.translated_text: May I not go to the white toothless one, the toothless white one, the slimy one; may I not go to the slimy one.

children.text: taddhaitad brahmā prajāpataya uvāca prajāpatir manave manuḥ prajābhyaḥ
children.translated_text: This, then, <s>Brahmā</s> taught to the <s>Prajāpatis</s>; <s>Prajāpati</s> taught it to <s>Manu</s>, and <s>Manu</s> to his offspring.

children.text: ācāryakulād vedam adhītya yathāvidhānaṃ guroḥ karmātiśeṣeṇābhisamāvṛtya kuṭumbe śucau deśe svādhyāyam adhīyāno dhārmikān vidadhad ātmani sarvendriyāṇi saṃpratiṣṭhāpyāhiṃsan sarvabhūtāny anyatra tīrthebhyaḥ
children.translated_text: Having studied the Veda in the teacher's household, returned home according to rule after completing what remains of service to the teacher, studying recitation in one's family in a pure place, establishing righteous dependents, settling all the senses in the self, and harming no beings except at sacred places,

children.text: sa khalv evaṃ vartayan yāvad āyuṣaṃ brahmalokam abhisaṃpadyate
children.translated_text: one who lives in this way for the full length of life attains <s>brahmaloka</s>.

children.text: na ca punar āvartate na ca punar āvartate ||
children.translated_text: And he does not return again; he does not return again.
